properties.name: Desert Trails RV Park & Golf Course
properties.price: The official rate sheet has no tent line. Dry park is $25/night, water and electric (gives you an outlet) is $37, full hookup is $45–50. Rates cover 2 people, with 2.5% off for cash. Expect the dry-park rate for a tent.
properties.reservations: Call ahead. Office hours aren't published. After-hours number (emergencies only): 760-791-2902. There is a $180 cancellation fee on reservations. Open year-round, and November is the start of snowbird season.
properties.access: Paved city streets about 2 mi south of the line through El Centro (Imperial Ave or 4th St, crossing I-8). Flat.
properties.notes: Tents are not mentioned on the operator's site. AAA lists about 100 tent sites, Good Sam lists a dedicated tenting area, and The Dyrt lists tent sites, so call to confirm. Restrooms are in 5 buildings, 3 of them with showers. Also: laundry, heated pool and hot tub. Mostly a 55+ snowbird park. A Campendium review describes disrepair, urban noise and crime, and spotty wifi. App DB entries osm-way-44388939, camp-res-94 and camp-res-135 are all this one park.

properties.name: Country Life RV Park
properties.price: No tent rate. RV full hookup $50/day for 2 people, plus $1 per extra person.
properties.reservations: Call. The Hipcamp page is an inactive placeholder, so you can't book it there.
properties.access: About 1.5 mi on paved streets: E Ross Rd near Old Hwy 111, east El Centro.
properties.notes: Sources conflict on tents. OpenStreetMap tags it tents=no. AAA (seen only in a search summary) lists 6 tent sites out of 169. MHBO describes a manufactured-home community, so expect mostly long-term residents. Call before counting on it.

properties.name: Sunbeam Lake RV Resort
properties.price: $41/night for an RV (reported Nov 2023). No published tent rate.
properties.reservations: Reservations accepted. A September 2025 reviewer got a last-minute spot while an hour out. Call first.
properties.access: About 8 mi west of El Centro on paved roads (Evan Hewes Hwy / Drew Rd to Seeley). Flat.
properties.notes: Tents are unconfirmed. The Dyrt and RVezy list tent sites, Campendium lists none, and the operator's site blocked our request. It is 8 mi in the wrong direction from Brawley, so it's only worth it as an El Centro fallback.

properties.name: Palm Lane RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: Call. No online booking.
properties.access: On W Main St in downtown Brawley, right on the route.
properties.notes: The only RV park in Brawley. It has 27 sites, mostly for full-time residents, and one listing says short-term guests are welcome. The Dyrt tags tent sites but has no reviews. Worth one call if you need to stop in Brawley.

properties.name: Wiest Lake County Park
properties.price: No 2026 rate published. Reports: $30 for a hookup site (2018); dry sites around $10 (undated).
properties.reservations: Reserve through Imperial County Parks (countyparksandrecreation@co.imperial.ca.us). Reviewers say there are no check-in signs and the ranger is hard to find, so they took an empty site.
properties.access: About 3 mi east of CA 111 on paved county roads (Rutherford Rd / Dietrich Rd), roughly 4–5 mi north of Brawley. Flat.
properties.notes: The county's 2026 parks page lists RV (partial and dry) and tent camping. Reports on showers conflict: a December 2020 tent camper found clean bathrooms with showers, a 2022 review says there are none. There's a loud, smelly cattle feedlot next door, so bring earplugs. Shade trees, lakeside, about 27 sites. The best legal tent stop near Brawley.

properties.name: Finney Lake (Imperial Wildlife Area, Finney-Ramer Unit)
properties.price: Camping is free, but anyone 16+ without a California fishing or hunting license needs a CDFW Lands Pass: $5.97/day in 2026, bought online in advance (valid only for the date printed). You also need a free daily entry permit from the self-registration booth.
properties.reservations: No reservations. Self-register at the booth, first come first served.
properties.access: About 3 mi from CA 111 via Titsworth Rd, Smith Rd, then Williams Rd. The last stretch is dirt, and GPS often routes you to the wrong end of Williams Rd.
properties.notes: Legal under 14 CCR §551(m): camping allowed only in the designated area at Finney Lake. Ramer Lake next door is closed until further notice. A January 2022 reviewer said the pit toilet was gone. Flies and odor (March 2025 review). Waterfowl hunters are around in November, so expect gunfire at dawn. Parts of the wildlife area can close for winter flooding. Carry all water.

properties.name: Del Yermo RV Park
properties.price: $25/night for an RV (reported April 2023). No tent rate.
properties.reservations: Call. In 2023 the manager was reportedly on site only noon–5 PM, three days a week.
properties.access: In Calipatria, 3 blocks east on Alamo St from CA 111/115.
properties.notes: 45 full-hookup sites, mostly long-term residents. Only one shower and restroom per sex, with broken door locks (2023). A December 2024 reviewer reported a DEA raid, ongoing drug activity and threats with guns. Not recommended. Tents are unconfirmed (The Dyrt's tag is generic).

properties.name: Red Hill Marina County Park ("Red Hill Park")
properties.price: No published rate. Reports: $7 for a tent (2017), $12 (January 2018).
properties.reservations: Through County Parks. No office on site.
properties.access: From CA 111 at Sinclair Rd (about mile 275), roughly 5 mi west on paved Sinclair Rd past the wildlife refuge, then Garst Rd and Red Hill Rd. Reviewers describe rough backroads and dirt at the end.
properties.notes: The county's 2026 page lists tent camping and RV (partial/dry) camping with no dump station. It's on the shrunken Salton Sea shore beside Sonny Bono NWR, with good birding. Brutal mosquitoes at dusk. A 2022 visitor found it 'super sketchy' with long-term residents and no staff. Phone-signal data was logged there on 10/30/26.

properties.name: Slab City (open camping on state land)
properties.price: Free
properties.reservations: None. Pitch anywhere unoccupied.
properties.access: From Niland, about 3.5 mi east on Main St and Beal Rd, paved to Salvation Mountain (Niland's Main St was being rebuilt in spring 2026). After that, sandy or dirt lanes. Gentle climb.
properties.notes: Legally grey. It is an unregulated settlement on state-owned land where camping has been tolerated for decades, not a designated campground. No restrooms (September 2026 guide). A tank at the community church dispenses water. A shooting in 2024; reviewers through 2026 describe trash and decline but food vendors and an open mic. Don't wander east: the Chocolate Mountain Aerial Gunnery Range is a live-fire area. Mojo's Slab Camp (next entry) is the softer landing.

properties.name: Mojo's Slab Camp
properties.price: Free to $25/night (The Dyrt).
properties.reservations: Reservations possible. A January 2024 reviewer pulled in after dark with no booking and was welcomed.
properties.access: Through Slab City to Coachella Canal Rd, about 4.5 mi from Niland. Paved most of the way, last bit dirt.
properties.notes: An established host camp inside Slab City with restrooms, showers, a communal kitchen and a campfire scene. Reviewed January 2024 and July 2026. Several local dogs roam loose. Its legal standing is the same grey area as the rest of Slab City.

properties.name: Bee Land! True Off-Grid Camping (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $36/night plus Hipcamp fees. Hipcamp lists the site as 'vehicles' only.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request to book, not instant. Active and bookable, 12 bookings, 4 of 4 recommend.
properties.access: A cleared dirt track off CA 111 between Niland and Bombay Beach. The host sends directions on arrival day.
properties.notes: 5 bare acres, no facilities, for self-contained campers. Tents aren't a listed site type, so message the host first. Only useful if you're stuck between Niland and Bombay Beach.

properties.name: Bashford's Hot Mineral Spa
properties.price: Operator's site (2014 footer, may be dated): $42/night without hookups, $50 with full hookups, for 2 people including the mineral baths. Extra person $10.
properties.reservations: Call. Facilities are for registered guests only. Check-out at noon. Season Oct 15–May 15.
properties.access: About 3.5 mi NE of CA 111 on paved Hot Mineral Spa Rd (the turn is about 4 mi SE of Bombay Beach). Gradual uphill.
properties.notes: The operator's site lists 'Tent sites' and AAA lists tents. Some directories call it an adult or 55+ park, so mention that when you call. Six mineral baths, pool, laundry. A reviewer has wintered there every year since 2023 (September 2026 review).

properties.name: Palm Springs RV Park & Glamis North Hot Springs
properties.price: Not published: the rate shows in the reservation system once you pick dates. RV sites were $50 in 2024. 25% off Sunday–Wednesday nights. Price covers hot springs, pools and saunas.
properties.reservations: Reserve online (CampLife) or by phone. Only 2 tent sites, so book ahead. Minimum stay on weekends and holidays. Check-in from 2 PM. Self check-in by a link in the confirmation email.
properties.access: About 3.75 mi NE of CA 111 on paved Hot Mineral Spa Rd. Gradual uphill toward the Chocolate Mountains.
properties.notes: Best tent stop between Niland and the Salton Sea State Recreation Area (SRA). Two tent sites near the pool complex, each with a PRIVATE BATHROOM AND ELECTRICITY (up to 5 tents per site). Season is Oct 23, 2026 to Apr 11, 2027. Store and cafe on site. The Chocolate Mountains block the westerly wind.

properties.name: Private Hot Springs & Organic Farm (Hipcamp, host Gordon)
properties.price: $72/night plus Hipcamp fees. One group (up to 5) at a time, so the whole site is yours.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book. Check-in 4–9 PM, meeting the host. Check-out 10 AM.
properties.access: Hot Mineral Spa Rd (paved, about 3.75 mi), then the host's private driveway into a fenced date farm.
properties.notes: Private natural hot-spring tubs, a flush toilet in a private bathroom, and reverse-osmosis drinking water. 302 bookings, 99% recommend, reviewers praise the host. Arrive by 9 PM.

properties.name: Salton Sea Seclusion (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $25/night plus Hipcamp fees.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK (0 hours' notice).
properties.access: About 2 mi inland (NE) from CA 111 north of Bombay Beach. Access details come after booking; expect dirt.
properties.notes: 30 undeveloped acres, 8 tent/RV spots, no facilities. Fill water in Bombay Beach. The host's dogs roam. Only 8 bookings, 88% recommend.

properties.name: Salt Creek Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA, primitive)
properties.price: Primitive: $10/night (seniors 62+ $8).
properties.reservations: No reservations, first come first served. Park open 24 hours.
properties.access: Directly off CA 111.
properties.notes: Open beach camping with picnic tables, fire pits and portable toilets. Not on the official closure list (only Mecca Beach and Bombay Beach are). Trains and the highway are close. The SR 111 washout with one-way traffic control is in this stretch of the park.

properties.name: Corvina Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA, primitive)
properties.price: Primitive: $10/night (seniors 62+ $8).
properties.reservations: First come first served. Pick any open spot.
properties.access: Directly off CA 111.
properties.notes: Water spigots plus free COLD showers (reviews January 2025 and earlier). Pit toilets, tables, fire rings, no shade. Trains pass close by. 2.5 mi short of the full-service HQ/New Camp.

properties.name: Salton Sea SRA – Headquarters & New Camp campgrounds (hike-and-bike sites)
properties.price: Developed tent site $20/night, primitive $10, hookup $30 (gives you an outlet). Seniors 62+ get $2 off. The park lists hike-and-bike sites but doesn't publish their fee.
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia (park 704), October–May. On Nov 2 the availability calendar showed open sites through Nov 17. Walk-ups get a site if one is free. Campground open 24 hours. Visitor center 9 AM–4 PM daily.
properties.access: Turn off CA 111 at the park entrance, then a short paved road (State Park Rd).
properties.notes: The park's 'main campground remains open' (checked Nov 2, 2026). Flush toilets and showers; reviewers in 2024 said the showers take tokens, so get them during visitor-center hours. OpenStreetMap marks hike-and-bike tent sites beside New Camp. Shade ramadas. Freight trains are loud, so bring earplugs. This is the last sure tent stop before Indio (about 30 mi).

properties.name: BLM Mecca Hills – Painted Canyon Rd dispersed camping
properties.price: Free (BLM limit: 14 days in any 28)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: From Mecca, about 4.5 mi NE on paved Box Canyon Rd (gradual climb), then Painted Canyon Rd: 1–4.5 mi of soft, deep sand wash where cars need 4WD. On a loaded bike that is mostly pushing. BLM: Box Canyon Rd has been CLOSED from Pinto Rd to Painted Canyon Rd since Oct 21, 2026 (flood damage from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel), so the pull-offs east of the Painted Canyon Rd junction are cut off.
properties.notes: Camp only along the non-wilderness road corridor: bicycles are banned inside the wilderness. Pit toilets halfway up Painted Canyon Rd (2025). Recreational shooting nearby. The sand wash was probably damaged by the storm. Last resort only.

properties.name: Forsythe Equestrian Club (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $75/night plus Hipcamp fees (combined tent/RV site).
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK. Check in on arrival.
properties.access: About 5 mi west of CV Link on Ave 54 (paved, flat). Exact address after booking.
properties.notes: A working horse farm with flush toilets, showers, kitchen, wifi and electric hookups. 39 bookings, 93% recommend. Pricey, but closer than Lake Cahuilla.

properties.name: Shadow Hills RV Resort
properties.price: Hipcamp from $39/night plus fees; the lowest rate, probably the tent site. 21 grass tent sites, 10 × 20 ft, no tent supplied.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK (0 hours' notice), or call. Check in on arrival.
properties.access: Half a mile off the line in north Indio: Jefferson St at Varner Rd, near I-10.
properties.notes: The operator advertises tent sites. Restrooms are a short walk, showers free (2021 review). Pool and spa, laundry, wifi, gated. Can be very windy. Sites by Jefferson St get road noise. Best confirmed tent spot in Indio, at the end of this segment.

properties.name: Wild West RV Ranch (primitive tent site)
properties.price: Primitive tent site booked via Hipcamp. The listing shows 'from $25/night'; one directory quoted the tent site at $40. Includes restrooms, hot showers, a water spigot, Wi-Fi, a picnic table and a fire pit. The tent site has no electric; RV sites have 30/50A pedestals (RV from about $50, Good Sam).
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp; same-day bookings accepted. Check-in from 2 pm with a host meet-and-greet; call for a late arrival. Open all year, all ages.
properties.access: Paved state highways, flat. From Maricopa (mile 21.7) ride about 12.5 mi south on AZ 347 / John Wayne Pkwy to AZ 84 ('Peters Corner'). Alternative: from Casa Grande ride about 18 mi west on AZ 84 through Stanfield to the ranch, then about 12.5 mi north on AZ 347 to Maricopa next morning. That adds about 9 mi to the planned line.
properties.notes: The best real tent campground between Casa Grande and Buckeye: a dedicated primitive tent site near restrooms and hot showers. Tent campers reviewed it in Aug and Oct 2026 (clean bathroom, easy check-in, some shade). Its own websites are dead (wildwestrvranch.com is an unconnected Wix domain; the old wildwestrvresort.com is now spam), so use Hipcamp or the phone. Main drawback: 12.5 mi off the line each way.

properties.name: BLM dispersed: W Ray Rd west of S Tuthill Rd (Buckeye Hills east)
properties.price: Free; 14 days in any 28.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Where the line turns from W Ray Rd north onto S Tuthill Rd (about mile 61), continue about 0.9-1.3 mi west on W Ray Rd (asphalt per OSM) to BLM land.
properties.notes: Land status comes only from BLM GIS; no camper reports found. The point is not inside the Lower Gila Terraces ACEC (checked against BLM's ACEC layer). Equestrian and other private parcels are nearby, so obey any 'no trespassing' signs. Fire Station 326 is right on the line at mile 61.2 for water.

properties.name: Vescent RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved, about 1 mi north of the line on Buckeye's east side, on MC 85 next to Vescent Church.
properties.notes: Appears only in OpenStreetMap; no website, phone or reviews found. It shares its location with Vescent Church. Worth asking in person while passing through Buckeye, but treat it as unverified.

properties.name: The Sunset Nooks (Hipcamp tent site)
properties.price: $55/night for the single tent site (about $64.53 all-in with the Hipcamp fee), up to 8 people. Host supplies a pop-up tent, table, chairs, BBQ and charcoal.
properties.phone: unknown (contact host Cory W. through the Hipcamp app)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice needed. Message the host with your ETA. Music down at 8pm, off at 10pm.
properties.access: Small private lot in south Buckeye by the Gila River, about 1 mile off the line at the Buckeye end (street address shown after booking). Paved streets, walk-in tent pad.
properties.notes: This is the only bookable tent pitch with a shower and toilet at the Buckeye end: 44 bookings, 96% recommend. It sits at corridor mile ~70, the start of this segment, so it works as a Buckeye night, not a mid-segment stop. A toilet is listed but its type isn't stated.

properties.name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
properties.price: $20/night per site (last reported Dec 2025). Restrooms with sinks and toilets; no water, showers or hookups.
properties.reservations: 7 primitive sites (A-G). Reserve online through the City of Buckeye at least 3 days ahead; unreserved walk-up stays are limited to one night (Dec 2025 review). Max 7 nights. The gate reportedly locks around 10 pm (one report says 9:30 pm), so arrive early.
properties.access: Paved: from Beloat Rd ride about 8 mi straight north on Watson Rd (crossing I-10 at exit 117) to 2600 N Watson Rd. The last 2 mi climb about 500-600 ft into the White Tank foothills (camp elevation 1,476 ft).
properties.notes: Legal, cheap, quiet and dark, but completely dry: the city says there is no drinking water in the park. Fill up in Buckeye (Circle K on Monroe Ave) before the climb. Sites C-E are farther from the busy trailhead. It is a 17-mi round-trip detour north, not on the way west.

properties.name: BLM dispersed off W Robbins Butte Game Rd (south of Buckeye; 'Buckeye Hills BLM')
properties.price: Free
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: From the line at Buckeye, take AZ 85 south across the Gila River (about 4-5 mi on the highway shoulder) to W Robbins Butte Game Rd, then 1-2 mi west on dirt with soft gravel and sand spots. Campers use a strip of about 1 mi on the SOUTH side of the road.
properties.notes: Last resort only. Legality is muddled: 'no overnight camping / no shooting' signs were seen in Apr 2025, rangers told campers 'no camping' in 2021, the adjoining Robbins Butte Wildlife Area (AZ Game & Fish) bans camping, and The Dyrt lists the nearby 'Buckeye Hills BLM' spot as CLOSED. People were still camping there in Jan-Feb 2026, and a sheriff patrols mornings. Reviews from 2021-2026 report heavy shooting (ricochets near a trailer in Aug 2024), theft, dumping and crowding. Not a good place for a solo tent.

properties.name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
properties.price: $20/night per campsite (7 sites, A to G). Each site has two 12x12 ft tent pads, a picnic table, a grill and a fire ring.
properties.reservations: Reservation required: request online or call Mon-Fri 9am-7pm. The city calls back within 72 hours to confirm and take payment, so same-day booking isn't realistic. Park hours are 5am-10pm.
properties.access: 2600 N Watson Rd, Buckeye. About 9 miles north of the line on paved Watson Rd (crosses I-10), climbing gently into the White Tank foothills. Coordinate is the OSM park centroid. The campsites are near the park entrance.
properties.notes: There's no drinking water anywhere in the park (the city says so explicitly), so carry it all in. Restrooms have sinks and toilets but no showers. It's only worth the 9-mile detour if you booked it a few days ahead.

properties.name: 3Acre Desert RV Camp (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $25/night for an RV site (about $29.58 with Hipcamp fees). Tent use isn't listed, so ask the host.
properties.reservations: Request-to-book, not instant. Message the host the day before. 1 booking so far, 100% recommend.
properties.access: Private fenced 3-acre lot about 1 mile off the line, between Arlington and Wintersburg (address after booking). It borders a wash and State Trust land. Drive-in, 2WD access.
properties.notes: Apart from Stage Stop, this is the only private option between Buckeye and Tonopah. The listing is RV-only, so get the host's OK to pitch a tent before counting on it. Potable water, fire pit and trash are listed.

properties.name: Stage Stop RV Park / Wintersburg General Store
properties.price: No tent rate. RV daily is $60 with utilities, plus a $300 refundable deposit on all lodging.
properties.reservations: Register at the Wintersburg General Store (open daily 5am-9pm; office Mon-Fri 6am-8pm, Sat-Sun 12-8pm). Rentals require a deposit and 2 IDs.
properties.access: 2614 S Wintersburg Rd, right at the line on Salome Hwy. The store is at the park entrance.
properties.notes: Worker park for Palo Verde nuclear plant staff. Showers are for tenants. Tent policy is unknown, so ask at the store. The store itself is the key resupply on this stretch: groceries, fresh produce, fuel and an ATM, with Tin Top Bar & Grill on site.

properties.name: Saddle Mountain RV Park
properties.price: Full-hookup sites are $50/night plus tax for 2 people. A Nov 2024 RoverPass listing showed tents at $30 (or $35 with power), but the 2026 operator site lists RV sites only.
properties.reservations: Call or email; $200 refundable deposit. Office is open Mon-Fri 9am-3pm (Sep-Apr). After hours, self check-in at the desk by the office door: pick a site from the board and pay by envelope.
properties.access: 40902 W Osborn Rd, half a mile south of I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave), on pavement.
properties.notes: Reopened under new management after showing 'permanently closed' in 2023. Ask whether they'll put a tent on an RV site. Self check-in makes late arrival easy. Flies from nearby egg and chicken farms have been reported in the area.

properties.name: El Dorado Hot Spring
properties.price: About $50/night (Feb 2026 review; The Dyrt lists 'from $40'). Has primitive tent sites plus 30A electric sites.
properties.website: unknown (old eldoradohotspring.com no longer resolves; listings link to a Facebook page)
properties.reservations: Call ahead. A March 2026 guest reported no check-in instructions and a double booking, so confirm by phone the same day.
properties.access: 41225 W Indian School Rd, Tonopah, 0.3 mile on pavement from I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave).
properties.notes: The one confirmed tent camp with showers at Tonopah. Outdoor showers and new restrooms were built in 2024. It's a clothing-optional hot spring with one 24/7 nude-only pool, and you can hear the interstate. Pilot, Chevron and Exxon are across exit 94.

properties.name: BLM land along Hovatter Rd (I-10 exit 53) - unverified fallback
properties.price: Free under the standard BLM rule (14 days in any 28) if the parcel is BLM.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: Take I-10 exit 53, then go south on Hovatter Rd. It's dirt and 'smooth but very sandy' at the start, so expect to push a loaded bike. The land is BLM Yuma Field Office until the Kofa NWR boundary about 20+ miles south. The coordinate is the road near the interchange, not a known campsite.
properties.notes: This is the only spot right on the interstate between Tonopah and Quartzsite, about 41 miles from Tonopah. I found no camper reports. Check a land-status map (BLM vs State Trust) before pitching and stay well away from the freeway. Bouse Wash rest area (restrooms, water unreliable) is 1 mile west; the Pilot at exit 45 is 8 miles west.

properties.name: Gold Nugget Rd BLM dispersed (I-10 exit 26)
properties.price: Free, 14-day maximum.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: I-10 exit 26 (Gold Nugget Rd), then south 1/4 mile. Loose small gravel and firm sand.
properties.notes: The first free pitch right on the interstate after Tonopah, 7-8 miles before Quartzsite. Cactus debris means puncture risk (reviewers say it isn't dog-friendly), plus freeway hum and ATVs. BLM says short-term camping around Quartzsite is limited to five designated areas and this isn't one of them, so obey any 'no camping' signs (Scaddan Wash is 6 miles on). The newest review is Feb 2024.

properties.name: Scaddan Wash BLM 14-day camping area
properties.price: Free, 14-day limit. A seasonal camp host registers campers.
properties.reservations: First-come; register with the host if present.
properties.access: Leave I-10 at exit 19 (Riggles Ave) and ride about 1.5-2 miles east on Dome Rock Rd E (the south frontage road; rough, so reviewers use the shoulder) to the area. Inside it's dirt and sand with washes.
properties.notes: The designated free area closest to town, within bike range of all Quartzsite services. Very loud near the freeway, so go well south. A Dec 2025 review reports dumped tires and a microwave.

properties.name: Plomosa Road BLM 14-Day Camping Area
properties.price: Free, 14 days in 28. One Campendium user entered '$44' in Feb 2026; every other report says free.
properties.reservations: First come. A seasonal host is sometimes present.
properties.access: Paved US 95 north about 5.5 mi, then east on asphalt Plomosa Rd. Camp on the gravel flats on either side and respect the marked day-use boundaries.
properties.notes: Less dusty and roomier than the areas near town (Feb 2026 review). It is 13 mi round trip in the wrong direction, so it's only a fallback.

properties.name: Hi Jolly BLM 14-day camping area
properties.price: Free, 14-day limit. Register with the camp host for a free 14-day pass when one is on duty.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: 3 miles north of Quartzsite on US 95 at milepost 112 (paved highway), gravel inside.
properties.notes: Crowded with RVs in season, though clean. Camp toward the east side, away from US 95 noise. Water, dump and propane are in town, 3 miles away.

properties.name: Tumbleweed RV Park (Rose's RV Park)
properties.price: $8-40/night per The Dyrt, which lists 'Standard (tent/RV)' sites. Showers were coin-op ($5 in 2019) and free in 2023.
properties.reservations: Call; no online booking.
properties.access: 600 Kuehn St, Quartzsite, next to I-10. City streets.
properties.notes: The cheap end of its range may be a tent or dry spot. Constant I-10 noise. A 2019 reviewer rode a bike to town and the RV show from here.

properties.name: Q View RV Park (formerly B-10 Campground)
properties.price: $25/night 'Dry Camping', plus a $2.50 booking fee, a 3% card fee and tax ($125/week). Hookup sites are $35-50.
properties.phone: (928) 927-4393 (site says this line is temporarily down; temporary number 501-691-5757)
properties.reservations: Book online or call. Open 365 days.
properties.access: 615 W Main St in central Quartzsite, near I-10 exit 17/19. City streets.
properties.notes: This is the baseline 'B-10 Campground' under its new name. It offers dry camping 'for non-RV folks' (a guest review quoted on its site), private hot showers that aren't coin-op, Starlink Wi-Fi, laundry and fire pits. The old B-10 had numerous tent sites. Confirm the dry site takes a tent when you book. Walking distance to everything in town.

properties.name: La Posa LTVA (North/South/West/Tyson Wash)
properties.price: In season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days; there's no one-night rate. The long-term permit is $180. A 2024 BLM plan proposed $200/$600, but I found no sign it was adopted.
properties.reservations: First-come; buy the permit on site or at the Yuma Field Office.
properties.access: About 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US 95 (from I-10 exit 17), with four sub-areas. Permits are sold at the entrance host station. Dirt roads inside, reported rough after the 2026 flooding.
properties.notes: The only Quartzsite camp with public water taps (8, though a reviewer calls the water salty, so carry drinking water), 10 vault toilets, dump and trash. Poor value for one night next to the free 14-day areas.

properties.name: Desert Gardens RV Park (Sky Resorts)
properties.price: Tent rate not published. RV sites start at $36/night (Good Sam).
properties.reservations: Book online or call. Open year-round.
properties.access: 1240 Acacia Rd, south-west Quartzsite. City streets.
properties.notes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator site advertises full-hookup RV sites only and AllStays calls it 55+. Call first.

properties.name: Road Runner BLM 14-day camping area
properties.price: Free, 14-day limit. A host issues free permits in season.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: About 6 miles south of I-10 on US 95 to milepost 99, then just west via N 53rd St / La Paz Valley Rd. Hard-packed gravel, with a steep drop-off at the road edge.
properties.notes: Huge and nearly empty in late Oct 2025. Go west, away from US 95 traffic. Note it's a 12-mile round trip off the westbound route.

properties.name: Dome Rock Mountain BLM 14-day camping area
properties.price: Free. Get the free 14-day permit from the seasonal camp host.
properties.reservations: First-come; register with the host.
properties.access: On the westbound route: Dome Rock Rd W (south frontage road), 3-5 miles west of town. Rocky but passable dirt. The camp host is near the entrance. Coordinates vary by source (Campendium 33.6494,-114.2715; The Dyrt 33.6409,-114.3151); the area is large.
properties.notes: Up to about 400 sites on hard, flat desert. Load all water in Quartzsite. Stay out of the marked gas-pipeline corridor. It's just past the segment end (mile ~176-178) and already on the road to Blythe, so it's the natural first night west of town.

properties.name: Saddle Mountain BLM dispersed camping
properties.price: Free, 14 days in any 28.
properties.reservations: First-come, no permit or host.
properties.access: The Salome variant runs right past it on W Courthouse Rd, paved from the east. Many entrances; a popular one is near Courthouse Rd mile marker 13. Sites sit on rocky, rutted dirt spurs (coordinate is approximate). From the main I-10 line it's about 8-10 riding miles SW of exit 94 via Indian School Rd, Saddle Vista Rd, Salome Hwy and Courthouse Rd. Don't follow GPS onto Salome Hwy from I-10 exit 81: it's dirt until Courthouse Rd.
properties.notes: Fill water at Tonopah (exit 94) or the Saddle Vista Ranch RV fill (about 10c/gal per a 2024 review). Reviews from Oct 26-27, 2026 call the fly swarms 'unbearable' (nearby egg/chicken farms), so expect them in early November. Also: weekend target shooting, rocky ground (bring stakes that hold in gravel), and a power-plant smell on some winds.

properties.name: Indian Hills RV Resort
properties.price: $39.20/night on Hipcamp for a 50x55 ft back-in 'RV/tent' site with full hookups and 30/50A (about $48.78 with fees). A furnished teepee is $85, casitas $125+.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book (same-day OK, 1-night minimum) or call. Office hours aren't published.
properties.access: 67668 Salome Rd, on paved Salome Rd at the SE edge of Salome. The variant passes the gate.
properties.notes: The best-equipped tent stop on the variant: hot showers, laundry, free Wi-Fi, a store and fitness room, all ages. It's the first camp after the 41-mile empty Harquahala Valley stretch. 13 Hipcamp bookings, 100% recommend.

properties.name: Centennial Park (La Paz County)
properties.price: $10/night dry camping, or $20 with water and electric (May 2025 review). Dump is $10.
properties.reservations: First-come with an on-site host (2022). Late-arrival rules unknown.
properties.access: 69725 Centennial Park Rd, about 3 miles east of Salome off US 60 (toward Wenden). Gravel park roads.
properties.notes: The cheapest legal pitch around Salome, plus a desert golf course. Facilities have been unreliable: 2018 and 2021 reviews mention showers, but in 2022 the restrooms were locked (porta-potties) and the well water was not drinkable. Call before relying on its water or showers.

properties.name: Salome KOA Journey
properties.price: Tent rate not published. KOA lists Deluxe and Premium tent sites; Good Sam mentions a gravel overflow tent area. RV sites start around $51/night (Good Sam).
properties.reservations: Online, KOA app or phone. Office is roughly 8am-4pm daily, with lit after-hours check-in. Open all year.
properties.access: 64812 Harcuvar Dr, just off US 60 about 2.5 miles west of Salome (near milepost 54). The variant line passes the entrance. KOA's own directions say 'US 60 to MP 54, then 2 mi S on Harcuvar Dr', but mapped coordinates put the park about 0.2 mile from US 60.
properties.notes: Pool, hot tub, laundry and a camp store. Salome Restaurant is about 0.2 mile away on US 60. New owners (the Johnston family, Dec 2025) are restoring a breakfast kitchen.

properties.name: Ramblin' Roads RV Resort (Hope)
properties.price: Tent rate not published. The Dyrt lists sites 'from free to $35/night'.
properties.reservations: Call or email. Arriving late: fill out an envelope at the after-hours registration on the front of the building (lobby open until 9pm). After 9pm, take any open site and pay when the lobby opens at 9am. Office Mon-Sat 9am-2pm, Oct 1 to Apr 1.
properties.access: 60655 US 60 at Hope. The variant goes by the door.
properties.notes: The operator's amenity list explicitly includes TENT CAMPING (plus good well water and free Wi-Fi), but it's a 55+ park. Confirm they'll take your party before relying on it.

properties.name: Vicksburg Pit Rd BLM dispersed
properties.price: Free, 14-day maximum.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: From Vicksburg Junction (US 60, variant mile about 66.5), about 2-3 miles north toward SR 72 and Vicksburg to Vicksburg Pit Rd. The access is wide, well-graded gravel; cross the railroad tracks slowly. From the main I-10 line: exit 45 (mile about 145), then about 8 miles north on Vicksburg Rd.
properties.notes: Quiet, few campers and dark skies (Feb 2026 reviews). Flies even in December. The BLM land borders private parcels, so stay on BLM. No services: get water at the Pilot at I-10 exit 45 or in Salome.

properties.name: Steve and Dawn Desert Getaway
properties.price: $15-30/night. There are 3 dry sites for tent or RV (no water or power at the site) and 2 full-hookup RV sites.
properties.reservations: Request to Book through The Dyrt.
properties.access: 10 fenced acres north of US 60 near Vicksburg; GPS may show Salome. About 5.6 miles in a straight line north of the variant, probably on dirt roads. Address comes with the booking.
properties.notes: The listing says there is 'as yet no bathroom on-site'. It's far off the line, so only worth it if everything closer is full.

properties.name: 3 Dreamers RV Park
properties.price: $32/night per The Dyrt (probably the RV rate). No tent rate on the operator site.
properties.reservations: Call. Office and campstore are open Mon-Sat 11am-5pm (Oct-Mar), closed Sunday. A Dec 2025 review says the owners helped with a late-night arrival.
properties.access: 54000 US 60, about 3 miles west of Vicksburg Junction, right on the variant.
properties.notes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator's site mentions only full-hookup RV sites. Call first. New owners in 2025; clean hot showers, laundry, campstore and propane.

properties.name: The Collier 15 (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $22.75/night (about $26.79 with Hipcamp fees) for an RV/tent site with full hookups and a 30A outlet. Two sites: 'The 2 mesquites' (concrete pad, fire pit) and 'The Willow'.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice. 17 bookings, 86% recommend.
properties.access: Fenced 55-acre property just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda (address after booking). Short dirt driveway.
properties.notes: The host calls it 'perfect for tent camping', and you get an outlet to charge. A toilet is listed but no shower. Buckaroos store in Brenda is about 5 miles west. Same host as The Dusty 40 next door.

properties.name: The Dusty 40 (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $8/night (about $11 with fees). Pitch anywhere on the property.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum. 5 bookings, 100% recommend.
properties.access: 40-acre desert parcel next to The Collier 15, just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda. Dirt access.
properties.notes: Bare land the host is still cleaning up, with broken glass in spots, so watch your tires and tent floor. Bring all water.

properties.name: Black Rock RV Village (Brenda)
properties.price: No tent rate. RV sites are $40-45/night.
properties.reservations: Office closes at 3pm and is closed Sundays.
properties.access: 46751 E US 60 in Brenda, on the variant, 3.7 miles before it rejoins I-10 at exit 31.
properties.notes: Lists RV sites only, so ask about a tent before counting on it. Black Rock Cafe on site (limited hours) and Buckaroos Country Store nearby make Brenda a food stop either way. Wi-Fi only works at the diner and pavilion.

properties.name: Ramsey Mine Rd BLM dispersed
properties.price: Free, 14-day maximum.
properties.reservations: First-come.
properties.access: Ramsey Mine Rd runs south from US 60 about 1 mile west of Brenda and crosses over I-10 on a bridge (no interchange). Camp along the smaller parallel gravel road on flat, hard ground. From the main I-10 line: exit 31 (mile about 159.5), then about 3.5 miles east on US 60 and south.
properties.notes: Room for 40-50 rigs, rarely more than 15 (Jan 2026). About 1 mile from Buckaroos Country Store (groceries, sandwiches) and Black Rock Cafe in Brenda. OHVs raise dust on Ramsey Mine Rd itself, and I-10 hum starts around 6am. Fires only Oct-Mar; no wood gathering.

properties.name: Quartzsite RV Resort
properties.price: Tent rate not published. A full-hookup RV night is $55 in November 2026.
properties.reservations: OSM gives reception hours of 8am to 7pm. Call ahead.
properties.access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then north on Riggles Ave.
properties.notes: A small park with 27 full-hookup RV sites. The website mentions only RV sites, so ask before counting on a tent.

properties.name: Arizona Sun RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. A daily RV site is $47 + $6.20 tax.
properties.reservations: Call for reservations. Check-in is at 1 PM.
properties.access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then 1/2 mi north on Plymouth Ave and 1/4 mi on Quail Trail.
properties.notes: 126 full-hookup sites with shower houses and laundry. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but the operator only lists RV rates, so call. The park is across the street from BLM desert.

properties.name: Desert Edge RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: OSM says reservations are recommended. Call.
properties.access: Paved, near I-10 exit 19.
properties.notes: The park's domain (desertedgervpark.com) now redirects to a parking page, so it may have changed hands. Its status is unverified.

properties.name: Pattie's RV Park & Propane
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: Small park, call ahead.
properties.access: On paved E Main St (Business 10), between exits 19 and 17.
properties.notes: A small park with back-in full-hookup sites, a smoothie and coffee bar, and laundry (2021 review). It also rents trailers. No tent information.

properties.name: Crawford's RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Off-season daily RV site is $45 + tax (2026–27 rates).
properties.reservations: Reservations by phone. The park says overnighters are welcome.
properties.access: On paved E Main St (Business 10).
properties.notes: 67 full-hookup sites, laundry and a rental cabin. The site never mentions tents, so call.

properties.name: Texas BBQ RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved, in town.
properties.notes: A cheap, basic lot with a bathroom, trash and a dump station, right beside I-10 (2022 reviews). No phone or tent policy found.

properties.name: Split Rail RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Nightly site is $50.
properties.reservations: Book online or call.
properties.access: Paved. About 1.25 mi north of Main St on US 95 (Central Blvd).
properties.notes: New management, with ATV rentals on site. The Dyrt also lists this address as 'Pyramid Lane RV Park' and 'Safari RV Park', which look like old names. No tent policy published.

properties.name: Shady Lane RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. RV was $35 in 2024.
properties.reservations: Reservations by phone. Open Sept 15 to Apr 15.
properties.access: Paved, two blocks north of Main St on Central Blvd.
properties.notes: Showers are coin-operated, 50 cents per 5 minutes. Mostly full-time workers live here (Oct 2025 review). One 2023 reviewer arrived late and staff came out to help. The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is unverified.

properties.name: Kofa Mountain 55+ RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. RV was $35 (Mar 2026).
properties.reservations: Call. Cash or check only.
properties.access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
properties.notes: An age-55-plus RV park. It has community showers but no published tent option, so it is unlikely to take a passing tent.

properties.name: American Trails RV Park & Tiny Cabins
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Daily RV is $45 (30 A) or $50 (50 A), March to November.
properties.reservations: Online through Newbook, or call.
properties.access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
properties.notes: About 90 RV sites plus tiny-home rentals, a pool and laundry. A reviewer called it a senior community. Tents aren't mentioned.

properties.name: La Mirage RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved, in town.
properties.notes: An April 2024 reviewer found no bathrooms or showers, only a laundromat, and called the price outrageous. Skip it.

properties.name: Tyson Wells RV Park (Tyson Wells Market Center)
properties.price: $25 per overnight, $125 per week, $225 per month plus electricity (operator's 2026 page)
properties.reservations: Call. RV parking season is Oct 1 to Mar 31.
properties.access: Paved streets in town, just south of Main St and Central Blvd.
properties.notes: The cheapest paid lot in town. It is the swap-meet grounds, and the January shows don't start until Jan 1. A Dec 2021 reviewer was living there in a tent, so tents have been accepted, but the operator doesn't say so: call first. It has toilets and hookups. Showers are unconfirmed.

properties.name: Holiday Palms RV Resort
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Peak-season (Nov 1 to Apr 30) RV sites start at $65/night plus tax and electric.
properties.reservations: Book online or call. There is an after-hours check-in box at the office door.
properties.access: Paved, on W Main St. The streets inside are paved.
properties.notes: Has a heated pool, hot tub and clean bathhouses, and is open all year. Its rules and FAQ never mention tents. Pricey for one night.

properties.name: Hassler's RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: Call. A registration form is on the website.
properties.access: Paved, on W Main St.
properties.notes: An adult-oriented park under new owners, with the welded 'Mechanical Zoo' sculptures. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but that is unverified.

properties.name: Gunny's RV Park & Military Museum
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved, in town.
properties.notes: A small RV park run by a retired Marine, with a military museum (2023 review). The Dyrt flags it as no tents. Low value for a cyclist.

properties.name: La Paz RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved US 95 south about 5 mi.
properties.notes: Only OSM data exists for this park. It is far off the line and not worth the detour.

properties.name: Villa Verde RV & Mobile Park
properties.price: Unknown. $21 was reported earlier and $40 cash in 2022.
properties.reservations: Pay cash at the office. A 2022 camper said the office staff disappeared.
properties.access: Paved. I-10 exit 1, then 1/4 mi north on Poston Rd and 1/8 mi west.
properties.notes: A run-down mobile-home park with some RV sites. A 2021 review says there are no showers and no bathrooms. Use it only as a last resort.

properties.name: Arizona Oasis RV Resort
properties.price: No tent rate published. RV sites run $63–115.
properties.reservations: Book online (RMS) or call. Check-in 12 PM, check-out 11 AM. The park is gated.
properties.access: Paved, at I-10 exit 1 on the Arizona riverbank.
properties.notes: An older listing description mentioned 'tent camping', but the 2026 website lists only RV sites, cabins and rentals. Call before counting on it. It has a pool, spa and river beach. The Flying J is next door.

properties.name: Ehrenberg–Cibola Road BLM Dispersed Camping
properties.price: Free. Rangers enforce the 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: First come, any hour
properties.access: From the Flying J at I-10 exit 1, take the south frontage road to Cibola Rd, which becomes Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd heading southeast. It is compacted gravel, washboarded for about 2 mi. Pull off onto open BLM desert about 3–3.5 mi from the exit.
properties.notes: The free fallback on the Arizona bank if the river parks are full or you arrive after the offices close. A Nov 2024 camper said you can barely hear I-10 from here. OHVs can raise dust at times. Fill water at the Flying J or Chevron at exit 1. BLM's Sandbowl page confirms dispersed camping is available in this area.

properties.name: Ehrenberg Sandbowl (BLM OHV area)
properties.price: Free
properties.reservations: None
properties.access: BLM directions: from the Ehrenberg exit take the south frontage road about 1 mi west, then turn left onto gravel Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd. The bowl itself is very soft sand, and a 2021 visitor's vehicle got stuck. Expect to push the bike.
properties.notes: Camping here is legal, but it's an OHV playground with dust and engine noise. Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, 3.5 mi out, is the better free choice.

properties.name: Levee Road BLM Dispersed Camping (Colorado River, AZ side)
properties.price: Free, 14 days
properties.reservations: None
properties.access: 8–9 mi south of Ehrenberg on a washboard dirt levee road. One 2018 driver took 1.5 hours to cover 11 mi in an RV. There are OHVs on weekends.
properties.notes: Riverfront spots, but rough, trashy in places and a long dirt slog with a loaded bike (Dec 2025 review). Only worth it if you want the river. McIntyre's paid tent sites are directly across the water.

properties.name: The Cove RV Resort (formerly Riviera RV Resort)
properties.price: Tent rate by phone. RV sites are $60/night plus Blythe's 10% lodging tax.
properties.reservations: Call; the office is open 8am to 5pm daily, California time. The store is open 8–5 Sunday to Thursday and 8–6 Friday and Saturday. A 2020 guest got a site at 9:30 pm, but call ahead for a late arrival.
properties.access: Paved. Just over the Colorado River on the California side, at Riviera Dr (I-10 exit 243). It is 0.1–0.5 mi from where the bike/foot bridge and I-10 land. One reviewer called the access road 'sketchy'.
properties.notes: The operator's own listing on The Dyrt (verified 2023) says: 'Backpacking instead of traveling by RV? We have sites to accommodate every kind of traveler, whether by bike, trailer or RV.' Campendium also tags it for tents. The 2026 website lists only RV sites, park models and day use, so confirm the tent rate. Restrooms and showers were recently renovated, and there's coin laundry, a pool and spa, Wi-Fi (new in 2026) and a store. This is the closest paid tent option to the line on the whole segment.

properties.name: Mayflower County Park (Riverside County)
properties.price: Tent or dry site about $35 (2023 dry-camp rate) and possibly higher now. Sites with water and electric were $49 in Sept 2026. Booking yourself online added an $8 fee in 2023.
properties.reservations: Riverside County reservations online (rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches) or call the office. Check-in is reported quick and friendly. Office hours not verified, so call before arriving late. Maximum stay 14 nights.
properties.access: All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go north on Intake Blvd (US 95) about 3.3 mi, east on 6th Ave 2.5 mi, then follow Colorado River Rd 0.5 mi to its end in the park. About 6.7 mi one way.
properties.notes: There is a separate tent and dry-camping area by the river (27 dry sites), plus 152 sites with water and electric for power. Hot showers and flush toilets, but only one bathhouse and it's far from some sites. Water spigots are everywhere, though one reviewer said the water tastes odd. Reviews from Sept and Oct 2026 confirm it's open and clean. There are no services nearby, so shop in Blythe first.

properties.name: McIntyre RV Resort (Peter McIntyre County Park)
properties.price: Standard tent site from $38/night, beachfront tent site from $43 (Campspot, Nov 2026). A 30-amp RV site is $50 if you need power.
properties.reservations: Book on Campspot (campspot.com/park/mcintyre-rv-resort-blythe-ca); walk-ins welcome. Office 7am to 4pm daily, California time.
properties.access: All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go south on Intake Blvd under I-10 for about 6 mi, then turn left onto Peter D McIntyre Ave (asphalt). About 6.6 mi one way.
properties.notes: About 20 tent sites on grass by the river, with newly renovated hot showers and restrooms for registered guests, a small store (ice and snacks), free Wi-Fi and a lagoon. New owners since June 1, 2025. A Campspot review from Oct 2026 and a Campendium review from Nov 2025 confirm it's open. Tent sites have no outlet.

properties.name: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area)
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit. No LTVA permit is needed because this is outside the Mule Mountain LTVA. Water and flush toilets are at the rest area 0.3 mi away, 24 h.
properties.reservations: None. You may NOT sleep inside the rest area itself: Caltrans has an 8-hour limit and no tents.
properties.access: Leave I-10 at exit 222. The Wiley's Well Rest Area sits on Wiley's Well Rd just north of the freeway. Ride a few hundred yards north on paved Wiley's Well Rd, or along the dirt powerline track parallel to I-10, and camp on open BLM desert out of sight of the road. Flat, firm ground.
properties.notes: Not a documented campsite; legal by land status. The BLM surface-management map shows BLM on every side of the interchange, inside Chuckwalla National Monument, and OSM shows no solar fencing here. It is the only spot between Blythe and Chiriaco where a dry camp sits beside water and toilets. It is 10 mi past the last store (BB Travel Center, exit 232) and 50 mi before Chiriaco. Two state prisons are 3 mi south, so stay north of I-10. Check for 'closed to camping' signs. Caltrans plans a rest-area water rebuild with no dates announced.

properties.name: Wiley's Well Campground (Mule Mountain LTVA, BLM)
properties.price: $40 LTVA short-visit permit, required Sept 15-Apr 15. It covers 14 consecutive days at any CA/AZ LTVA; there is no nightly rate.
properties.reservations: No reservations. Buy the permit from the camp host (not always present) or a BLM office. Tents are allowed only at designated sites within 500 ft of the vault toilet.
properties.access: Exit 222, then south on Wiley's Well Rd: 3 mi paved past the Chuckwalla Valley and Ironwood state prisons, then 6 mi of graded dirt that is normally washboarded. BLM notice dated Oct 15, 2026: the road was damaged by Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, is 'impassable for RVs and trailers', and is 4x4 only. A loaded bike will be slow, with possible walking. 18 mi round trip.
properties.notes: A real campground with tables, fire rings, a very clean vault toilet, trash and a dump station, but NO water; bring it from the rest area 9 mi back. Coon Hollow, 3 mi further south on the same damaged road, takes the same permit. Probably not worth the detour this week.

properties.name: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange)
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Exit 201, south side. Paved Chuckwalla Valley Rd meets Corn Springs Rd at the ramps; go a few hundred yards west of Corn Springs Rd onto BLM desert. Keep clear of the fenced Maverick Solar project north and east of the exit.
properties.notes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map, inside Chuckwalla National Monument). It saves the sandy 7.8-mi ride to Corn Springs campground. A dry camp: the nearest water is Wiley's Well RA, 21 mi back, or Chiriaco, 29 mi ahead. Small dirt service roads (pipeline/utility) criss-cross the area.

properties.name: Corn Springs Campground (BLM)
properties.price: $6/night, first come first served, 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: First come, first served: 9 sites including 1 group site, no reservations. Quiet hours 9pm-8am.
properties.access: Exit 201, then south and west on Corn Springs Rd: about 7-8 mi of compacted/graded dirt with soft sandy wash crossings (a 2019 review said '4WD recommended'), climbing gently to about 1,600 ft. Condition after the October 2026 storm is unknown.
properties.notes: A palm oasis with petroglyphs, shade ramadas, tables and grills; usually nearly empty midweek. BLM lists potable water, but a Jan 30, 2026 visitor reported 'No water available', so carry all you need. The round trip is more than 15 mi of dirt and sand. The Countri Bike rider (2016-17) considered it and went on to Chiriaco.

properties.name: BLM land south of Desert Center, I-10 exit 192
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Exit 192 (Desert Center). On the south side a rough dirt track (OSM grade 4) runs south-west across BLM land; camp a few hundred yards in. Off limits: the town lots, the Caltrans yard, and the fenced Oberon/Athos solar fields north and east of the exit.
properties.notes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map). Halfway between Blythe and Chiriaco. Desert Center has NO store, water or gas, so carry dinner, breakfast and water for the 19 mi to Chiriaco. Lake Tamarisk Library, 2 mi north, has a fountain only Tue/Thu/Sat in the daytime.

properties.name: BLM land north of Eagle Mountain Rd, I-10 exit 189
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Exit 189, then north on paved Eagle Mountain Rd. BLM desert lies on both sides just north of the interchange.
properties.notes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map; no solar fields mapped here). An alternative to the Desert Center exit. Dry camp.

properties.name: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM)
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Exit 182 (Red Cloud Rd), south side. A big gravel lot sits right by I-10, and dispersed sites run along a 2.2-mi graded dirt road toward the Chuckwalla Mtns. Light washboard and dips, with soft sand in places: a 2WD van got stuck in 2022.
properties.notes: The only DOCUMENTED dispersed area near the line between Blythe and Chiriaco (Campendium, 6 reviews, latest Apr 2023). Freeway noise near the lot, a high-voltage line nearby, Border Patrol around. It is 9.5 mi before the Chiriaco store, which makes it the stop if daylight runs out (sunset is about 4:45 pm PST). No water.

properties.name: Chiriaco Summit - Patton Museum Dry Camp Area
properties.price: Free. There are no facilities at the sites; water and restrooms are at the Chevron food mart (open 24 h) and the coffee shop, 400 m away.
properties.reservations: First come, first served. A camp host takes your name and plate number. If you arrive after dark, set up and check in the next morning (Dec 2024 review). Maximum stay is 5-7 nights.
properties.access: Exit 173. Paved to the museum, then take the dirt access road on the right side of the museum (sign: 'Welcome to Chiriaco Summit Dry Camp Area') to marked sites behind it. About 0.3 mi; the Chevron and cafe are about 400 m away.
properties.notes: The key camp on this segment: free, hosted, on BLM land, with marked sites including tent-only spots and stone fire rings. The NPS lists Chiriaco Summit as a camping option south of the park. Nearby: the Chevron food mart (24 h), Foster's Freeze (8am-9pm) and the coffee shop (6am-11pm). A 2021 reviewer got free water at the station. Some I-10 truck noise. A cyclist camped here in 2016 and sat in the coffee shop until it closed. A Jan 2026 reviewer described a dozen trucks parked in the area, so confirm with the host or the store. It is 68 mi from Blythe and 49 mi from the last water at Wiley's

properties.name: Joshua Tree South BLM Dispersed Camping (Cottonwood Springs Rd)
properties.price: Free; 14-day limit.
properties.reservations: None, first come. There are hundreds of fire-ring sites and it effectively never fills.
properties.access: Exit 168, then north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd; dirt roads branch east and west just north of the freeway and are passable by car. Camp only in the BLM sections on the NPS map: east of the road between I-10 and the Edison power-line road, west of the road north of the power line, and a block further east. It is checkerboarded with private land, and the NPS says to camp 300+ ft from roadways.
properties.notes: 155 Campendium reviews through May 2026; a 2024 tent camper liked it, and the NPS BLM map was updated May 2026. The ground is crushed granite and sand, with little freeway noise. Mostly RVs, busier on weekends; good Verizon/T-Mobile coverage. No water: fill at Chiriaco, 4.3 mi east, or at Cottonwood, 6 mi uphill (needs the $15 park entry). This is also mile ~4 of the Mecca variant.

properties.name: Cottonwood Campground (Joshua Tree National Park)
properties.price: $35/site/night (up to 6 people and 3 tents), plus a $15 per-person 7-day park entry on a bike. Group tent-only sites cost $55.
properties.reservations: Reservation only, year-round, on recreation.gov. There is NO cell service at the campground, so book before leaving I-10. Check-in at noon; the campground is open 24 h. Availability on the night of Nov 1: 43-50 sites free for Mon-Thu Nov 2-5 and Mon Nov 9, 26 for Sun Nov 8, but only 1 site (B16) left for each of Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.
properties.access: Exit 168, then 7 mi north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd/Pinto Basin Rd, climbing about 1,250 ft (1,750 to 3,000 ft). Slow when loaded; return the same way. The NPS describes the park's paved roads as crumbling and uneven.
properties.notes: The only campground with potable water and flush toilets between Blythe and Indio; no showers. Limit is 14 nights Oct-May. A riding group in Dec 2019 found it full, and rangers enforced the rules. The only current park alert is the Geology Tour Rd flood closure, which is not on this route. Worth the climb only for water and a proper site.

properties.name: Thousand Trails Palm Springs RV Resort
properties.price: No tent site type is offered. Non-member RV sites were about $46/night (Campendium, Dec 2025). WiFi costs extra.
properties.reservations: Non-members can book nightly online. Campsite check-in is at noon; the office is open Mon-Fri 9-5. A reviewer advises arriving in daylight.
properties.access: Paved and flat. On Varner Rd just north of I-10 at Washington St, about 0.5 mi off the line.
properties.notes: Open for the season 9/15/2026-5/15/2027. Its rules allow '1 RV, 2 vehicles, and 2 tents' per site, but booking only offers RV back-in and pull-through sites. Call and ask whether a tent-only cyclist can take an RV site. It has a pool, spa, showers and laundry, and sits right on the line.

properties.name: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $39/night, $45.93 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Under Desert Skies' tent/RV site with power and water hookups.
properties.reservations: Request to book (not instant). The host approves, then emails registration and waiver forms, and gives a 15-minute orientation on arrival. Full refund if you cancel 3 or more days ahead. Request at least a day or two before you arrive.
properties.access: About 9.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Long Canyon Rd/21st Ave (bike router). The last mile is a maintained dirt road. About 200-250 ft of net climbing (to about 770 ft). The host sends directions because phone GPS is often wrong.
properties.notes: The closest good tent spot to Palm Springs: hot outdoor showers, accessible porta-potties, mineral well water and an outdoor kitchen. 575 bookings, 97% recommend. The host warns of frequent high winds and near-freezing winter nights. The pool is winterized mid-Oct to April. It is a sober community farm.

properties.name: Palm Springs Oasis RV Resort
properties.price: No tent rate. Non-member RV site about $95 (Jan 2024 review).
properties.reservations: Thousand Trails/Encore booking; ask by phone.
properties.access: Paved and flat. On Date Palm Dr in Cathedral City, about 0.4 mi off the line.
properties.notes: An Encore/Thousand Trails park. All 140 sites are full-hookup RV pads, mostly long-term guests, under the airport approach. Reviewers complain about the showers. Expect a no on tents, but it is right on the line.

properties.name: Happy Traveler RV Park (aka Happy Traveller)
properties.price: No tent rate published (call for rates). RV sites about $100 (Nov 2025).
properties.reservations: Call or email happytrav@hotmail.com. A night manager is on site.
properties.access: Paved and flat. About 1.4 mi from the line through south Palm Springs streets to W Mesquite Ave. About 1.1 mi from downtown.
properties.notes: The only campground in central Palm Springs, sheltered from the valley winds. The operator lists only full-hookup RV sites and says nothing about tents. Call. Reviewers say the bathhouse is dated.

properties.name: Windy Point x Palm Springs (Hipcamp off-grid lot)
properties.price: $30.40/night, $37.63 with Hipcamp fees.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp Instant Book. The host sends a custom wind report before your stay.
properties.access: Paved and flat. Just off CA-111 at Windy Point via Overture Dr/Palm Oasis Ave, about 0.5 mi off the line. You enter over a 6-inch curb.
properties.notes: A 7,500 sq ft lot with a 5-ft chain-link fence, a lockable gate, a streetlight and a picnic table. It is completely self-contained: no water, toilet, power or trash, and the host asks you to bring a portable toilet. The host warns that 'Standard free-standing tents generally don't work here' because gusts can reach gale force. Book it only when the forecast is light, and read the host's wind report. NWS shows easterly flow Nov 5-8, which can still gust at the pass mouth. Water and snacks at Windy Cove Market & Gas, 60490 Overture Dr. 98% recommend (20 ratings).

properties.name: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy)
properties.price: Free (donations appreciated).
properties.reservations: Reserve at least 48 h ahead with the online request form (check the campground calendar first). Walk-ins are accepted only if the campground is not full and you check in at the ranger station before 4:15 pm. The preserve is open 8 am-5 pm. Check-out 11 am. Up to 3 nights per 30 days; capacity 30 guests a day. Reservations can be cancelled for hazardous weather.
properties.access: Paved. Leave CA-111 at Tipton Rd and follow Whitewater Cutoff to Whitewater Canyon Rd at Bonnie Bell, then 4.2 mi up the 2-lane canyon road to the preserve. That is about 6.5-9.5 mi from the line depending on the turn (the bike router gives 9.5 mi from the I-10/CA-111 junction). You climb about 1,000 ft (roughly 1,100 to 2,190 ft). Next morning, descend and get on I-10 westbound at the Whitewater exit, which is bike-legal there.
properties.notes: The best-value stop on the segment: a free tent area with flush toilets, drinking water, a river and ponds. No fires of any kind, no generators, and no cell signal on site (signal starts about 3.5 mi down the road). The WHOLE PRESERVE WAS CLOSED SUN 11/1/2026 for hazardous weather and flood conditions, and the operator warns of more El Nino closures this winter. Confirm with whitewaterpreserve@wildlandsconservancy.org or by phone, and submit the form by about Nov 3 for a Nov 5-6 night. If you miss the 4:15 pm check-in, fall back to the Windy Point lot or to Banning KOA (about 15 mi on, with af

properties.name: BLM land along lower Whitewater Canyon Rd (Sand to Snow NM), unverified dispersed camping
properties.price: Free, if camping is legal there.
properties.reservations: None. Unverified; ask BLM before relying on it.
properties.access: Paved road. About 1.5-2.5 mi up Whitewater Canyon Rd from Bonnie Bell, roughly 5 mi from the line. The BLM parcels are mixed in with private land, and boundaries are not marked as far as we know.
properties.notes: The BLM land-status map shows BLM parcels beside the lower canyon road inside Sand to Snow National Monument. The monument page sends campers to BLM's general dispersed-camping rules but says nothing about this canyon, and no camper or rider report was found. Last resort only, for example if you miss the preserve's 4:15 pm check-in. Stay out of sight of homes and make no fire. The pass mouth is very windy.

properties.name: Cabazon Escape (private lot, The Dyrt)
properties.price: unknown (the listing shows a $1 placeholder).
properties.reservations: Request to book on The Dyrt, or by phone or email.
properties.access: Paved local streets. About 3-3.5 mi southeast of central Cabazon via Main St, Broadway, Bonita Ave and Almond St (the bike router gives 5.5 mi from the I-10 line). At about 1,520 ft, it is lower than Cabazon.
properties.notes: Listed in 2023 for tents and RVs. One of its two reviews (2023) called it 'more like a landfill' and left at once; the other, by a Dyrt staffer, praised waterfall access. It may be inactive. Call first; it is the only private listing at the Cabazon end.

properties.name: Banning Stagecoach KOA
properties.price: Tent rate not found (koa.com blocks automated reading). Recent nightly reports, probably for RV sites: $50 (2022) and $54 (2025). Tent sites 95-99 have water only, no power.
properties.reservations: Book with KOA online or by phone. The office closes around 5-6 pm (2022 review), but self check-in is available after hours; registration packets are left at the office.
properties.access: Paved and slightly downhill. From Ramsey St (the line) ride about 1 mi south on S San Gorgonio Ave (CA-243) under I-10. The ride back up next morning is mild, about 120 ft.
properties.notes: The only campground in the Cabazon-Banning-Beaumont stretch confirmed to take tents (sites 95-99), and the safest late-arrival option in the pass. It is gravel and RV-oriented (a 2016 reviewer said it is 'really not for tent camping'), with one bathhouse. 2025-26 reviews report broken sprinklers, overgrown grass and occasional broken toilets. The pool is closed in winter, and train horns carry at night. Reviews continue through May 2026.

properties.name: Country Hills RV Park
properties.price: No tent rate. Full-hookup RV site $68/night for 2 people, plus a one-time $15 resort fee (operator site, 2026). Showers take quarters.
properties.reservations: Book online or by phone with a credit card; cancel at least 72 h ahead. Check-in 1 pm. Gated, so call ahead for a late arrival (a 2023 guest arranged one).
properties.access: Paved. About 1.7 mi from the line in Beaumont via Pennsylvania Ave, 1st St, Michigan Ave and Roadrunner Dr, south of I-10 (bike router). The park is gated and needs a gate card.
properties.notes: The park rules are written entirely for RVs and say nothing about tents; The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is generic. Call before counting on it. Laundry is reported to cost $10 a load because of a card system.

properties.name: Noble Creek Regional Park RV campground (Beaumont-Cherry Valley Recreation and Park District)
properties.price: $35/night (2022) to $35-50 (The Dyrt), for RV sites. There are 9 dry sites.
properties.reservations: Required. Currently by phone or office@bcvparks.com to the district office only (Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-noon). No on-site check-in was reported.
properties.access: Paved and flat. About 0.8 mi west of Beaumont Ave on Oak Valley Pkwy.
properties.notes: The district's 2026 brochure lists 24 full-hookup, 15 half-hookup and 9 dry-camping sites. 2022 reviewers called it a parking lot with no visitor restrooms. The Dyrt shows tent sites and toilets, but no review confirms tents. A district notice says the park was closed for fire-camp operations one summer. Call.

properties.name: Bogart Regional Park campground (Cherry Valley)
properties.price: $35/night (sites 1-30); pets $2/day (district fee page).
properties.reservations: Book by phone or office@bcvparks.com with the district office, Mon-Thu 8-5 and Fri 8-noon. Online booking is suspended 'until further notice'. The park is open 7 am-sundown, with an attendant only Sat-Sun 8-3. The gate may be shut in the evening (a reviewer arriving after 5 pm worked the gate switch themselves). Max stay 7 nights.
properties.access: Paved, with about 400 ft of climbing (2,785 to 3,180 ft). From the line at Beaumont Ave and Cherry Valley Blvd, ride 2.3 mi via Cherry Valley Blvd, Live Oak Ave, Vineland/Noble/Dutton St and Cherry Ave (bike router). It is about 2 mi past the segment end.
properties.notes: A shaded foothill campground run by the local park district with flush restrooms and drinking water. At 3,180 ft it runs a few degrees colder than Banning, where lows of 51-57 F are forecast. The district warns of bears, and a campfire ban was in place at its last notice. Tents were barred during COVID (a cyclist found it closed to tents in 2021), but reviewers tent-camped in Aug 2025. Call by Friday noon for a weekend night.

properties.name: Fisherman's Retreat (San Timoteo Canyon)
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: Unknown; call. It is a membership resort (Halo Resorts) with a separate non-member area.
properties.access: Paved: about 6.3 mi from Cherry Valley Blvd/Calimesa Blvd (mile ~358.6) via Palmer Ave and San Timoteo Canyon Rd, about 785 ft downhill going in. On to Redlands is 10–11 mi via San Timoteo Canyon Rd and Alessandro Rd (470–730 ft of climbing), rejoining the line at ~mile 366–368, so the detour costs about 10 mi.
properties.notes: Private RV resort on three stocked fishing lakes, with a store, restaurant and pool. Runs as a membership park with a non-member section. The Dyrt lists showers, drinking water and toilets. Non-member nightly rates, tent policy and 2026 status are all unverified (no website, Facebook only). Long detour into the canyon.

properties.name: Yucaipa Regional Park
properties.price: Tent spaces A–I. The county lists $35 Mon–Thu / $45 Fri–Sun for no-hookup sites (max 6 people), and group tent camping at $5/person plus a $20 group fee. Add a $10 non-refundable reservation fee. Seniors/veterans/military get $5 off Sun–Thu. Expect roughly $35–55 total for one person.
properties.reservations: Online only at parkreservations.sbcounty.gov, at least 24 h ahead (no same-day booking). Check-in 3 pm. If you arrive after the 5 pm closing, go straight to your site; after-hours instructions come in the confirmation email (check spam). Park hours are 7:30 am–5 pm from Oct 31, 2026 to May 2027.
properties.access: Paved: about 4.7 mi from Calimesa Blvd (Hist US 99, mile ~360.8) via Avenue G, Wildwood Canyon Rd, Yucaipa Blvd and 5th St to Oak Glen Rd, about 570 ft of climbing. On to Redlands via Oak Glen Rd, Avenue D, 17th St and Tennessee St is about 7 mi, rejoining at ~mile 366, so the detour costs about 6 mi. Stay on paved roads; routers may suggest the Crafton Hills Ridge Trail.
properties.notes: San Bernardino County park with 9 designated tent spaces (A–I on the park map) next to the 42-site RV loop; tents are allowed only there. The county lists hot showers and restrooms, but a 2024 reviewer in group site A said there were no showers near the tent area. Potable water, fire rings, three fishing lakes. A June 2025 reviewer camped in 'tent site E'. Elevation about 2,600 ft, and power-safety shutoffs are possible. The park also closes on the third Wednesday of November (Nov 18), after his window.

properties.name: The Unhitched Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $99.51/night base for the ranch's RV/tent site (about $117 with Hipcamp fees)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (the host approves). Usually one group at a time on the ranch.
properties.access: Paved but hilly: about 9 mi from Barton Rd (Loma Linda, mile ~372.7) via Barton Rd and Reche Canyon Rd, a narrow two-lane canyon road with commuter traffic; about 900 ft of climbing. Leave via Reche Canyon Rd and Washington St to Colton (7.5 mi, rejoining at ~mile 375), so the detour costs about 14 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
properties.notes: Family-run Clydesdale and longhorn ranch of about 40 acres, with wild burros nearby. Potable water, toilets, laundry, Wi-Fi, electric and water hookups, campfires allowed. 168 bookings, 100% recommend. Expensive for one rider, and the climb in is steep. The Hipcamp map pin is approximate.

properties.name: Riverview Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $33.25/night base for the tent site (about $39 with Hipcamp fees)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book; arrival details come after booking.
properties.access: Paved: about 8.7 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Riverview Dr, mostly downhill (about 550 ft). Back to the Pacific Electric Trail is about 11 mi via Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave (about 650 ft up, rejoining at ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 16 mi.
properties.notes: Private, shaded property near Mt. Rubidoux and the Santa Ana River. The listing promises clean bathrooms and hot showers, plus potable water, a shared fire ring, picnic tables and Wi-Fi. The tent site has 36 bookings and the listing is 95% recommended. It is next door to Rancho Jurupa and is a cheaper, quieter alternative. The map pin is approximate.

properties.name: Rancho Jurupa Regional Park
properties.price: $40–55 per site per night (2025–26 reports; $55 is full hookup). No separate tent rate found.
properties.reservations: Reserve at rivcoparks.org or 800-234-7275. Walk-ups register at the staffed entrance gate (single-file line). Late arrivals with a reservation get gate, bathroom and laundry codes (Dec 2025 review).
properties.access: Paved: about 8.9 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Wallace St, mostly downhill (about 500 ft). To rejoin, take Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave to the Pacific Electric Trail (11 mi, about 650 ft up, ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 17 mi.
properties.notes: Large Riverside County campground on the Santa Ana River. The Lakeview side has gravel roads with water/electric sites; the Cottonwood side has paved full-hookup sites. Tents are allowed. Showers on both sides (tokens on the Lakeview side), laundry, a small store, ranger patrols. Busy and loud on weekends. A ranger warned campers to lock up bikes in 2020. rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches, so fees come from reviews.

properties.name: Harmony Heaven Campyard (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $64/night base for 'Starlight', a pre-pitched 4-person safari tent (about $75 with fees). A-frame campers from $79.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book.
properties.access: Paved: about 3.5 mi north of the Pacific Electric Trail (mile ~397.6) via Hellman Ave, Lemon Ave, Beryl St and Carnelian St, about 570 ft of climbing. Back down to the trail at Carnelian St is 4 mi (~mile 399), so the detour costs about 6 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
properties.notes: Private half-acre 'campyard'. You sleep in the host's safari tent; no bring-your-own-tent site is listed, so ask the host. Private outdoor bathroom with a hot shower, outdoor kitchen, fire pit, pool, Wi-Fi, laundry and farm animals. 12 bookings, 100% recommend. It is the only tent-style stay near the Pacific Electric Trail between Rialto and Pomona. The map pin is approximate.

properties.name: Fairplex RV Park (former Los Angeles/Pomona Fairplex KOA)
properties.price: unknown; call (2020 reports: about $50–75 per site)
properties.reservations: Call or book online; 72-h cancellation policy. Office hours are not published.
properties.access: Paved and flat: 1.1 mi from Bonita Ave via White Ave (mile ~408). Back to Bonita Ave is 2.1 mi, so the detour costs about 2 mi.
properties.notes: 183 full-hookup sites plus cabins beside the LA County Fairgrounds. Showers, laundry, heated pool and spa, mini-market, free Wi-Fi. As a KOA it sold tent sites with electric (2020 review), and The Dyrt and Campendium still list tent sites. It is no longer a KOA, and its own website now advertises only RV sites and cabins, so confirm tents by phone. Sites are tight and some are near traffic. The new Metro A Line stations at La Verne and Pomona (opened Sept 2025) are within a couple of miles.

properties.name: Bonelli Bluffs RV Resort & Campground
properties.price: $30/night walk-in tent site for up to 2 people; +$10 per extra person (max 6); pets $2/day
properties.reservations: Tent sites can't be booked online; call 909-599-8355. The guest-service lobby and market are open Sun–Wed 8 am–5 pm and Thu–Sat 8 am–7 pm. A kiosk is open 24 h, with an after-hours line.
properties.access: Paved: about 2.6 mi from Bonita Ave (San Dimas, mile ~409) via Wheeler Ave and Puddingstone Dr to the resort entrance on Camper View Rd, about 200 ft of climbing onto the bluff. Continue via Puddingstone Dr and Walnut Ave back to Bonita Ave (3.7 mi, ~mile 411), so the detour costs about 4 mi. Avoid the park's dirt trails that routers suggest.
properties.notes: The best-equipped tent option in the LA basin: walk-in grass tent sites with picnic tables and fire pits above Puddingstone Lake. Clean restrooms, showers, laundry (6 am–11 pm), two pools, a market and free Wi-Fi. The tent area is on a slope with a carry from parking, so wheel the bike in. Expect small-plane noise from Brackett Field and occasional late weekend parties. LA County day-use areas close Mon/Tue, but the resort office lists hours every day. It is 31 line-miles from the theater, and the Metro A Line San Dimas station is a few miles away.

properties.name: Marshall Canyon Regional Park campground
properties.price: unknown
