properties.reservations: Reservation only, through LA County Parks (reservations.lacounty.gov). It appears geared to groups. LA County regional parks are closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
properties.access: Paved and steep: about 6.3 mi north from Bonita Ave/White Ave in La Verne (mile ~407) into the foothills, about 1,070 ft of climbing.
properties.notes: LA County says the park has 'forty campsites' with barbecues and a fire circle, available for reservation, next to the Marshall Canyon equestrian center. I found no details on individual bookings, fees or restrooms. Long climb. Use it only if Bonelli Bluffs and Fairplex are full.

properties.name: Gould Mesa Trail Camp (Angeles NF)
properties.price: Free (no camping fee; the Adventure Pass applies only to parked vehicles)
properties.reservations: First-come, first-served; no reservations. Arrive before dark because of the creek crossings (sunset about 4:55 pm).
properties.access: 6.2 mi from Colorado Blvd (Pasadena, mile ~434.6): Orange Grove Blvd, Rosemont Ave and Arroyo Blvd to the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead (paved, about 600 ft up), then 2 mi up the Gabrielino Trail (dirt and broken pavement, several creek crossings; bikes allowed). About 820 ft of climbing in all. From camp to the Elysian Theater is 11.9 mi.
properties.notes: Free primitive trail camp with about 6–10 sites, tables, fire rings, a vault toilet and bear boxes. No potable water (creek only, treat it) and no showers. Steady day-hiker and mountain-bike traffic. It is not in the Eaton Fire closure, which shut the Millard and Idlehour camps through 2027, and a Feb 2026 reviewer used it. The new USFS website has no page for it, though, so call the district to confirm. Fire danger is 'Very High': no wood fires. It is the closest legal tent site to the Elysian Theater. Stay limit is 14 days.

properties.name: Unnamed OSM caravan site on N Pinal Ave (likely RV section beside Rodeo Estates MHP)
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: About 3 mi north of downtown on N Pinal Ave (paved), behind the direction of travel.
properties.notes: App baseline entry (OSM way 1348098748). It has no name and sits next to Rodeo Estates Mobile Home Park. I found no evidence that it takes overnight or tent guests. Do not count on it; candidate for removal from the app.

properties.name: High Chaparral RV Park (OSM 'Unnamed campground')
properties.price: Tent rate unknown. RV overnight $37 with the 50% Passport America discount (reported Nov 1, 2026), so roughly double without it.
properties.website: unknown (highchaparralrvpark.com now redirects to an unrelated spam site; do not use it)
properties.reservations: Office check-in; reviewers checked in easily. Late-arrival policy unknown.
properties.access: About 10 mi south-east of I-8 exit 174 on paved roads (Arizona City side), behind you.
properties.notes: Baseline 'Unnamed campground' node 13092955624 is this park. Adults-only (18+); kids allowed only Apr–Sep for up to 7 days. Mix of park models and RVs, pool, laundry. The Dyrt tags it 'tent sites' but no review or rule confirms tents. Call first.

properties.name: Motoland MX Park (weekend camping only)
properties.price: Free on practice weekends (Fri–Sun). Race-weekend fee not published.
properties.reservations: Message them before arriving; weekends only.
properties.access: South of I-8 between exits 172 and 167. Operator address: 'just east of 6734 Sisler Rd'. Local route unverified; about 2.5 mi on rural roads.
properties.notes: Operator FAQ: camping allowed only Friday–Sunday, and you should message ahead. You would pass on Monday Nov 2, so this is effectively not usable. The site says racing resumes in winter 2027 and posts no practice dates.

properties.name: Mammoth Homestead (Hipcamp farm stay)
properties.price: $32/night base plus Hipcamp fees. One RV/tent site, up to 4 guests; includes main-house bathroom, shower, laundry, water, 30A power and Wi-Fi.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp booking required. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation policy.
properties.access: Listing says 'right off I-8'; Montgomery Rd exit 167 is the likely exit. Exact address is given after booking, and the Hipcamp pin is approximate.
properties.notes: The only full-service tent-friendly stop near the line in the Casa Grande area, but only about 11 mi into the day. New listing with no reviews yet. No campfires. Goats and chickens on site.

properties.name: Desert Springs 55+ RV Ranch (OSM 'Unnamed campground')
properties.price: Tent rate unknown. RV about $30/night (2023 report).
properties.reservations: Reservations accepted (Campendium). Late-arrival policy unknown.
properties.access: I-8 exit 167, then 1.5 mi north on Montgomery Rd (paved).
properties.notes: Baseline 'Unnamed campground' way 761144406 is this park. Campendium: 55+ park, adults only (18+), full-time residents. The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is not backed by any review. Don't count on it; call. Feedlot and dairy smells on east winds.

properties.name: Camp Liebre (Hipcamp, off-grid site)
properties.price: $17/night base plus Hipcamp fees, with no amenities. One site, 6 guests max.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation.
properties.access: About 4 mi east of I-8 exit 151 on paved AZ 84, then about 0.5 mi on unpaved Liebre Rd. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate. About 0.5 mi off AZ 84 if you ride the AZ 84 alternative.
properties.notes: Raw pack-in/pack-out desert site next to a big saguaro: no toilet, no water, no campfires. You need to arrive with water. New listing with no reviews.

properties.name: West Pinal County Park (Jim Kortsen / West Pinal Park campground)
properties.price: $10/night standard site (plus about $2 online booking fee); larger or group sites about $35. Each site has a shade ramada, picnic table and grill. No cash.
properties.phone: 520-866-6920 (Pinal County Parks office, weekdays, per camp host; Campendium lists 520-866-6910)
properties.reservations: Online only (Campspot); cash no longer accepted. Booking on your phone on arrival works, including after dark; cell coverage is excellent on all carriers. Reserve ahead in winter, when it often fills. Stay limit 14 days (host) or 7 (Campendium).
properties.access: I-8 exit 151 (AZ 84, mile 27.2), then about 1 mi east on paved AZ 84 to the entrance at 50801 W Hwy 84, then a well-graded gravel loop. On route if you ride AZ 84.
properties.notes: Clean county dry camp with sites far apart; a reviewer notes tent campers hear the I-8 road noise. Porta-potties only: no water, power or showers. Fill up in Stanfield or at Wild West RV Ranch, which also sells dump and fill. Ground fires banned. Feedlot smell on east winds. Volunteer camp host Oct–Easter. Last review Oct 10, 2026: clean, well maintained.

properties.name: Supreme's Therapeutic Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $36/night base plus Hipcamp fees. One site, 6 guests max.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation.
properties.access: About 3.5 mi north of AZ 84 near I-8 exit 151, on local roads of unknown surface. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate.
properties.notes: The description says tent campers get bathroom and shower access, but the amenity list says no toilet, no showers and no potable water. Confirm with the host. Horses and chickens; campfires allowed. New listing with no reviews.

properties.name: Patriot Place (private 5-acre camp, The Dyrt request-to-book)
properties.price: $10–$20/night (The Dyrt listing)
properties.reservations: Request to book on The Dyrt; contact the host ahead.
properties.access: About 3 mi north of the I-8 exit 151 area on S Hidden Valley Rd, which OSM tags as unpaved. Pin from The Dyrt.
properties.notes: Host-run 5-acre private property in a 55+ neighborhood. The listing offers tent sites, showers and trash, and allows fires and quiet dogs. No reviews; unverified.

properties.name: Off Road Camp @ Jurassic Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $32/night base plus Hipcamp fees. Includes water hookup and Wi-Fi.
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book.
properties.access: North of I-8 exit 151 toward Hidden Valley, about 9–10 mi on local roads, some likely unpaved. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate.
properties.notes: Horse ranch 1,000 ft from a BLM off-road trailhead. Four dispersed RV/tent spaces with water and Wi-Fi but no toilet; campfires allowed. Booked once, no reviews. Far off the line; only worth it if everything else is full.

properties.name: Vekol Valley Road BLM dispersed (Sonoran Desert National Monument)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None; walk in any time.
properties.access: I-8 exit 144 (Vekol Rd), then south on graded gravel Vekol Rd with some washboard. The first ~0.3 mi is private land. BLM runs from about 0.4 to 1.2 mi, then a private parcel at about 1.2–1.6 mi, then BLM again from about 1.7 mi on. Climb is minor; the exit is at roughly 1,700 ft.
properties.notes: Most popular free camp on this stretch, legal from an interchange. Campendium lists it as tent-OK; reviews from Nov 2025 and Feb 2026. Ride at least 1–2 mi in to escape truck noise and the trash near the entrance. Border Patrol traffic is frequent, military jets pass over, and it can be crowded in Feb–Mar. BLM warns the southern monument is a smuggling corridor. No water anywhere: carry everything from Casa Grande or Stanfield.

properties.name: Freeman Rd exit 140 / Lost Horse Tank BLM dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None; walk in any time.
properties.access: I-8 exit 140 (Freeman Rd). Go under the interstate and about 500 ft south on washboard gravel to a T, then right (west) on W Old 84, an old unmaintained paved road. Sites start within about 0.5 mi. BLM also lies north of the exit ('Freeman Rd Camping'). Elevation about 1,800 ft, near the Maricopa Mountains summit of I-8.
properties.notes: Legal and close to an interchange; Campendium rates it 5.0 across 22 reviews (latest Nov 2025: no one else there, no road noise). A reviewer felt 'very comfortable and safe'. Strong Verizon signal from a nearby tower. No services for about 20 mi either way (Gila Bend Pilot is 21 mi on).

properties.name: BLM Road #8029 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off I-8, no ramp)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: No interchange. A two-track leaves I-8 directly through a gate around milepost 135–136, with a 4-inch drop off the pavement, rocky and sandy. The first several miles are a wilderness cherry-stem with only ~50 ft of non-wilderness each side; open camping at the Big Horn area 3.5–4 mi in.
properties.notes: Gray-area fallback only. Leaving a controlled-access interstate between interchanges is not a designated exit, so use it only if wind stops you between Freeman (38) and Gila Bend (59). Camp beside the two-track: bikes are banned inside the wilderness. The companion road #8011 leaves the EASTBOUND lanes and cannot be reached westbound.

properties.name: BLM Road #8030 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off I-8, no ramp)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: No interchange. An unsigned two-track leaves I-8 through gates around milepost 129–130, with V-shaped wash dips and sandy washes; 4WD country. It passes old corrals and tanks, then enters a ~50 ft-wide wilderness cherry-stem corridor.
properties.notes: Same gray-area access caveat as #8029. Weak cell signal in this dip between the Freeman and Gila Bend towers. Pitch near the road or the corral area, never in the wilderness.

properties.name: BLM Road #8032 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off westbound I-8)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: No interchange. The road leaves the WESTBOUND lanes through a gate around milepost 127. It splits into several spots west of the wilderness boundary and eventually reaches AZ 238. Not suitable for trailers.
properties.notes: Gray-area access as for #8029, but it is on your side of the highway. Sites further from I-8 are quieter. A couple of bars of cell signal. Gila Bend's Pilot is about 9 mi on.

properties.name: BLM land along Old Highway 84, east of Gila Bend exit 119 (incl. the 'BLM road 8035' spot)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit). Buy water, food and a truck-stop shower at the Pilot or Love's.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Legal route: I-8 exit 119 (Butterfield Trail, mile 58.7), north about 0.5 mi past the Pilot, then east on Old Highway 84. It is a compacted dirt track (OSM: grade 2, smoothness 'bad') on the north side of I-8. The first ~1.4 mi of the track is State Trust land, which needs a permit to camp. BLM begins at about 32.9234,-112.6413 and continues about 4 mi to the track's end at the 'BLM road 8035' spot (32.9090,-112.5950), which can also be reached by a gate straight off the I-8 shoulder near MP 124.
properties.notes: The closest legal tent spot to Gila Bend, since no town campground takes tents. Fill up at the Pilot (exit 119), ride about 2 mi back east on the dirt track and camp on flat desert. It is within 0.5 mi of I-8, so expect truck noise. Some illegal dumping near town. Cell service is good. Land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, and The Dyrt describes free scattered sites beyond the gate at the 8035 end.

properties.name: Augie's Quail Trail RV Park (status unknown)
properties.price: unknown
properties.phone: unknown (The Dyrt shows 928-683-2850, which is Sonoran Desert RV Park's number)
properties.website: unknown (augiesquailtrailrvpark.com and aqtrvaz.com no longer resolve)
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: The Dyrt pin is on Butterfield Trail beside Sonoran Desert RV Park.
properties.notes: Only a bare listing on The Dyrt with no reviews; not in OSM. Probably closed or absorbed by the neighbouring park. Treat as nonexistent unless you see it in person.

properties.name: Palms Mobile Home & RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate unknown. RV $25–$38/night (2021–2023 reports), half price with Passport America.
properties.reservations: Walk-in; call ahead because the office is often unattended.
properties.access: On the line in Gila Bend, one block off Pima St (I-8 Business), walking distance to Love's, Chevron and Circle K.
properties.notes: Mostly a run-down mobile-home community with a few back-in RV spaces. Reviewers report loose dogs, roosters, trains, an office that is often empty (pay through the door slot), and a sign advertising showers that one reviewer could not find. Laundry was reported burned in 2023. The only possible in-town option; ask whether they will take a tent, and expect no.

properties.name: BLM land on Agua Caliente Rd, north of Sentinel exit 87
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: I-8 exit 87 (Sentinel), past Conde's and the Chevron, then north-west on paved Agua Caliente Rd. The first ~1.5 mi is State Trust land; BLM begins about 1.6 mi from I-8 (32.8804,-113.2259) and continues along the road. A BLM strip also lies about 0.4–1 mi south of I-8, behind a private frontage parcel, with no mapped road. Further east and south is the Goldwater Range: keep out.
properties.notes: I found no camper reports for this exact spot. Land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, and BLM land is open to dispersed camping unless posted. Check for 'no camping' signs and camp out of sight of the road. Water and snacks at Conde's Middle of Nowhere and the Chevron at the exit (hours unverified). The State Trust land closer to I-8 is legal only with an Arizona State Land Department recreation permit.

properties.name: BLM land at Sentinel exit 87 (dirt track south or frontage road west)
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
properties.phone: 623-580-5500 (BLM Lower Sonoran Field Office / Phoenix District)
properties.reservations: None; first come. Arrive any time.
properties.access: I-8 exit 87 (Sentinel). South option: a graded dirt track (OSM grade3, way 1144544092) leaves the exit beside Conde's/Chevron and runs south. BLM land starts about 0.3 mi south of I-8 (32.854,-113.215) and runs at least 2 mi south. The Barry M. Goldwater Range (USAF), which is closed, begins 2-4 mi south: do not cross its signs or fence. North option: a paved frontage road runs west from the exit along the north side of I-8. BLM land starts about 1.3 mi west (32.859,-113.235), about 1.5 riding mi from the exit, and continues toward the Sentinel rest area. The first 1.3 mi north of the exit is State Trust land (ASLD permit needed). A third option, from segment I8-A: BLM land along paved Agua Caliente Rd, about 1.6 mi NW.
properties.notes: I found no camper reports for these spots. The land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, checked at 6 points: BLM directly south of the exit and west along the north frontage road, State Trust land NW of the exit, and USAF range about 4 mi south. Camp out of sight of I-8; Border Patrol traffic is normal here. Water and snacks at Conde's Middle of Nowhere and the Chevron at the exit (hours unverified). ADOT's Sentinel rest areas, about 2-3 mi west (corridor mi 94.6 and 95.3), reopened in January 2024 with new restrooms and water but are not legal campsites.

properties.name: Sun Portal Acres (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $25/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (one RV/tent site, up to 4 guests)
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Check-in 2-10 PM; strict no-refund cancellation; 1-night minimum; bookable 12 months out.
properties.access: I-8 exit 73 (Aztec): 0.3 mi on historic US 80/Aztec Rd, then about 1.8 mi south on unpaved N Avenue 69 1/2 E. The host says 2WD access; loose gravel, flat. South of I-8.
properties.notes: A new listing with no reviews yet. Private open-desert acreage with a firepit and trash bin, and nothing else. Carry all your water from Sentinel (13 mi back) or Dateland (6 mi ahead). Aztec has no store.

properties.name: Aztec Hills Retreat (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $15/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (40 dispersed RV/tent sites)
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp.
properties.access: I-8 exit 73 (Aztec): historic US 80/Aztec Rd, then south on unpaved N Avenue 69 1/2 E, about 2.5 mi in all. Open 80-acre parcel south of I-8; you camp where you park.
properties.notes: It is the cheapest paid tent spot on this segment. One Hipcamp review (100%). No toilet, water or shade, but campfires are allowed. Sun Portal Acres is about 0.5 mi away if this one is full. Water: Dateland Travel Center, 6 mi ahead.

properties.name: Oasis RV Park at Aztec Hills
properties.price: Tent rate not published. RV full hookup was $35 (Mar 2025) and $40 (Mar 2026).
properties.reservations: Call ahead. A 2025 reviewer got a call back within minutes for a one-night site. Also a Harvest Hosts host (self-contained RVs only).
properties.access: On the old US 80 frontage road between exits 73 and 67, 0.5 mi south via Ave 66E/Morton Rd (1401 S Ave 66E). From Dateland exit 67, ride 1.6 mi back east on paved Old Highway 80 (about 2.2 mi total). From Aztec exit 73 the frontage road runs about 4 mi west to it; OSM shows part of it unpaved.
properties.notes: 35-site, 10-acre park with a pool, laundry, showers and a rec hall. Quiet and dark, though trains are audible; reviewed Mar and Apr 2026. No listing (Campendium, The Dyrt, RoverPass) shows tent sites, and The Dyrt marks it RV-only. Ask by phone. Dateland RV Park, 3 mi on, takes tents.

properties.name: Dateland RV Park
properties.price: Not published. Last reported nightly rate $26 (May 2023); The Dyrt lists 'from $25'. Ask for a tent rate.
properties.reservations: Walk-in. Register at the gift shop; dateland.com lists 8 AM-9 PM daily for the travel center. After-hours arrival is unverified, so call before 9 PM.
properties.access: I-8 exit 67 (Dateland / Ave 64E): south of the interchange, 1/8 mi on the frontage road. Register at the Dateland Date Gardens gift shop / travel center across the road.
properties.notes: Campendium and The Dyrt list tent camping. A cyclist tented here in Sept 2022 under trees, noting 'very sandy roads' and a long walk to the showers. Another rider called the 'tent spaces' RV pull-throughs. Private shower rooms (sink, toilet, shower), dated laundry. I-8 on one side, Union Pacific trains about every 30 min on the other. An April 2026 review says the water tastes 'thick'. The travel center has a Chevron, Pizza Hut and date shakes, the only food between Sentinel and Tacna.

properties.name: BLM dispersed on S Avenue 52 1/2 E (Mohawk, I-8 exit 54)
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: I-8 exit 54. North side: about 0.3 mi west on Old Highway 80 / County 2nd St N, then north on S Avenue 52 1/2 E. BLM land begins at Old Hwy 80 and lines both sides of the road for 1.5+ mi. iOverlander says the road is washboard for the first 1/2 mi and some sites need you to cross a gravel berm. Between Dateland and here the old frontage road is abandoned (OSM access=no), so ride I-8 from exit 67 to exit 54 (about 13 mi).
properties.notes: This is the only free camp found between Dateland (mi 112) and Wellton (mi 150). An iOverlander report calls it 'dozens of free, level BLM sites, well dispersed'. I could not open the full listing to date it. The federal land map shows BLM at every point I checked along the road (8 points). Fill water at the Mohawk Rest Area (I-8 MP 56, corridor mi 124.6-125.1), 1 mi before the exit: OSM tags a public drinking-water fountain, restrooms and vending machines. Nearest food is Tacna, 13 mi west.

properties.name: Arizona State Trust land south of Tacna (ASLD recreation permit)
properties.price: Legal only with an Arizona State Land Department individual recreational permit: $15 for 12 months, bought online in advance. Camping is capped at 14 days per year.
properties.reservations: No reservations. Buy the permit online before you lose signal and carry proof (a screenshot works).
properties.access: I-8 exit 42 (Tacna): south past the Pilot/Shell on Main St/Ave 40E toward Copper Mountain RV Park. The federal land map shows State Trust land around the park on the north, east and south (checked at 7 points). Use an existing two-track and keep clear of the RV park, fenced or leased parcels and anything posted.
properties.notes: This is a legal fallback only; I found no camper reports for these parcels. It splits the 38-mi Dateland-Wellton gap if the Mohawk BLM site does not work out. All Tacna services are at the exit. In 2013 a cyclist was allowed to tent free behind the Chaparral Motel in Tacna; that is not current, but asking a business is a last resort.

properties.name: Coach Stop RV Park (adults only)
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Dry site $30/day, $42/day with electricity (rates effective Oct 2025).
properties.reservations: Call the office or use the site's reservation form.
properties.access: In Wellton, just north of Los Angeles Ave on Wellton Mohawk Dr.
properties.notes: The rate page says 'Coach Stop RV Park is an Adults Only Park' (not stated as 55+). Its $30 dry-site rate is the cheapest showers-and-toilets option in Wellton if they accept a tent, which no source confirms. 190 sites, laundry, game room.

properties.name: Desert Sands RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: On Los Angeles Ave (old US 80), Wellton, directly on the line.
properties.notes: The town directory gives this park the same phone number and description ('10 RV spaces, full hook-ups, cable TV, propane and coffee shop') as Lazy Cactus RV Park, so it may be the same operator or a directory mix-up. It has no reviews anywhere. Call the number and ask about both.

properties.name: Lazy Cactus RV Park
properties.price: From $25/night (The Dyrt, owner-managed listing, updated June 2025)
properties.reservations: Call; the park takes reservations.
properties.access: 10319 Maybelle St, beside the Wellton post office and town hall, one block off Los Angeles Ave.
properties.notes: A 10-unit park with a coffee shop. Its owner-claimed Dyrt listing offers RV and tent stays from $25. Neither The Dyrt nor Campendium lists showers or restrooms, so confirm before you count on them. Del Sol supermarket, Circle K, Family Dollar, Dollar General and Geronimo's are all within 0.5 mi. The only review is from 2019.

properties.name: Tier Drop RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. A tent camper paid $20 (Jan 2020). The operator lists RV daily at $40 (2026); a Campendium report says $37 (Feb 2026).
properties.reservations: Book through the park website or by phone. The posted (summer) office hours are Mon-Fri 8-4. A 2023 guest arrived at 8:30 PM and paid cash in an envelope at the office. The website was returning errors on Nov 2, 2026, so phone ahead.
properties.access: From Wellton's main street (Los Angeles Ave/William St) go south on William St across I-8 at exit 30, then 0.7 mi west on County 11th St (the south frontage road). Paved.
properties.notes: This is the most reliable tent spot between Dateland and Yuma. It advertises 'No Age Restrictions', which is rare here. Campendium lists 'Tent camping: Yes'. A repeat tent guest pitched 'in a more remote section, quiet and clean' (2020), and The Dyrt lists tents. AAA's directory says 'No tent. RVs only', so confirm by phone. Amenities: heated pool and spa, two laundries, restrooms and showers, clubhouse. Chevron and Jack in the Box are at exit 30; Del Sol supermarket is 1.5 mi.

properties.name: Welton Canal dispersed area (BLM / State Trust patchwork)
properties.price: Free on the BLM parcel. The State Trust parcel needs the $15/yr ASLD recreational permit.
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: From Wellton south on William St / S Avenue 29 E across I-8 (about 1.8 mi), then E County 13th St to the Wellton-Mohawk canal, about 2.7 mi from the line. Land is a checkerboard on the federal map: BLM (32.635,-114.140 and 32.637,-114.135), State Trust (32.640,-114.140) and Bureau of Reclamation canal land. Camp on the BLM piece, or carry an ASLD permit to be legal on the State Trust piece.
properties.notes: The Dyrt lists tents. A Jan 2026 review: 'Good group of people using the area. The trains do move through the valley at night. Could not hear the highway. Level and easy entry.' A Dec 2023 reviewer said it is State Trust land needing a permit but had never seen anyone check. Stock up in Wellton first.

properties.name: Brewery on an Organic Date Farm (Naked Date Farms / High Tanks Brewing, Hipcamp)
properties.price: $40/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (dry 'RV/Tent' sites under the palms; max 7 nights)
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp or request through The Dyrt. The Dyrt gives the camping season as Nov 1-Apr 30; the brewery and restaurant are open Nov-Apr, Thu-Sun 11-5.
properties.access: From Wellton exit 30: S Ave 29E, Colorado Ave, Canal Ave, E County 12th St, then E City 12 Rd west about 2.5 mi, S Avenue 25 E south about 1.5 mi, and Gila Ranch Rd. About 6.5 mi; the last leg is a well-kept dirt road ('a Corolla handles it'). Leaving west, rejoin I-8 at Dome Valley exit 21 (corridor mi 161.1) via Ave 25E north and paved old Hwy 80 west, about 8.3 mi. That loop adds only about 6 mi over riding I-8 straight through.
properties.notes: This is the best-reviewed camp on the segment: 149 Hipcamp reviews, 97% recommend, a 2024 'Best in Arizona' finalist. Sites are named 'RV/Tent Site 1-6 - Dry Camping', and car, rooftop-tent and van campers reviewed it through April 2026. A reviewer reports a 'decent restroom with showers'. You camp in shade among Medjool date palms, with date beer and food Thu-Sun and live music some weekends. One complaint is a generator. Wi-Fi at the brewery only.

properties.name: Camp'n Dirty (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $35/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (5 private RV/tent sites)
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Late arrival works: a Feb 2025 guest arrived 7-8 PM and the host flagged them in. It is very dark after sunset.
properties.access: Same farm roads as the date farm, about 1 mi further west via Gila Ranch Rd and S Avenue 24 E (sand and rock). About 7.5 mi from Wellton exit 30, or about 9.3 mi from Dome Valley exit 21 via old Hwy 80 and Ave 25E.
properties.notes: 40-acre off-grid desert property beside the Goldwater Range. Tent guests reviewed it in Nov 2025 and Jun 2024 (93% recommend, latest March 2026). No toilet or water. Eat and fill bottles at the date farm brewery, 1 mi east, on Thu-Sun.

properties.name: Liguerta (Ligurta) Station RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: I-8 exit 21 (Dome Valley / Ligurta), north side on paved E Highway 80 (old US 80).
properties.notes: It exists in OSM and in an unclaimed RoverPass listing (updated Jul 2025) that claims showers, laundry, a pool and a dump station, rated 2.0 from 4 reviews. It is not on Campendium, The Dyrt or Hipcamp. Phone before relying on it. The I-8 'Ligurta parking areas' at this exit are truck parking, not legal campsites.

properties.name: BLM land at Dome Valley / Ligurta exit 21
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: I-8 exit 21: about 0.5 mi west on paved E Highway 80 (old US 80) on the south side. The federal map shows BLM on both sides of the road west of the exit (32.662-32.670 N, 114.300-114.315 W), and an OSM track enters it at 32.6672,-114.3044. North of the exit, BLM also starts about 0.5 mi up Ave 20E / Dome Valley Rd.
properties.notes: I found no camper reports here; legality comes from the federal land-status map only. West of this exit I-8 climbs Telegraph Pass with no exit for about 7 mi. The unpaved alternative is the 'Route of Butterfield Stage' county road (OSM, surface unknown), about 11 mi NW to US 95 at the Yuma VFW BLM camp. There is no water between Wellton and the Fortuna Foothills, about 16 mi.

properties.name: Yuma VFW BLM dispersed area (Blaisdell, US 95)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None; first come. A camp host is sometimes listed but rarely present.
properties.access: From I-8 exit 12 (Fortuna Rd): north on paved S Fortuna Rd about 1.8 mi, then Old Ocean-to-Ocean Hwy, Rifle Range Rd and Ave 12E to US 95 (about 5.8 mi). Enter the VFW Post driveway (7120 US-95), go around the west side of the building and north onto the open flat. Map pins can be 0.5 mi off, so navigate to the VFW building. Coming from Dome Valley exit 21, the 'Route of Butterfield Stage' back road reaches it in about 15 mi without crossing Telegraph Pass. Expect loose 'sugar sand'.
properties.notes: Current and busy: an Oct 28, 2026 Dyrt review says 'Fine for a night. Maybe a dozen other campers.' Reviews mention tents. Downsides are UP freight trains and US 95 right alongside, jets, and dust in wind. A 2021 reviewer reported unsettling campers in the back brush, so camp near others. The federal map shows the land as Bureau of Reclamation; Campendium and The Dyrt list it as BLM Yuma FO dispersed camping. Do not use the nearby 'Gila Canal' spot (32.739,-114.430), where a sign reads 'State Property... No Camping'. Buy food and water in the Foothills first: Fry's, Circle K and Chevron at For

properties.name: Blue Sky RV Resort
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Full-hookup RV sites from $58/night (operator, 2026).
properties.reservations: Book online. A camp host is on site 24/7, so late arrival is plausible; call.
properties.access: South of I-8 exit 12 on the south frontage road.
properties.notes: Sources conflict. AAA's guide lists it with 'Tents, RVs' and AllStays lists tents but also '55+'. The operator's 2026 site only markets full-hookup RV sites, and Campendium says it is open to all ages. Worth one phone call because of the 24/7 host.

properties.name: Lazy K RV Park (Yuma)
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: North of I-8 near exit 9 via the north frontage road and S Ave 9E.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only park. A mobile-home directory lists 'Lazy K (all ages / pet friendly)' at this address, and The Dyrt's 'Lazy K RV Park' page is a Texas park. It may be long-term only.

properties.name: Sandbar RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Next to Yuma Lakes RV Resort in the North Gila Valley, about 8.5 mi from I-8 exit 7 via Araby Rd and Laguna Dam Rd.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only listing; I found no listing, reviews or website. Do not plan on it.

properties.name: Windhaven RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: A 2021 reviewer said three first-come, first-served one-night spots sit at the front. Otherwise call.
properties.access: I-8 exit 7 (Araby Rd), south about 0.5 mi to E 32nd St (Business 8 / old US 80), then 0.15 mi west.
properties.notes: It is not age-restricted, which is rare in Yuma ('one of the few in the area friendly to young people and families', 2021). The owner-claimed Dyrt listing, updated Dec 2025, lists 'Tent Sites' along with showers and restrooms, and one AAA record mentions tent-only sites. Another AAA record and AllStays say 'RVs only, no tent'. Call; this is the closest possible tent spot to central Yuma's I-8 exits.

properties.name: Rocking K RV Park
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Back-in RV lot $50 + tax/day incl. electric; pull-through $55 + tax (2026 rate page).
properties.reservations: Call or use the site's booking form ($100 deposit for longer stays). Campendium's description says '3-day minimum stay Oct.-April'; the current rate page does not mention it, so ask.
properties.access: I-8 exit 7 (Araby Rd), south about 0.5 mi to E 32nd St, then about 0.65 mi west (paved, busy arterial).
properties.notes: The operator's facilities page lists 'Tent Camping Sites', 'Clean bathrooms & Free showers', laundry, clubhouse Wi-Fi and 24-hour on-call maintenance; Campendium also lists tents. A Jan 2024 reviewer found it overpriced. The possible 3-night minimum is the catch for a one-night rider. It may now include the closed Yuma Mesa RV Park next door; Good Sam lists 'Rocking K Grande' at that ID.

properties.name: Lost Traveler RV Park (formerly Southern Mesa)
properties.price: Tent rate not published. Back-in RV sites $45/night + tax.
properties.reservations: Check-in must be before dark; check-out 11 AM; one-night cancellation fee.
properties.access: I-8 exit 3 (Ave 3E), about 9 mi south on Ave 3E toward Somerton/San Luis; flat farm road.
properties.notes: It markets itself as the 'Best Family-Friendly Park in Yuma' (not 55+), with free showers, laundry and a pool. The Dyrt tags it 'RVs, Tents', but the park's own pages mention only RV sites. It is 9 mi off route, so only worth a call if the Yuma options fail.

properties.name: Avenue B RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: West on 16th St from 4th Ave about 1.8 mi.
properties.notes: One directory calls it a 'boutique' 55+ community, so treat it as no tents.

properties.name: Lazy 8 RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: W 8th St, 1.8 mi west of 4th Ave.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only park with no web presence found. It is probably long-term.

properties.name: Sherwood Forest RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: W 3rd St west to Ave B, then W 5th St.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only park; the Campendium and Dyrt pages under this name are for other states.

properties.name: Unnamed RV park at 345 S May Ave (OSM 'Unnamed campground')
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: W 5th St / S May Ave, west Yuma.
properties.notes: Reverse geocodes to 345 S May Ave, next to Desert Breeze RV Park; it may be part of it. Nothing online.

properties.name: Desert Breeze RV Park (386 S May Ave)
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: W 5th St / S May Ave, west Yuma.
properties.notes: Not the Army's 'Desert Breeze Travel Camp' at Yuma Proving Ground, which is military-ID only; Campendium mixes the two up. No independent listing was found.

properties.name: A Shady Tree RV Park
properties.price: unknown (no rates published)
properties.reservations: unknown: no published contact; you would have to walk in during the day
properties.access: W 3rd St, 0.6 mi west of 4th Ave.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only park; one directory shows a single Google review. Its tent policy is unknown.

properties.name: Blew In RV Park
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: W 3rd St, 0.6 mi west of 4th Ave (next to A Shady Tree).
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only park with no listings found.

properties.name: Yuma River Front KOA Journey (former Riverfront RV Park)
properties.price: About $40/night plus fees for a tent site (Oct 2026 tent review). Tent sites have no hookups, sand, a table and fire ring, one tent per site.
properties.reservations: Reserve on koa.com or call; KOA advertises a well-lit after-hours check-in. Open year-round.
properties.access: From 4th Ave near the Colorado River (corridor mi about 185), west on 1st St, or the paved Colorado River levee path, to W Water St, about 2.3 mi. It sits beside the Yuma East/West Wetlands and their riverside trails, about 1.5 mi west of the 4th Ave (Business 8) bridge into Winterhaven.
properties.notes: The surest tent bed in Yuma. It converted to a KOA Journey in Dec 2025 (new owners, new bathhouses, pool and spa); a Jan 2026 reviewer called the bathrooms 'new and immaculate'. An Oct 2026 tent camper felt $40+ was poor value and could only see the canal, not the river; another 2026 tent review called it great. A Dec 2025 reviewer reported a dispute over a dog pen. Grocery: Walmart Neighborhood Market and Food City on W 8th St, about 1.5 mi.

properties.name: McCoy Mobile Home / RV Park
properties.price: No tent rate. Jan 2025: $30 for an electric-only spot behind the office with no bathroom access, showers $8 extra. Full hookups about $400/month (2022). Passport America rates for up to 3 nights.
properties.reservations: The manager shows you the open sites; call ahead.
properties.access: Winterhaven, via 2nd Ave, G St and 1st Ave.
properties.notes: This is an OSM-only mobile-home and RV park on Quechan land with no listings, probably long-term only.

properties.name: Sleepy Hollow RV Park (Quechan Tribe)
properties.price: No tent product. On Campspot, a primitive no-hookup RV site starts at $35/night and full hookups at $50.
properties.reservations: Book on Campspot or walk in. Office hours are Mon–Sat 8–7 per the tribe page (reviews say Mon–Fri 8–5). Late arrivals: 24-hour security tells you to pick a spot and pay in the morning (Mar 2025 and Jan 2026 reviews).
properties.access: Paved, flat: from I-8 exit 166 ride about 1.6 mi south on Algodones Rd toward the Los Algodones border crossing.
properties.notes: Campspot lists 0 tent sites, so ask whether a tent can use a primitive site. It has showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, and a store (Mon–Sat 7am–6pm) with groceries, water and burritos, which is the last real store before Holtville apart from the Felicity Chevron. Border traffic on Algodones Rd is heavy on Fri and Sat evenings. OSM's unnamed polygon way 1448344108 (baseline mile 191.2) is this park.

properties.name: Encore Pilot Knob RV Resort
properties.price: Tent rate not published. RV $53/night (Feb 2026). A Feb 2026 guest learned that non-guests can dump, fill water and shower for $20.
properties.phone: (928) 750-3775 (resort office per operator listing); also (760) 572-0875; Thousand Trails reservations (877) 570-2267
properties.reservations: Online or by phone through Thousand Trails/Encore; check-in noon. After-hours arrivals call (877) 864-2728. The office has closed around 4 pm in past reports.
properties.access: Paved, flat: leave Center of the World Dr at Sidewinder Rd (exit 164), go under I-8 to the south frontage (old Hwy 80), then about 0.6 mi west.
properties.notes: The operator's own listing says 'We also have tent sites with electricity and water', and The Dyrt lists tent sites. AAA and AllStays still say no tents, so confirm when you call. This is the best full-service stop in the first 40 miles: hot showers, laundry, pool and spa. I-8 and night-train noise are loud. The Chevron mini-mart is at the exit.

properties.name: Pilot Knob 14-Day Camping Area (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: No reservations; first come, first served.
properties.access: About 0.4 mi of pavement, then 1.2–1.6 mi of gravel with soft sand patches, flat. South on Sidewinder Rd past the Chevron, then turn right (west) on the dirt road just before the LTVA at the BLM '14 day camping' sign. A Jan 2026 report says the entrance is blocked by a dirt berm and a bush, so walk the bike around on the side track. It turns to mud after rain.
properties.notes: A signed BLM 14-day area, and the land status checks out as BLM. Open, flat desert pavement with Border Patrol traffic and noise from I-8 and the trains, about 400 yd away. It is windy. Buy water at the Chevron at the exit. Stay outside the paid LTVA.

properties.name: Sidewinder Road BLM (north of I-8, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: No reservations; first come, first served.
properties.access: Gravel/dirt, flat with a gentle rise: north on Sidewinder Rd about 2–2.5 mi. The first mile or so north of I-8 is private land and inside the LTVA's 1-mile buffer (the land layer shows private ownership at 32.7535), so keep going until you are clearly on open BLM desert. A '4x4 recommended' sign further in; ground is packed desert pavement.
properties.notes: Land at the listed point is verified BLM, and reviews run from 2018 to 2024. Quieter than the south side, though trains run nearby. One 2021 camper preferred it because of migrant traffic south of I-8. No services.

properties.name: American Girl Mine Rd / Sidewinder Rd NW BLM (Ogilby Rd, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: No reservations.
properties.access: Paved Ogilby Rd north about 5 mi with a gentle climb. Just past the railroad tracks turn right onto Sidewinder Rd (NW) or American Girl Mine Rd, both hard-packed gravel. The ISDRA vehicle-fee zone runs along Ogilby Rd south of the tracks.
properties.notes: A large, popular snowbird boondocking area. The land is verified BLM and a Feb 2026 review is positive. The mine waters the main road for dust, and it can be very windy when Yuma is calm. Gold Rock Ranch (showers) is about 4 mi further north. It costs about 10.5 mi round trip off the route, so use it only if the Pilot Knob areas will not do.
properties.sources: ["freecampsites.net listing #5668 (American Girl Mine)","freecampsites.net listing #8074 (Sidewinder Road northwest side)","https://gis.blm.gov/arcgis/rest/services/lands/BLM_Natl_SMA_LimitedScale/MapServer"]

properties.name: Gold Rock Ranch RV Park
properties.price: unknown. RV $45 (Dec 2022), Passport America $22.50. In 2020 a non-guest shower was $10 and a dump $15.
properties.website: unknown (goldrockranch.us no longer resolves as of Nov 2026)
properties.reservations: unknown
properties.access: Paved Ogilby Rd (CR S34) north about 9 mi, then about 1 mi west on dirt Gold Rock Ranch Rd. That is roughly 20 mi round trip off the route.
properties.notes: AAA lists it as RVs only with no tents; MapQuest and The Dyrt list tent sites. The newest reviews are from 2022 and the website is dead, so call before committing to a 20-mile round trip. Mainly useful as a place to shower and do laundry.

properties.name: Buttercup Campground (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
properties.price: Free for a cyclist going by the rule's wording: the ISDRA permit ($55 weekly online, $70 on site, $185 season, Oct 1 to Apr 15) applies to 'primary street legal vehicles used for transportation to the recreation site'. Confirm with the ranger.
properties.phone: Buttercup Ranger Station (760) 572-2220 (2020 brochure); BLM El Centro (760) 337-4400
properties.reservations: First come, first served, 14-day limit. The ranger station is staffed Fri–Sun in season.
properties.access: Paved and flat: leave I-8 at exit 156 (Grays Well Rd) and go east past the Buttercup Ranger Station. Off the pavement it is soft sand.
properties.notes: An OHV staging and camping area with vault toilets and dumpsters, and the land is BLM. Engines and generators run on weekends (Nov 7–8); weekdays are quiet. BLM rules allow small tent stakes. Caltrans lists the Sand Hills Rest Area on I-8, about 0.3 mi west, with drinking water and toilets. The border fence is close and Border Patrol is active. BLM's only current ISDRA closure (Cement Flats, from Sept 8, 2026) is in the north dunes on Hwy 78, not here.

properties.name: Midway Campground (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
properties.price: Free for a cyclist (the ISDRA permit is per street-legal primary vehicle); confirm at Buttercup Ranger Station.
properties.reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
properties.access: Exit 156, then about 2.4 mi southwest on Grays Well Rd (paved BLM road, flat), then a short gravel spur.
properties.notes: Campendium marks tent camping 'Yes'. A camping strip parallel to I-8 facing the dunes, the border fence and Mexico, with vault toilets and dumpsters. Traffic noise is moderate.

properties.name: Grays Well / Plank Road camping area (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
properties.price: Free for a cyclist (permit is per street-legal primary vehicle); confirm with BLM.
properties.reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
properties.access: Exit 156, then about 3.4 mi on paved Grays Well Rd, flat. The pavement ends here. Going west to Gordons Well Rd / Evan Hewes means about 1.5 mi of compacted and sandy BLM track; otherwise ride back to exit 156.
properties.notes: Paved access road, toilets, and the Old Plank Road display. The land is BLM. A dead end for road bikes.

properties.name: Dune Buggy Flats (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
properties.price: Free for a cyclist (ISDRA permit is per street-legal primary vehicle).
properties.reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
properties.access: From exit 151 (Gordons Well Rd), about 1.2 mi east on compacted and sandy BLM tracks (BLM 386/468), flat. Alternatively about 4.3 mi from exit 156 on mostly paved Grays Well Rd.
properties.notes: Gravel camping area with vault toilets and dumpsters (BLM brochure); the land is BLM. It is the last ISDRA camp before the route leaves I-8. Gordon's Well RV Park and its weekend diner are 1.5 mi west.

properties.name: Gordon's Well RV Park & Storage
properties.price: Not published. The park has 99 full-hookup RV sites, mostly seasonal dune-trip rentals.
properties.reservations: Reservations taken by phone or email (office@gordonswellrvparkandstorage.com). Season Oct 1 to May 31.
properties.access: On the route: paved East Evan Hewes Hwy just west of I-8 exit 151, flat.
properties.notes: The only RV park in the dunes, under new owners since 2020 and remodeled, with men's and women's restrooms with showers and a coin laundry. Duner's Diner restaurant and bar next door is open weekends only. No tent policy is published, so call. Even if they refuse a tent, ask to buy a shower and water: after this it is about 26 mi with no services to Holtville.

properties.name: East Mesa BLM dispersed (along East Evan Hewes Hwy)
properties.price: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Paved Evan Hewes Hwy, flat. Turn off onto any existing dirt route and camp within about 300 ft of it, out of sight of the road. Soft sugar sand lies off the packed tracks.
properties.notes: This is a map-verified fallback, not a reviewed site: the BLM land layer shows BLM on both sides of the road from about mile 216 to 224. To stay legal, keep more than 1 mile outside the Tamarisk LTVA (Hwy 98 side, about miles 214–217.5) and the Hot Spring LTVA (about miles 223.5–226.5), where camping is banned. Near miles 209–217 the strip south of the road is Bureau of Reclamation canal land; do not camp there.

properties.name: BLM 14-day area south of Holtville Hot Springs (free)
properties.price: Free (14 days in any 28)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: At the hot spring turn south on Holdridge Rd: about 0.3 mi paved, then compacted gravel with sandy spots, about 1.8 mi in all, flat. Camp past the big power lines and the BLM '14 day' signs, about 2 mi south of I-8. Sugar sand lies off the packed tracks.
properties.notes: A legal free BLM area with signs, confirmed in reviews from 2014 to 2025; the land is verified BLM. Reviewers say it is quiet with good AT&T and T-Mobile coverage. A 2021 report mentions theft and a brush fire. Carry water: the nearest is Holtville, about 7 mi. The hot spring rinse shower is 1.8 mi back if it is running.

properties.name: Los Cerritos Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $35/night base (about $41.22 with Hipcamp fees) for one RV or tent site, 2 guests max, 1 vehicle.
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp, up to 12 months ahead, 1-night minimum, flexible cancellation. Check-in after 7 AM and you meet the host on arrival, so message ahead if you will arrive in the evening.
properties.access: Paved roads, then a 2WD gravel pad. The host says it is about 1 minute out of Holtville near the Alamo River; flat.
properties.notes: Star Host Gerardo, 97% recommend (19 ratings), with stays from Dec 2025 to May 2026, including a tent camper in May 2026. Quiet farm with animals and mesquite shade. The listing says no toilets, showers or potable water, but a Jan 2025 guest found porta-potties. Fill water in Holtville. There is only one site, so book as soon as the day is set.

properties.name: NAF El Centro RV park (military only)
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: Military/DoD ID holders only.
properties.access: On the base, behind a security gate.
properties.notes: This is the baseline's OSM 'Unnamed campground' at 32.8167,-115.6800 (mile 250.9): the community-recreation RV park on Naval Air Facility El Centro. RV LIFE flags it 'Military Only'. Not open to Nick unless he holds military or DoD ID.

properties.name: Superstition Mountain OHV area, 'The Dip' / Wheeler Rd (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: North on Huff Rd from Evan Hewes about 7.5 mi (surface not verified), flat. The Wheeler Rd OHV staging is about 2.5 mi further west on dirt.
properties.notes: A large BLM OHV open area with free dispersed camping. It is very busy and dusty on weekends from Oct to Apr and quiet on weekdays. Worth it only as a detour; Plaster City OHV, 6 mi further on and right beside the route, is easier.
properties.sources: ["freecampsites.net listing #34243 (Superstition Mtn - The Dip Area)","freecampsites.net listing #50725 (Superstition Mt - Wheeler Rd OHV)","https://thedyrt.com/camping/california/supersitition-mountain"]

properties.name: Plaster City OHV Area staging (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: Pull off paved S80 onto the dirt staging area north of the road (railroad tracks run alongside). Flat.
properties.notes: The BLM Plaster City OHV open area (OSM relation 15006797) borders the route from about mile 256.5 to 267, and the land is verified BLM on both sides here. OHV groups make it busy on weekends, and trains pass. No water: the last is Seeley (mile 251.7) and the next is Ocotillo (mile 270–273).

properties.name: Plaster City East OHV (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: About 1.7 mi north of S80 on dirt OHV routes near the USG plant; sand is possible.
properties.notes: A second staging point in the same BLM open area, farther from the road and trains. The land is verified BLM. There are no recent reviews.

properties.name: Plaster City West / Painted Gorge Rd (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: At the Painted Gorge Rd junction with S80: camp on BLM land just off the pavement, or go up compacted Painted Gorge Rd toward the Coyote Mountains. The wilderness boundary is far up the road, and bikes are not allowed inside it. Flat.
properties.notes: The closest documented free camping to Ocotillo. The land is verified BLM on both sides of S80 here. Ocotillo's Chevron and market are 4–6 mi on.

properties.name: Ocotillo Trailer Park & Motel
properties.price: unknown
properties.reservations: unknown (the website is an old Flash site with no content)
properties.access: Paved town streets, flat, next to the Ocotillo community center.
properties.notes: The only private lodging business in Ocotillo (motel plus trailer park). It is unknown whether it rents overnight RV or tent spaces; the motel rooms count as a hotel, which you don't want. Red Feather Market & Cafe and the post office are next door.

properties.name: BLM dispersed land north of Ocotillo (Shell Canyon Rd / S2)
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed; 14 days in any 28-day period; campfire permit required)
properties.reservations: None. First come, no check-in, arrive any hour.
properties.access: Paved. From Ocotillo (I-8 exit 89, Imperial Hwy/S2) ride north on Shell Canyon Rd. Public BLM land starts about 1.6-1.8 mi north of I-8, and the road stays paved to about 3.2 mi before turning to dirt. Alternative: BLM land along S2 2-4 mi northwest of town. Flat desert floor.
properties.notes: Free legal fallback at the foot of the In-Ko-Pah grade. Sleeping here lets you start the 2,700-ft climb fresh in the morning instead of fighting afternoon wind. Pitch within 300 ft of the road, or within 50 ft once you are inside the Ocotillo ACEC, which begins about 2.5 mi north. Stay off wind-farm service roads and out of the way of quarry trucks. Do NOT camp south of I-8 along SR-98: the Yuha Basin ACEC allows camping only at designated sites. There is no water, so fill up at the Ocotillo Chevron/Food Mart at exit 89. Expect heavy Border Patrol traffic and November lows in the 40s.

properties.name: BLM dispersed south of Ocotillo (BLM route 321 off Hwy 98)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: From the I-8/S2 interchange go south on S2 / Hwy 98 about 0.5 mi, then onto compacted dirt BLM route 321, about 1 mi south. BLM land starts about 0.6 mi south of town. Flat.
properties.notes: Map-verified only (BLM land at 32.714–32.720N), with no user reports. It is near the border, so expect Border Patrol traffic and lights.

properties.name: Jacumba Mountains Wilderness edge, Davies Valley access (BLM, free)
properties.price: Free (14-day limit)
properties.reservations: None.
properties.access: South from Ocotillo on S2 to Hwy 98, east 0.7 mi to the BLM sign, then a bumpy, sandy dirt road to the wilderness boundary. Bikes are prohibited inside the wilderness, so camp outside the boundary.
properties.notes: Remote and next to the border; a 2018 camper left after Border Patrol searchlights. The BLM route 321 spot above is closer and easier.

properties.name: Smuggler's Gulch Dispersed (BLM, I-8 exit 80 Mountain Springs Rd)
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed)
properties.reservations: None. First come, any hour.
properties.access: Halfway up the grade. Leave westbound I-8 at exit 80 (Mountain Springs Rd) onto the old concrete Hwy 80 remnant and dirt spurs. One rough patch needs vehicle clearance, so walk the bike there.
properties.notes: Bail-out spot for when the wind beats you on the In-Ko-Pah climb. The BLM land-status layer puts it on BLM land inside the Ocotillo ACEC, so camp within 50 ft of the route. It is a recreational shooting area: broken glass, rusty metal and shell casings everywhere, so watch your tires. Freeway noise. No water, so carry it from Ocotillo.

properties.name: The Desert View Tower (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $45/night per site (Hipcamp all-in price; tent-only; up to 14 people)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant). Arrival is strictly before dark: before 4 pm in winter months. The host will not accept after-dark arrivals.
properties.access: Take I-8 exit 77 (In-Ko-Pah Park Rd) and ride about 1 mi north on paved In-Ko-Pah Park Rd to the tower. The sites are walk-in among the boulders with no vehicle access, so push the bike the last stretch.
properties.notes: Top of the In-Ko-Pah grade at about 3,000 ft, camping among the boulders beside the historic 1920s tower. Flush toilets and water at the sites, no showers. The host warns the winds can be 'ferocious' and asks you to check the Boulder Park, CA forecast. Book a day ahead and plan to arrive by 4 pm; if the grade runs late, use Smuggler's Gulch or Elliot Mine instead. Active listing with 98% of 164 reviews positive; latest reviews April 2026.

properties.name: In-Ko-Pah Spirit Retreat (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $40/night (Hipcamp; 4 RV/tent sites plus 1 container cabin)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant). Check in before 5 pm in winter months, 7 pm in summer.
properties.access: From In-Ko-Pah Park Rd / Old Hwy 80 near I-8 exit 77, 1.6 mi of bumpy, rutted dirt road. The host says it turns to clay mud when wet, so avoid it after rain. Sites 2-3 are a 0.13-mi pack-in on a rough trail.
properties.notes: Off-grid 10-acre retreat running on solar, wind and well water. The host lists flush toilets, showers and a kitchen at the Home Base site. No pets. Rattlesnake and cholla country. No trash service, so pack everything out. Latest reviews September 2026.

properties.name: Elliot Mine area BLM dispersed (Old Hwy 80 spur south of I-8 exit 77)
properties.price: Free (BLM dispersed)
properties.reservations: None. First come, any hour.
properties.access: The dirt entrance is off the old Hwy 80 spur just south of I-8 exit 77 (32.6398, -116.1070). The camp spurs beyond are very rough and rocky (4WD, high clearance), so expect to push the bike.
properties.notes: The BLM land-status layer confirms BLM land at the entrance and at the Dyrt 'Elliot Mine' point (32.6254, -116.0819). The app's OSM pin at 32.6258, -116.0963 falls on private/undetermined land, so do not camp there. The site sits beside the border wall with constant Border Patrol trucks and searchlights. No facilities and no water: fill up at Ocotillo or plan on Jacumba. The adjacent Jacumba Wilderness is closed to bikes.

properties.name: DeAnza Springs Resort
properties.price: Tent/dry sites from about $39/night on Hipcamp (all-in). Direct booking on Campspot. Campendium users report $73-76 for RV sites.
properties.reservations: Book via Campspot (campspot.com/book/deanzaspringsresort) or Hipcamp (instant book), or call. One Hipcamp reviewer says check-in must be before 4 pm; call if you will be late.
properties.access: From Old Hwy 80 in Jacumba, take Carrizo Gorge Rd north. The first 1.1 mi is paved and passes the I-8 exit 73 Shell/Chevron. Then about 1.75 mi of graded dirt to the resort; dusty but fine on a touring bike when dry.
properties.notes: Best amenities on this stretch: showers, two pools (one indoor and heated), hot tub, café/bar, Wi-Fi and laundry. It is still a clothing-optional resort: its own 2026 FAQ says so, and Hipcamp campers report the pool and jacuzzi are nude-only. Otherwise family-friendly and pet-friendly. The Goat Canyon Trestle trail starts here. Elevation about 2,800 ft, so expect cold November nights. Recent reviews (Feb and Jul 2026) are positive.

properties.name: BS Ranch, Home of the Big Spots (Hipcamp, Jewel Valley)
properties.price: $50/night (Hipcamp); 25 dispersed RV/tent spots on 78 acres
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book
properties.access: Jewel Valley, south of Old Hwy 80 between Jacumba and Boulevard. About 3.5 mi via Jewel Valley Rd, partly unpaved/compacted. Exact address on booking; the listing coordinates are approximate.
properties.notes: Backup only: just 5 reviews, the latest from September 2025. No campfires; pets OK.

properties.name: Sagewinds Farm High Desert Camp (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $40.50/night (Hipcamp all-in)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book
properties.access: Just off Old Hwy 80 about 3.5 mi west of Jacumba toward Boulevard. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate); the final approach is probably dirt.
properties.notes: Certified-organic white-sage farm at 3,500-3,800 ft with boulders and caves. Two flush toilets and potable water, no showers, no campfires. 98% of 300-plus reviews recommend it; latest reviews September 2026. Expect cold nights.

properties.name: Lark Canyon Campground (BLM, McCain Valley; lower & upper loops)
properties.price: $6/site/night BLM fee (fee tube reported missing at times); 15 sites plus group sites
properties.reservations: First come, no reservations
properties.access: From Old Hwy 80 about 2 mi east of Boulevard, go north on McCain Valley Rd: 2.4 mi paved, then graded gravel. The lower loop is about 4 mi in; the upper loop (32.7278, -116.2736) is about 5.5 mi.
properties.notes: Designated BLM campground in the McCain Valley RCA. BLM's 2020 map lists upper and lower Lark Canyon with non-potable water, fire rings, trash and vault toilets. It is an OHV motorcycle area with wind turbines nearby and a migrant route with Border Patrol traffic. Carry all drinking water from Boulevard (Mountain Top Market, mile 300). Recent reviews are scarce and BLM's web page for it now returns 404, so call the El Centro office to confirm it is operating.

properties.name: Boulevard / Cleveland National Forest KOA Holiday
properties.price: Tent sites roughly $45-55/night (third-party reports: Dyrt low $45, Roadtrippers $53). The KOA site blocks automated price checks, so call.
properties.reservations: Reserve online or by phone (reservations line 800-562-0271). After-hours arrivals use night registration: pick a site and settle up in the morning.
properties.access: Paved. From Old Hwy 80 at Ribbonwood Rd (Boulevard), follow Hwy 94 about 3.4 mi, then turn right on Shasta Way for 0.7 mi; the entrance is on the left where the pavement ends. From the Golden Acorn / Crestwood exit it is about 6.6 mi via Church Rd (BIA 10), which is partly unpaved.
properties.notes: Open year-round; an October 2026 reviewer found it quiet with no freeway noise. KOA describes tent pads with water and electric; there is also a store, laundry and showers. Elevation about 4,000 ft, so plan on freezing nights. 2026 reviews are mixed: dusty dirt tent pads in wind, and one scathing review of the owner. The app's old pin (32.677, -116.313, 0.5 mi off) is wrong: the KOA is 4.2 road miles south of the line.

properties.name: Cibbets Flat Campground (Cleveland NF)
properties.price: $20/night single site, $40 double (USFS fee schedule)
properties.reservations: First come, first served
properties.access: From Old Hwy 80 at Kitchen Creek Rd (by I-8 exit 54), about 5 mi north on paved Kitchen Creek Rd with a steady climb all the way.
properties.notes: USFS lists the site as 'Site Open', with 24 sites, potable water and vault toilets. Quiet oak and creek setting away from the freeway. Cleveland NF elevated fire restrictions are in effect, so use only established fire rings if fires are allowed at all; a stove is safer. No services: carry food from Boulevard or the Golden Acorn travel center.

properties.name: Boulder Oaks Campground (Cleveland NF)
properties.price: $5/night walk-in tent site; $20 single, $40 double (USFS fee schedule)
properties.reservations: Family and walk-in sites are first come. Only the equestrian loop is on Recreation.gov, and it showed 'Not Reservable' for Nov 2-9.
properties.access: Directly on Old Hwy 80, about 2 mi east of the Buckman Springs Rd / I-8 exit 51 junction. Paved.
properties.notes: Best value right on the line: a $5 walk-in site with potable water and vault toilets, and the PCT at the gate. Oak and boulder setting, but you will hear I-8 traffic. A camp host was on site in January 2026. No showers.

properties.name: Lake Morena County Park
properties.price: About $24-29 per tent or standard site (Dyrt and reviewer reports; partial-hookup sites with outlets about $29-34), plus an $8 reservation fee. Confirm on the county site.
properties.reservations: County online system (parksres.sandiegocounty.gov), bookable from today with a 1-night minimum, or call 858-565-3600. Camping hours are 24/7. The site grid checked Nov 2 showed about 88-93 of 97 units free Nov 2-5 and Nov 8-9, and about half booked Fri-Sat Nov 6-7.
properties.access: Paved. At Buckman Springs Rd (I-8 exit 51) go south 5.3 mi on Buckman Springs Rd, right on Oak Dr for 1.6 mi, then 0.5 mi on Lake Morena Dr. The app's 3.5-mi figure is straight-line distance; it is 7.5 mi by road, and you climb back out the next morning.
properties.notes: Full facilities: flush toilets, coin showers ($0.50 per 4 min, quarters from the ranger station), tent-only sites, and partial-hookup sites with 110 V outlets if you need to charge. Oak Shores Store is about 0.25 mi away (burgers, groceries, the only Wi-Fi in town). No 2026 closures listed for the campground. Elevation 3,000 ft, frost possible.

properties.name: Bobcat Meadow Campground (Cleveland NF, Corral Canyon OHV Area)
properties.price: $15/night single site (card only, no cash)
properties.reservations: Recreation.gov. All 18 sites were available Nov 2-6 when checked (4 reserved for Nov 7).
properties.access: From Buckman Springs Rd, take Morena Stokes Valley Rd / Corral Canyon Rd about 5.8 mi to Four Corners, then Los Pinos Rd about 1 mi. A May 2026 camper describes about 7 mi of rough off-road driving. Hard on a loaded touring bike, with heavy climbing.
properties.notes: Last resort only: no water, a rough dirt approach, and OHV traffic that peaks in the October-April red-sticker season. It was open and clean per Jan and May 2026 reviews.

properties.name: Kitchen Creek Road dispersed sites (Cleveland NF, free permit required)
properties.price: Free, but you need a free Descanso Ranger District dispersed-camping (visitor) permit
properties.reservations: Request the permit by email (SM.FS.DescansoRD@usda.gov) or phone (Mon-Fri 8:30-3:30, closed 11:30-12:30) a few business days ahead. No campfires; limit of 14 days per calendar year (Forest Order 02-26-11).
properties.access: From I-8 exit 47 (Sunrise Hwy at Laguna Junction), climb Sunrise Hwy about 6.5-7 mi, then ride about 1 mi down paved Kitchen Creek Rd past the 'Leaving Mt. Laguna Recreation Area' sign. Pullout sites on both sides. A big climb, and forest road gates can close as fire danger changes.
properties.notes: The only legal free dispersed option near Pine Valley; dispersed camping is banned inside the Laguna Mountain Recreation Area. High elevation, so expect a freezing night. A February 2026 report says the gate was open; another report mentions a closure gate about 3 mi along. Usually a poor trade against Boulder Oaks or Lake Morena.

properties.name: Thousand Trails Oakzanita Springs
properties.price: Unknown: dynamic online pricing. RV sites were reported at about $85 in March 2025; tent sites are listed separately.
properties.reservations: 'No Membership Needed to Book': the public can book online, tent sites included. Online check-in available. Campsite check-in from noon. Ranger station hours Nov 1-Apr 1 are 9 am-6 pm.
properties.access: About 3 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso: paved, narrow and curvy with little shoulder, uphill to about 3,800 ft.
properties.notes: Open year-round, though pools and activities shut down in winter. Reviewers mention warm, clean bathrooms and Wi-Fi in the lodge. Steep, narrow internal roads (fine on a bike). Trails lead straight into Cuyamaca Rancho SP. Camp store has basics only.

properties.name: Green Valley Campground (Cuyamaca Rancho State Park)
properties.price: $40/site/night (+$10 per extra vehicle); no hike/bike rate
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia through Nov 30; the park showed open dates Nov 5-17 when checked. Walk up if a site is vacant.
properties.access: About 4.5 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso: paved, narrow, climbing to about 4,000 ft.
properties.notes: Creekside oak campground with flush toilets and pay showers. Elevation about 4,000 ft, so nights near or below freezing. Bikes are limited to pavement and approved trails. Food: Descanso stores (mile 328.9).

properties.name: Paso Picacho Campground (Cuyamaca Rancho State Park)
properties.price: $40/site/night
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia through Nov 30; first come Dec 1-Mar 31
properties.access: About 9.6 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso, climbing roughly 1,600 ft to about 5,000 ft. Paved, narrow.
properties.notes: Only if Green Valley is full. Nearly 10 mi off the line and about 1,600 ft up, making it the coldest site on the segment. Flush toilets and pay showers.

properties.name: Stallion Oaks Ranch (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $35/night (Hipcamp)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp instant book. Within the tent areas (Barn Yard, Lake Basin) sites are first come.
properties.access: Rural roads north of Descanso. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate); the last stretch is probably dirt.
properties.notes: 240-acre Unity Center retreat with a bathhouse (six flush toilets, six showers). Hipcamp marks the water as not potable, so bring drinking water from Descanso (Perkins Store, mile 328.9). Fires only in the communal ring when the fire marshal approves. Limited cell service. Latest reviews September 2026.

properties.name: King Creek Campground (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $25/night (Hipcamp)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant)
properties.access: Rural dirt roads northwest of Descanso. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate). The host says some sites need 4WD and are not for small cars.
properties.notes: Former 1950s Boy Scout camp on 140 acres of oak meadow. Pit toilets; the host delivers well water to your site on request. No pets. Very secluded. Latest reviews September 2026.

properties.name: Ma-Tar-Awa RV Park (Viejas)
properties.price: Unknown. Reports: $25 (April 2024 camper who 'boondocked' in the meadow) and $35 (2019 RV).
properties.reservations: Call ahead. The park's own domain (matarawarvpark.com) did not resolve on Nov 2, 2026.
properties.access: Paved roads off Willows Rd / Browns Rd near Viejas Casino.
properties.notes: On the Viejas reservation near the casino, mostly occupied by long-term residents per reviews. Tent policy is unconfirmed, so call before counting on it. Viejas Casino itself only allows RV parking in its lot (no tents).

properties.name: San Diego Canyon Creek (Hipcamp)
properties.price: $45/night (Hipcamp)
properties.reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book. The host asks you to arrive in daylight if at all possible.
properties.access: South of I-8 between Alpine and El Cajon, in the Harbison Canyon area. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate). Shallow creek crossing at the entrance.
properties.notes: Small creekside property with 3 tent sites and a cabin. Shared outdoor kitchen; the bathroom and shower are in the house, with one water heater, so keep showers short. No campfires. 95% of 358 reviews recommend it; latest reviews October 2026.

properties.name: Lake Jennings Campground (Helix Water District)
properties.price: $45 Sun-Thu / $50 Fri-Sat for a no-hookup tent site (lake view $53/$58), plus an $8 processing fee. Partial-hookup sites with power start at $58 Sun-Thu.
properties.reservations: Online at reserve.lakejennings.org. The office and reservations line are open daily 8 am-5 pm, so book ahead if you will arrive after 5.
properties.access: From Old Hwy 80 at Lake Jennings Park Rd (I-8 exit 23), climb about 2 mi north to the campground kiosk on Bass Rd. Paved, steep in places.
properties.notes: Open year-round with 44 non-hookup tent sites. Hot showers open 24 hours, free Wi-Fi, lake and city views. Low elevation, so mild nights. The old app record showing $10 is wrong.

properties.name: Rancho Los Coches RV Park
properties.price: $25-40/night tent site (+$5 per extra person over age 3)
properties.reservations: Only 2 tent sites, and tent reservations are by phone only (not online). Check-in after 1 pm. Tent stays are limited to 3 nights.
properties.access: On Old Hwy 80 (Hwy 8 Business) by Los Coches Rd. Flat and paved.
properties.notes: The closest tent site to the line in the Lakeside/El Cajon area. Pool, hot tub, laundry, and clean bathrooms per reviews; free Wi-Fi at the pool/spa. This is the app's OSM 'Unnamed campground' at 32.8375, -116.9021. Call early because there are only two tent sites.

properties.name: Santee Lakes Recreation Preserve campground
properties.price: 2026 standard sites $62–$97/night (priced by demand) + 10% City of Santee TOT. Tents go only on the 15 designated tent sites (1 tent, max 6 people). Reservations have a 2-night minimum.
properties.reservations: Reserve online or by phone and say you are a tent camper; the park says it is near capacity year-round. FAQ: you can stay without a reservation 'subject to site availability'. Check-in 1 pm. After-hours check-in until about 9:30–10 pm (press the gate call button). Park office at Lake 5, 8 am–5 pm. Cancelling within 48 h gets no refund.
properties.access: Paved, about 6.9 bike miles north of El Cajon (Magnolia Ave/Cuyamaca St → Mission Gorge Rd → Fanita Pkwy). Gentle grade, no big climb. The baseline's OSM 'Unnamed campground' (osm-way-130000939, tagged caravan_site) is this campground.
properties.notes: Best full-service stop near El Cajon on weeknights: showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, store. Expensive for one tent, and the 2-night reservation minimum hurts. Call the day before and ask for a 1-night walk-in tent site. Most of the 300 sites have hookups, so ask for a tent site with a power pedestal. Adds about 14 miles round trip.

properties.name: Kumeyaay Lake Campground (Mission Trails Regional Park)
properties.price: $22.78 per site/night including 1 vehicle. All sites are primitive/dry with no hookups. Card only, no cash.
properties.reservations: OPEN FRIDAY AND SATURDAY NIGHTS ONLY (day use Sun–Thu). In Nick's window that means Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7. Book online (SDRecConnect/ActiveNet) at least 48 h ahead. Same-day walk-ups are welcome, first come first served. Entry office is open Fri–Sat 12–5 pm in winter. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Cancel 14 days ahead.
properties.access: Paved, about 5.9–6.3 bike miles from the La Mesa/Grossmont part of the line. Ride Mission Gorge Rd (busy 4-lane road with shoulder/bike lane) to the second Father Junipero Serra Trail entrance. Mild climb.
properties.notes: Cheapest real campground between El Cajon and the coast. The restrooms have potable water, sinks and showers. Quiet lakeside site with 46 sites and a 30-night/yr cap. Useless Sun–Thu nights.

properties.name: Sweetwater Summit Regional Park campground
properties.price: $33/night tent-only site (county fee table, effective Jan 2, 2026). $39 partial / $42 full hookup if you want power at the site. Showers take tokens (2 per $1) from the ranger station.
properties.reservations: Book at reservations.sdparks.org up to 24 h before arrival. Same day: phone the reservation center, or pay on site if a site is open. Camping access 24 h/day. About 112 sites, all with water and electricity per the brochure. 24-hour hot showers.
properties.access: Paved, about 9.5 bike miles south from La Mesa/Lemon Grove. Rolling streets, then a steep final climb up Summit Meadow Rd to the hilltop campground. This takes you away from the coast; you backtrack or cut west via Bonita/National City.
properties.notes: Solid county campground if Kumeyaay is closed (Mon–Thu) and you want to stop before the coast. It's a big southward detour with a stiff climb, though; Campland and Mission Bay RV are on the line about 21 miles further. No county closure notice for this park as of 11/2/2026.

properties.name: San Diego Metro KOA Resort
properties.price: Unknown. KOA advertises 'Tent Sites with hookups' and 'Premium Tent Sites' but publishes no rate. Campers reported about $110/night for RV sites in 2025. Call.
properties.reservations: Open all year. Book by phone; the KOA page says internet reservations are not currently available for this park. Tent check-in 1 pm, check-out noon. Nov 5–8 is an event weekend before Veterans Day (busy).
properties.access: Paved, about 7.9 bike miles south of the City Heights part of the line on urban streets, flat to rolling. A detour away from the coast.
properties.notes: Full-service resort (pool, Wi-Fi, café, laundry) with a power outlet at tent sites. Probably the most expensive tent night on the segment, and well off the coast route. Reviews from Oct 2026 mention lots of kids on e-bikes.

properties.name: Campland on the Bay
properties.price: Winter 2026 (Tue after Labor Day to Memorial Day) 'Limited' water+electric site, which Campland recommends for tents: $72–$92/night + 12.75% TOT (about $81–104). Optional $10/night site-selection fee. The tent-only 'Primitive' sites ($66–77) are summer-only. City of San Diego residents get 20% off.
properties.reservations: Book online or by phone (can book 2 years out). Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Arrivals after 10 pm count as late arrivals; quiet setup is allowed. Cancel at least 72 h ahead for a refund less $30. Tents only on sites with ground to stake (Limited section; J row is popular).
properties.access: On the line at the NE corner of Mission Bay (Pacific Beach Dr / Rose Creek bike path), flat.
properties.notes: First on-route campground after El Cajon (about 27 miles). Market, café, laundry, pool, free (limited) Wi-Fi. The city approved a 15-year lease extension in July 2025, so no closure risk.

properties.name: Mission Bay RV Resort — North section (tent-only sites)
properties.price: Winter 2026 'Standard (unpaved) TENT ONLY' site from $52 weekday / $63 weekend + 12.75% TOT (about $59–71). Optional $10/night site selection.
properties.reservations: Book online or by phone. Tents allowed ONLY on the unpaved North-section sites (147 sites added 2023–24). Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Arriving after 10 pm you may still set up your tent quietly. 24-h hospitality rangers.
properties.access: Paved, at De Anza Cove next to Campland (Mike Gotch Memorial Bridge bike/ped path). The North section, across from Mission Bay Golf Course, is about 0.8 bike miles off the line.
properties.notes: Cheapest full-service tent night in San Diego. The North section has two restroom/shower buildings, full-hookup pedestals with 30/50-amp outlets, and Wi-Fi. Guests can use Campland's amenities across the bridge. Lease extended alongside Campland's in 2025.

properties.name: Surf & Turf RV Park (Del Mar Fairgrounds)
properties.price: Unknown. RV sites reported at $40–77/night (Campendium reviews, 2022–24).
properties.reservations: Historically by reservation, 1-night stays allowed. Closed every summer for the fair and races (normally reopens mid-September).
properties.access: Paved, about 1 mile off Coast Hwy 101 on Jimmy Durante Blvd/Via de la Valle.
properties.notes: Gravel RV lot between I-5 and Hwy 101 with no restrooms, showers or laundry, and an RV-age rule. No evidence it accepts tents. San Elijo's $15 hike/bike site is 3 miles further, so skip this.
