properties.name: San Elijo State Beach — hike & bike site (plus standard sites)
properties.price: $15 per person/night on the shared hike/bike site (HB1, Middle Section). Standard sites from $50/night (Northern/Southern sections) + $8.25 reservation fee; premium and hookup sites cost more.
properties.reservations: parks.ca.gov says the hike/bike site is first come first served: register after 2 pm, out by noon, max 2 consecutive nights, 10 hike/bike nights per calendar year, photo ID requested, pay before entering the site. HB1 also appears in ReserveCalifornia (park 709) with nightly availability: the 11/2/2026 snapshot showed it Available Nov 5–11 at $15, so it may be bookable online. Standard sites are ReserveCalifornia only (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Snapshot: Fri 11/6 and Sat 11/7 each had 1 of 147 sites free; Tue 11/10 2; Wed 11/11 3.
properties.access: Directly on Coast Hwy 101 (bike lanes), flat.
properties.notes: The best cyclist stop on this segment: an official $15 hike/bike site on the blufftop with showers and flush toilets, and markets and taco shops across Hwy 101 in Cardiff. It is the ONLY official hike/bike site between El Cajon and Dana Point; ReserveCalifornia lists no hike/bike site type at South Carlsbad, San Onofre, San Clemente or Doheny.

properties.name: South Carlsbad State Beach campground
properties.price: Standard campsite from $50/night; premium bluff sites from $70 (southern end); + $8.25 reservation fee. No hike/bike site type exists here in ReserveCalifornia.
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia only (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Check-in 2 pm. 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 sold out. Sun 11/8–Thu 11/12: 45–62 of about 200 sites free each night. Fri 11/13: 1. Sat 11/14: 0. Walk-up only if the kiosk has a vacancy, so call first.
properties.access: On Carlsbad Blvd (bike lanes), flat. Entrance at 7201 Carlsbad Blvd; drivers can't turn in from Poinsettia Ln and must U-turn at Breakwater Rd.
properties.notes: The earlier 'possible closure / no availability' red flag is resolved: the park is open and taking normal weeknight bookings. Big blufftop campground with stairs to the beach and coin showers; camp store is seasonal. The weeknight backup if San Elijo is full, 6 miles further on.

properties.name: Oceanside RV Resort (Thousand Trails) — tent sites
properties.price: Unknown. Dedicated tent sites exist but no public rate; one reviewer was quoted about $58 for a site (type and date unclear). Tent sites have a 2-night minimum (10-night max), so you pay for 2 nights.
properties.reservations: No membership needed; book online or by phone. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am. Welcome Center/store 9 am–5 pm; arrange late arrival in advance. Tents only on designated tent sites ('No camping tents within RV sites').
properties.access: On S Coast Hwy in south Oceanside, flat.
properties.notes: The only tent-legal camp right on the line between South Carlsbad and San Clemente, but the 2-night minimum hurts. Railroad next door (loud). Full services: restrooms/showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, store. Last full-service stop before the 20-mile Camp Pendleton crossing.

properties.name: Guajome Regional Park campground
properties.price: $42/night (the county's 2026 fee table lists Guajome campsites at the full-hookup rate; the brochure shows water+electric sites). Shower tokens are 2 per $1 at the ranger station.
properties.reservations: 33 tent/RV sites plus a cabin. Book at reservations.sdparks.org up to 24 h ahead; same day by phone, or on site if a site is open. Camping access 24 h/day.
properties.access: Paved, about 9–10 bike miles inland from the Oceanside coast. Mostly on the car-free San Luis Rey River Trail, then N Santa Fe Ave/Guajome Lake Rd, gently uphill. Return the same way. Mile 415 is where you leave the coast route; the closest point on the line is inside Camp Pendleton (417.2).
properties.notes: The legal fallback near Oceanside when the beach parks are full (weekends) or to avoid the 2-night minimum at Oceanside RV. Costs about 19 extra miles round trip, but mostly on a bike path. No county closure notice for Guajome as of 11/2/2026.

properties.name: San Onofre State Beach — San Mateo Campground
properties.price: $40 standard campsite (sites 68–100) or $45 tent/primitive sites (101–157); $65 water+electric hookup sites (1–67, the only sites with power); + $8.25 reservation fee. No hike/bike site.
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Campground hours 6 am–10 pm, so arrive before 10 pm or get gate instructions. Open year-round. 11/2/2026 snapshot: on Sat 11/7 only $65 hookup sites were left (16 free units park-wide); Sun 11/8–Thu 11/12 had 110–123 free units.
properties.access: Paved, about 2 bike miles off the line: up Cristianitos Rd (gentle climb) from the I-5/Cristianitos interchange at the south end of San Clemente.
properties.notes: The state park with the most open sites at the north end of Camp Pendleton: hot indoor showers and flush toilets. 1.5-mile Panhe/Trestles trail to the beach. Freeway and motorcycle noise. A good first stop after the 20-mile base crossing; groceries about 1.5 miles away at Avenida Pico.

properties.name: San Clemente State Beach campground
properties.price: $45/night tent site (Tent Campground East, sites 100–160, and West, sites 73–99); $50 premium tent; + $8.25 reservation fee. The $70 RV hookup loop (sites 1–72) is tagged tents=no in OSM (baseline osm-way-310354752). No hike/bike site.
properties.phone: 949-670-8276 (pass office and camping late arrival); recorded info 949-492-3156
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia only; online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Park hours 6 am–10 pm. Late-arrival line 949-670-8276 (Mon–Thu 9–4, Fri 9–2). 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 3 of 128 sites free (East section), Sat 11/7 0, Sun 11/8 37, Mon 11/9 51, Fri 11/13 2, Sat 11/14 0.
properties.access: Paved, 0.4 mile off the line up Avenida Calafia, short climb.
properties.notes: Clifftop camp in town with food and groceries nearby (Avenida Del Mar/El Camino Real). The cheapest coastal tent site in Orange County at $45. Weekend nights are nearly sold out.

properties.name: Doheny State Beach campground
properties.price: $50 standard campsite (North Loop sites 1–59/120/122, South Loop 60–119/121); $65 premium beachside; + $8.25 reservation fee; $2 off for seniors 62+. ReserveCalifornia lists no hike/bike site type. Touring-community reports of an informal hiker/biker area are unconfirmed (iOverlander says none), so ask the kiosk.
properties.reservations: ReserveCalifornia only, 1–7 nights; online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Since 7/1/2026 the booking window is 3 months, ahead of a construction closure expected 2027–2029; State Parks says the campground stays open through at least the end of 2026. 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 1 of 108 sites free, Sat 11/7 0, Sun 11/8 and Mon 11/9 47 each, Fri 11/13 and Sat 11/14 0.
properties.access: On the line at Dana Point, flat; paved beach trail through the park.
properties.notes: Flat beachside camp at the north end of the segment; trains pass right alongside. After mid-October 2026 coastal flooding the park stayed open during debris cleanup, with some parking closed. Last state-park camp before Crystal Cove (segment I8-F).

properties.name: Crystal Cove State Park — Moro Campground
properties.price: About $55 for one of the 30 'low-impact' tent/van sites, or about $75 for a hookup site. These are 2020–2025 reported rates; the 2026 rate was not confirmed. Add the $8.25 ReserveCalifornia fee; an extra vehicle is $15. No dedicated hike & bike site was found. A 2022 GearJunkie listing mentions a $5 hike/bike-in fee, which is unconfirmed, so ask at the kiosk.
properties.phone: (949) 494-3539; reservations (800) 444-7275; late-arrival arrangements (949) 494-9143 (per The Dyrt listing)
properties.reservations: Reservations only via ReserveCalifornia; there are no first-come sites. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 1 pm. The entry gate is locked 10 pm–6 am, so if arriving late, call during business hours to make arrangements. A parks.ca.gov availability snapshot checked 11/2/2026 showed two-night availability within 11/5–11/17 only for arrivals on 11/11, 11/15 and 11/16. Check for single nights and cancellations.
properties.access: Paved. Turn off PCH at the signal for El Morro School and climb the short campground road to the mesa, about 0.7 mi. The entrance sits inside the current Caltrans PCH work zone between Reef Point Dr and Irvine Cove Dr.
properties.notes: The best-located full-service camp on the segment, but expensive and mostly booked. There are 58 sites: 30 dry 'low-impact' sites for tents and 28 RV sites with 30/50A water and electric. Showers are hot and token or coin operated. PCH WORK ZONE: since mid-October 2026, emergency bluff stabilization has closed both southbound lanes between Reef Point Dr and Irvine Cove Dr, leaving one lane each way with no end date. properties.name: Crystal Cove State Park — Lower Moro backcountry camp
properties.price: $25 per site per night with one vehicle included (The Dyrt and campers' reports 2019–2026), plus the ReserveCalifornia reservation fee.
properties.reservations: Book through ReserveCalifornia 48 hours to 7 months ahead (per the park site). The park infosheet says the permit can also be obtained at the Moro Campground kiosk, where every backcountry camper must check in for the overnight permit. Within the area you reserve, sites are first-come. Check-in/check-out time is listed as 9 am.
properties.access: Start from the Moro Campground entrance (mile 455.5): about 0.7 mi paved, then about 2.8 mi of dirt fire road up Moro Canyon, gaining roughly 750 ft (about 125 ft to about 875 ft). Mountain bikes are allowed on backcountry fire roads but not after dark. Expect to push a loaded bike on the steep pitches. The park describes all primitive sites as a 3–4 mi hike from the parking lot.
properties.notes: The cheapest legal camp on the segment, but a real hike-a-bike: 13 sites, pit toilet, picnic tables, ocean view. There is NO water, so haul 4–5 L up from Moro Campground. Stoves only (no fires), no pets, 4 people per site. Same-day online booking is not possible (48-hour minimum), so ask at the Moro kiosk. Trails close after rain. Corrected position: the baseline camp-res-107 coordinates (33.573,-117.808) are in the canyon bottom; the camp itself is the OSM node used here.

properties.name: Crystal Cove State Park — Deer Canyon backcountry camp
properties.price: $25 per site per night, plus the ReserveCalifornia reservation fee.
properties.reservations: Same as Lower Moro: book 48 hours or more ahead on ReserveCalifornia, or get the permit at the Moro Campground kiosk.
properties.access: From the Moro Campground entrance: about 0.7 mi paved, then about 3.5 mi of dirt fire roads, gaining about 530 ft to about 650 ft. Bikes are legal on fire roads but not after dark.
properties.notes: Smallest of the three camps (OSM lists 5 tent pads). No water, no fires, no dogs.

properties.name: Newport Dunes Waterfront Resort & Marina (RV resort, tents on Small sites)
properties.price: No separate tent rate is published. Tents go on a Small RV site (22×25 ft, full hookups with 30/50A power): $84–$165/night in the winter season (Tuesday after Labor Day to Friday before Memorial Day). Rates include the $5 online fee, change with demand, and tax is added. One vehicle pass included.
properties.reservations: Book online (camplife.com, linked from newportdunes.com) or call 949-729-3863. Walk-up availability is not documented. Check-in is from 2 pm. If you arrive after the registration office closes but before 10 pm, the gate sends you to your reserved site and you register by 11 am the next morning. Arrivals after quiet hours begin (10 pm Sun–Thu, 11 pm Fri–Sat) are sent to the main parking lot until 8 am. Tent stays are capped at 14 nights in any 3 months.
properties.access: Paved and flat. Leave PCH at Jamboree Rd / Back Bay Dr (bike lanes); the gate at 1131 Back Bay Dr is about 0.5 mi away.
properties.notes: The LAST tent-legal campground before Los Angeles on the I-8 line. Pricey, but a full resort: hot showers, laundry, heated pool, basic wifi, and electricity at the site. Tents are allowed only on Small RV sites, two per site at most. The 2025 rules say tents must be FREESTANDING and stakes are strictly prohibited, so weight the tent down. Lock the bike to a fixed object (resort rule). Bikes are welcome on resort roads (5 mph) and the beach promenade (3 mph). Back Bay Bistro is on site; stores in Newport and Costa Mesa are 1–2 mi away.

properties.name: Hipcamp — Vintage Camper in LBC Garden (trailer rental with room for a tent)
properties.price: unknown. The nightly rate is not shown. You book the 1968 Shasta camper (sleeps up to 4); the listing says there is 'additional room to set a tent, if desired'. Optional driveway parking is $10/night.
properties.reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Check-in 3–11 pm (early or late may be possible), check-out 11 am, 1-night minimum, strict cancellation. Host Lena W. has an 80% response rate, typically within about 5 hours.
properties.access: Urban streets. Hipcamp lists it 3.5 mi from central Long Beach and about 10 minutes from the ports of Long Beach and San Pedro, so it is likely west or north Long Beach near the LA River path. The exact address is given only after booking; the coordinates are the Long Beach city centroid (APPROXIMATE).
properties.notes: The ONLY tent-allowing place found between Newport Dunes (mile 461) and Los Angeles. It is a vintage trailer in the host's shared backyard garden (88% recommend). Reviews from October 2025 to October 2026 mention ants, roaches, floodlights, neighborhood noise and weak water pressure. The shower is cold only, and the host says to bring your own drinking water. Book before leaving Newport so you have the address.

properties.name: Hopkins Wilderness Park group camps (Pine / Sycamore / Gumwood) — PIER VARIANT, not usable
properties.price: Group booking only: $374 staffing fee per overnight reservation, plus per-person fees (a 2024 report says $10 per adult).
properties.reservations: Reserve 2–3 weeks to 6 months ahead through WebTrac or at the Alta Vista Racquet Center, 715 Julia Ave. Check-in Saturday 2 pm, check-out Sunday noon.
properties.access: On the Santa Monica Pier variant only (Long Beach to Redondo Beach): about 13.3 riding mi from Long Beach, then 0.3 mi off PCH at Prospect Ave or about 1.5 mi up from the Esplanade/Strand. Paved.
properties.notes: NOT usable for a touring cyclist. City rules prohibit bicycles in the park. It is tent-only Saturday-night group camping booked weeks ahead, and the staffing fee alone is $374. The app's OSM pins for Pine Camp, Sycamore Camp and Gumwood Camp should be marked unusable.

legality.summary:
Bike legality and road conditions westbound, Casa Grande to the Elysian Theater. I checked the app's own candidate lines (/Users/nicklynn-rulon/App Projects/grimey-trip-planner/data/corridors/lines.json) against official bike-access data and OpenStreetMap, point by point.

ARIZONA: the January 2018 ADOT policy on bikes on freeways (TGP 1030, Table 1030-A) bans bikes on I-10 only from MP 114.86 (Miller Rd, exit 114, Buckeye) to MP 270.59 (Kolb Rd, Tucson). On I-8 the only ban is Trekell Rd to the I-10 junction. That makes all of I-10 west of Buckeye legal: Tonopah (exit 94), Quartzsite (exit 17), the Dome Rock pass and Ehrenberg (exit 1). West of Brenda, I-10 is also signed US Bicycle Route 90. A 2024 bill amendment to ban bikes on all rural freeways was removed before it passed.

CALIFORNIA I-10 (Caltrans District 8 bike map, 2021, and District 8 highway conditions data, 2022): bikes are allowed in only two places.
- Mesa Dr in Blythe (exit 232) to Dillon Rd in Indio (exit 146).
- Haugen-Lehmann Way (exit 110) to the SR-62 junction (exit 117).
Bikes are banned from the Arizona line to Mesa Dr, from Dillon Rd to SR-62, and from Haugen-Lehmann west to the LA County line. A separate bike and foot bridge on US Bicycle Route 90 crosses the Colorado River beside I-10.

PROBLEMS IN THE APP'S I-10 LINE:
(1) Mi 198.3–206.1: about 7.8 mi on I-10 through Blythe (exit 240 to 232), where bikes are banned. Use Hobsonway west to the Mesa Dr on-ramp instead.
(2) Mi 292.1–293.7: the line stays on I-10 past Dillon Rd (exit 146) to Golf Center Pkwy (exit 144), where bikes are banned. Get off at Dillon Rd.
(3) Mi ~31.5–48.5: about 17 mi of unpaved desert tracks between AZ 238 and paved Riggs Rd. This is BLM land inside Goodyear city limits, not tribal land. The paved option is about 11 mi longer.
(4) In Buckeye the line uses a service road marked private, plus canal roads.
(5) Smaller unpaved pieces: Tom Wells Rd (about 4 mi of packed dirt), the Tamarack Service Rd track at Whitewater (2.7 mi) and a dirt track into Banning. Each has a paved alternative, but the Banning one is disputed.

OTHER:
- Caltrans is rebuilding I-10 from Wiley's Well to the Arizona line ($241M), with completion planned for winter 2026.
- CV Link is open in three pieces totalling about 41 mi, with on-street gaps through Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells.
- CA 111 has no shoulder for about 11 mi from near Bombay Beach to the Riverside County line.
- I-8 comparison: the In-Ko-Pah grade is legal up to exit 77. The app's I-8 line crosses Camp Pendleton on base roads that need a base bike pass. The no-pass legal route is the I-5 shoulder from Harbor Dr to Las Pulgas Rd. The LA River path has an 8-mile gap from Maywood to Elysian Valley.

LIMITS: the web-search budget ran out partway through. Arizona construction for 2026 (AZ 238, Salome Hwy, I-10 west) and Arizona shoulder widths and traffic counts are not checked. azdot.gov blocks automated fetches, so the ADOT policy was read from an archived copy. Caltrans bike-access data is from 2021–22, so signs on the ground win. Shoulder widths and traffic counts are Caltrans 2016–2022 data. My scratch scripts, including the line-against-Caltrans check, are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-nicklynn-rulon/9ce86c39-790c-4e33-a1c1-886b206b5e93/scratchpad.

legs.detail: No freeway. Route is N VIP Blvd → Cowtown Rd → Maricopa–Casa Grande Hwy into Maricopa. There are no controlled-access roads on the line.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Two-lane rural county highway. OSM has no shoulder widths or bike lanes mapped. Traffic counts not verified.
legs.hazards: Commuter and farm traffic into Maricopa; no services in between. Search budget ran out before local conditions could be checked.

legs.detail: AZ 238 (Maricopa Rd) is legal for about 7.4 mi. From line mi ~31.5 to 48.5 (about 17 mi) the line runs on OSM highway=track desert roads: an unnamed track (way 316332168), 'Empire Boulevard' (a track) and the west end of W Riggs Rd (also a track). Paved Riggs Rd resumes at S Bullard Ave (~-112.375). Overpass is_in shows these tracks are inside Goodyear city limits and BLM's Lower Gila Terraces & Historic Trails ACEC, which is public land, not Gila River Indian Community. After that, Rainbow Valley Rd, Tuthill Rd and Beloat Rd are paved two-lane roads. In Buckeye (mi ~71.5–74) the line uses unnamed canal/service roads and one service road tagged access=private (way 769895506) before W Baseline Rd; reroute on public streets. I-10 east of Miller Rd (exit 114) is banned for bikes (ADOT), so it is not an option. Paved, legal alternative from bike routing: AZ 347 → Riggs Rd → St John's/Ray Rd → 67th/75th/79th Ave → Baseline → 99th/Southern → Estrella Pkwy → MC 85 → Buckeye, 59.7 mi versus 48.9 mi.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: AZ 238: two lanes, 60 mph posted, no bike lanes (OSM cycleway:both=no); shoulder width not mapped. Rainbow Valley, Tuthill and Beloat Rds: paved two-lane secondary roads. The tracks are probably dirt two-track (surface not mapped).
legs.hazards: About 17 mi of possibly sandy dirt with no water or services, a poor fit for a loaded touring bike. Private service road in Buckeye. AZ 238 truck traffic not verified. Search budget ran out before any 2026 construction could be checked.

legs.detail: W Baseline Rd → W Salome Hwy → 411th Ave → I-10 at exit 94. The metro-Phoenix interstate ban ends at Miller Rd (exit 114, MP 114.86), so the I-10 shoulder from exit 114 west to exit 94 is also a legal fallback.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Baseline Rd: paved two-lane, 50–55 mph (OSM). Salome Hwy: paved two-lane secondary. Shoulder widths not mapped.
legs.hazards: Fast two-lane rural roads with farm trucks. Search budget ran out before 2026 Maricopa County construction could be checked.

legs.detail: ADOT TGP 1030 (January 2018), Table 1030-A, bans bikes on I-10 only from MP 114.86 (Miller Rd) to MP 270.59 (Kolb Rd). Nothing west of Buckeye is restricted. I-15 and I-40 have no bans; I-8 is banned only from Trekell Rd to the I-10 junction. The policy says bikes may be banned only where an alternate route is comparable or better. OSM tags this I-10 stretch bicycle=yes, and bicycle=designated (US Bicycle Route 90) from about Brenda west. The older 2002 policy ended the ban at 107th Ave and was sunsetted in 2017. A 2024 SB1184 amendment to ban bikes on all controlled-access roads was removed before the bill passed.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Two lanes each way, 75 mph posted (OSM), full paved shoulder. ADOT and Arizona traffic counts not verified.
legs.hazards: Rider in April 2025: 'pretty easy riding' but trash and tire pieces on the shoulder and burned-car debris about every mile. Tire-wire flats, heavy truck traffic, and long gaps between interchanges.

legs.leg: Quartzsite → Dome Rock → Ehrenberg → Colorado River → Blythe (mi 173.6–197.4)
legs.detail: All legal in Arizona. Route is Dome Rock Rd West (paved), then I-10 over the Dome Rock pass (US Bicycle Route 90), then Tom Wells Rd, which OSM marks surface=compacted (unpaved) for about 4 mi from exit 5 to Ehrenberg. You can skip it by staying on the I-10 shoulder to exit 1 and taking Frontage Rd N. The line crosses the river on a separate bike/foot bridge beside I-10 (OSM cycleway 314745291: bicycle=designated, concrete deck, compacted approaches, part of US Bicycle Route 90 since 2015) and lands on E Hobsonway in Blythe. Caltrans District 8 data lists I-10 from Mesa Dr to the Arizona line as banned for bikes, while OSM tags the I-10 bridge to Riviera Dr (exit 243) as bicycle=yes. A 2012 rider could not find the path from the exit-1 access road and rode the I-10 bridge 'perfectly fine'. A 2025 group noted a bike lane across the river.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Dome Rock Rd West: paved with no shoulder (CycleBlaze). I-10: 75 mph posted with shoulder. The bridge path is separate from traffic.
legs.hazards: Loose gravel or dirt on the bridge approaches and on Tom Wells Rd. Caltrans I-10 Blythe Pavement Rehabilitation runs from PM 134.0 to the state line, with completion expected winter 2026, so expect lane shifts and closures near the bridge. ADOT has a Dome Rock Rd–Scaddan Wash paving project with night lane closures; its dates were not verified.

legs.detail: Caltrans District 8 bike map (2021, postmiles from 2016 records) and the 2022 District 8 data agree. I-10 is closed to bikes from Mesa Dr (PM 145.1, exit 232) to the Arizona line and open from Mesa Dr west to Dillon Rd (PM 58.9). OSM also tags I-10 bicycle=no from Riviera Dr to Mesa Dr. The app line rides I-10 from mi 198.3 to 206.1 (exit 240 to exit 232), which is banned. Fix: take E/W Hobsonway and W Hobson Way (I-10 Business, two-lane asphalt) west to Mesa Dr, then the westbound on-ramp at exit 232, which OSM tags bicycle=yes. Ragsdale Rd at Desert Center (old US 60/70, paved) is a frontage option. I could not find a 'Chuckwalla Valley Rd' frontage in OSM near Blythe.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Caltrans minimum outside shoulder is 10 ft, except about 2.5 mi just west of Mesa Dr where it drops to 5 ft. Two lanes each way. Posted 70 mph (OSM); the Caltrans dataset says 65. About 25,600–27,300 vehicles per day (2016 counts).
legs.hazards: The Caltrans $241M rebuild covers PM 134.0–156.5 (Wiley's Well to the state line), with completion expected winter 2026. It brings reduced speeds, lane closures and crossovers in Blythe, and temporary signals at the Wiley's Well overcrossing (exit 222). Also tire debris, heavy trucks and long service gaps.

legs.detail: Inside the open Mesa Dr–Dillon Rd stretch. Frontage pieces: Ragsdale Rd and Eagle Mountain Rd at Desert Center, plus the Red Cloud Rd (exit 182) and Hayfield Rd (exit 177) interchanges. Otherwise ride the shoulder.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Caltrans minimum shoulder is 10 ft, except about 3 mi just east of Chiriaco Summit where it is 5 ft. Two lanes each way, about 26,000 vehicles per day (2016), 65–70 mph.
legs.hazards: Steady westbound climb to Chiriaco. 2023 rider journals call the Indio–Blythe shoulder wide, decent and fairly clean. Watch for truck tire-wire and the narrow 5-ft piece near Chiriaco.

legs.detail: I-10 is legal westbound only to Dillon Rd (exit 146). Caltrans lists the SR-62 junction to Dillon Rd as banned, and OSM tags I-10 bicycle=no west of exit 146. The app line stays on I-10 for about 1.6 mi more (mi 292.1–293.7) to Golf Center Pkwy (exit 144), which is illegal. Fix: exit at 146 and take Dillon Rd to Indio Blvd.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Shoulder 10 ft minimum (5 ft just east of Chiriaco). About 26,500–27,000 vehicles per day (2016). 65–70 mph.
legs.hazards: Long descent shared with trucks, crosswinds, tire debris.

legs.detail: No freeway. Indio Blvd → Country Club Dr → Tamarisk Row Dr → CV Link (West Valley piece) into Palm Springs. CV Link officially opened Nov 5–10, 2025, and is open in three pieces, about 41 mi total: West Valley, 19.63 mi (Palm Springs Visitor Center to Date Palm Dr, Cathedral City); Central Valley, 5.44 mi (Palm Desert, Bump-n-Grind to Cook St); East Valley, 16.02 mi (Washington St, La Quinta, to Airport Blvd, Coachella). Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells pulled out, so those stretches are on-street.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Path: 20 mph limit, open day and night, solar lighting, water stations; restrooms at the Palm Springs Visitor Center and parks. Bikes share with golf carts and other low-speed electric vehicles.
legs.hazards: Golf carts and e-bikes on the path; arterial traffic in the on-street gaps.

legs.detail: Route is CA 111, where bikes are permitted (the freeway section from Snow Creek to I-10 is also open to bikes), then Tipton Rd and Whitewater Cutoff (paved). Next comes 'Tamarack Service Rd': OSM highway=track with no surface or access tags, added March 2026, about 2.7 mi along the north side of I-10 through the wind farm. Then Tamarack Rd → Haugen-Lehmann Way → Railroad Ave (paved) → Cabazon. Paved legal alternative: the I-10 westbound shoulder from Whitewater (exit 114) to Haugen-Lehmann Way (exit 110). Caltrans opens I-10 to bikes only from Haugen-Lehmann to the SR-62 junction (PM 24.55–29.4), so you must exit at 110. I-10 is banned from 110 west to the LA line, and from SR-62 (exit 117) past Indian Canyon Dr (exit 120) to Dillon Rd.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: CA 111 is a divided highway with shoulders, and bikes are permitted. The I-10 shoulder between 114 and 110 is open to bikes; its width was not pulled.
legs.hazards: San Gorgonio Pass wind corridor: a 2018 rider hit gale-like head and crosswinds in the afternoon; expect blowing sand. The Tamarack track is likely loose dirt. Westbound the road climbs toward Banning.

legs.detail: Line: Main St/Apache Trail/Seminole Dr → Johnson Lane (old US 60/70/99, asphalt) → about 0.6 mi of dirt track (OSM way 925048796, surface=dirt, no access tag) into E Ramsey St. Two alternatives, both uncertain. (1) I-10 westbound from Malki Rd (exit 103) to Ramsey St (exit 102), about 1.8 mi. OSM has tagged it bicycle=yes since 2012, but the Caltrans District 8 bike map (2021) and 2022 data list I-10 from the LA/San Bernardino county line to Haugen-Lehmann as banned. Obey whatever is posted at the Malki Rd on-ramp. (2) Morongo reservation roads (Hathaway St–Morongo Rd–Ramon Rd–Martin Rd), tagged access=permissive in OSM, with Martin Rd tagged access=private.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Seminole Dr is four lanes at 45 mph (casino traffic). Johnson Lane is a quiet old highway.
legs.hazards: Dirt surface, unclear right of way on the track and reservation roads, wind.

legs.detail: Ramsey St (old US 60/70/99). I-10 through Banning and Beaumont is banned for bikes (Caltrans).
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: A Banning city plan describes a Ramsey St bike lane from Highland Springs Ave to San Gorgonio Ave, with widening and added shoulders on parts of Ramsey. Current striping not verified.
legs.hazards: A bicyclist was killed and another seriously injured in March 2026 on the 5300 block of W Ramsey St near Apex Ave. Busy arterial.

legs.detail: Beaumont Ave → Cherry Valley Blvd → Calimesa Blvd (I-10 frontage) → E Citrus Ave. I-10 and SR-60 here are banned for bikes (Caltrans District 8).
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Local arterials; shoulder widths not mapped.
legs.hazards: Long descent off the pass; suburban traffic in Calimesa and Yucaipa.

legs.leg: Redlands → Rialto → Pacific Electric Trail → Claremont (mi 369.4–405.4)
legs.detail: Barton Rd (buffered bike lane) → Loma Linda Wash Path → Fairway Dr → W Olive St → Cactus Ave side path → Pacific Electric Trail, about 19 mi of concrete path. TrailLink lists the trail as about 20 mi, from Claremont Blvd & Huntington Dr (Upland) to N Cactus Ave (Rialto). A 1.75-mi Rialto extension is still in development (CEQA filing 2025; June 2026 news still describes it as 'future'). The line jogs onto E Arrow Hwy (35 mph) near mi 400. No 2025–26 closure found.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Separated path for most of the leg. Barton Rd has a buffered bike lane.
legs.hazards: Street crossings on the trail, short on-street gaps.

legs.detail: Bonita Ave (OSM bike lanes in Claremont and La Verne) → Juanita and Mauna Loa Aves → Vernon Ave → Royal Oaks Dr → W Olive Ave (bike lane, Monrovia) → Colorado St/Colorado Blvd (Historic US 66) into Pasadena.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Colorado St in Arcadia is four lanes, 45 mph, with no bike lane tagged in OSM. The other roads are residential or collector streets.
legs.hazards: Busy arterial on the Arcadia–Pasadena stretch of Route 66.

legs.detail: W Union St (25 mph) → Colorado Blvd (Eagle Rock) → Norwalk Ave → Verdugo Rd → Elysian Valley (1944 Riverside Dr). The Glendale Narrows section of the LA River path is nearby. LA City repaired its Zoo Dr–Riverside Dr stretch in 2024.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: City streets; Colorado Blvd is four lanes.
legs.hazards: Urban traffic. The Riverside Dr detour was described as poorly paved during path closures.

legs.detail: No controlled-access roads. The first ~5 mi use W Indian School Rd (OSM shows dirt or compacted pieces) and Saddle Vista Rd. Instead, go back south on 411th Ave to the paved Salome Hwy. Then Salome Hwy → Courthouse Rd → Harquahala Valley Rd → Salome Rd, which is asphalt two-lane for about 32 mi with no services.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Two-lane paved county roads; OSM has no shoulder data. Traffic counts not verified.
legs.hazards: Long stretch with no services; dirt pieces at the Tonopah end if you follow the drawn line. Search budget ran out before 2026 construction could be checked.

legs.detail: US 60 (Quartzsite–Wickenburg Hwy) is part of US Bicycle Route 90 in Arizona. Adventure Cycling's Southern Tier notes say US 60 has good shoulders once it leaves I-10.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: OSM: two lanes, 65 mph, paved shoulder (cycleway:both=shoulder, bicycle=designated, smoothness good to excellent).
legs.hazards: 65-mph traffic and RVs; sparse services (Salome, Hope, Brenda).

legs.detail: US 60 for 3.7 mi, then the I-10 shoulder for 13.5 mi. Legal under ADOT TGP 1030 and part of US Bicycle Route 90.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: I-10: two lanes each way, 75 mph posted, full shoulder (OSM).
legs.hazards: Tire debris, trucks, and burned-car debris reported in 2025.

legs.corridor: I-10 variant: Box Canyon to Mecca
legs.leg: Chiriaco Summit → Box Canyon Rd → Mecca (variant mi 0–24.7)
legs.detail: I-10 for 4.4 mi from exit 173 to exit 168 (legal; 70 mph posted), then Box Canyon Rd, which turns into 66th Ave into Mecca. The app labels this piece 'Cottonwood Springs Road', but Cottonwood Springs Rd is the road north into Joshua Tree National Park. The road southwest to Mecca is Box Canyon Rd (OSM: asphalt, smoothness intermediate). Mostly downhill westbound.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Two-lane county road with no shoulder. Riders describe it as quiet with light traffic.
legs.hazards: Flash-flood washes. 2018 storms washed out much of the road; it reopened after a roughly $3M Granite repair in 2019, and the county closes it in storms. Check Riverside County road closures after any rain. No services from Chiriaco to Mecca.

legs.corridor: I-10 variant: Box Canyon to Mecca / Hybrid
legs.detail: Lincoln St → Buchanan St → 58th Ave → CV Link East Valley piece (paved, open since November 2025) into Indio.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Farm roads, then a separated path.
legs.hazards: Farm trucks on Lincoln St and 58th Ave.

legs.corridor: Hybrid (I-8 to El Centro, Salton Sea, I-10 line)
legs.detail: Dogwood Rd (CR S31) → S Imperial Ave → CA 111. No freeway.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Two-lane county road; shoulder width not mapped.
legs.hazards: Agricultural trucks.

legs.corridor: Hybrid (I-8 to El Centro, Salton Sea, I-10 line)
legs.detail: Caltrans District 11 data shows no bike ban on CA 111.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Caltrans minimum outside shoulder is 8 ft for about 13 mi from Brawley to Calipatria and 4 ft elsewhere. About 5,400–6,800 vehicles per day south of Calipatria and about 3,500 from Calipatria to Niland (2016 counts). 65 mph.
legs.hazards: 65-mph traffic, farm trucks, heat. Services in Calipatria and Niland only.

legs.corridor: Hybrid (I-8 to El Centro, Salton Sea, I-10 line)
legs.detail: Bikes are not banned (Caltrans District 11).
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Minimum shoulder mostly 2–4 ft, dropping to 0 ft at bridges and culverts. About 2,200 vehicles per day (2016). 65 mph.
legs.hazards: Narrow shoulders at 65 mph, no services until Bombay Beach, sun and heat exposure.

legs.corridor: Hybrid (I-8 to El Centro, Salton Sea, I-10 line)
legs.leg: Bombay Beach → North Shore, CA 111 (hybrid mi 296.2–314.4)
legs.detail: Legal. The Caltrans District 8 bike map lists CA 111 from the Imperial/Riverside county line to 66th Ave as 'Bicyclists Permitted'.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Caltrans records a 0-ft minimum shoulder for about 11 mi, from roughly 3 mi southeast of Bombay Beach to the Riverside County line, with about 1,500 vehicles per day (2016) at 65 mph. In Riverside County the shoulder is 2–4 ft (1-ft pinch points), about 5,000 vehicles per day, 55 mph.
legs.hazards: Effectively no shoulder at highway speed, trucks, no water between Bombay Beach and North Shore.

legs.corridor: Hybrid (I-8 to El Centro, Salton Sea, I-10 line)
legs.detail: Bicyclists permitted (Caltrans District 8 bike map).
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: About 4-ft minimum shoulder with 1–2 ft pinch points. About 5,000 vehicles per day (2016). 55 mph.
legs.hazards: Farm trucks into Mecca.

legs.leg: Ocotillo → In-Ko-Pah grade → Jacumba (I-8 line mi ~273–291)
legs.detail: Caltrans District 11 data: I-8 is open to bikes from Ocotillo up the Mountain Springs/In-Ko-Pah grade to In-Ko-Pah Park Rd (exit 77). It is banned from exit 77 west to near Live Oak Springs, where Old Hwy 80 runs parallel, and from Ocotillo east toward El Centro, where Evan Hewes Hwy (S80) runs parallel. The app line already does this: I-8 bicycle=yes for about mi 276–285, then exit 77 to Old Hwy 80. Old Hwy 80 is not an alternative on the grade itself, because I-8 replaced old US 80 from the In-Ko-Pah on-ramp down to Ocotillo.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Minimum shoulder 10 ft (0 ft on bridges). About 7,300–9,000 vehicles per day (2016). 65–70 mph.
legs.hazards: Strong winds on the grade, and Caltrans closes In-Ko-Pah Gorge in bad weather. Long sustained climb with trucks.

legs.leg: Oceanside → Camp Pendleton → San Clemente (I-8 line mi ~412–436)
legs.detail: The app line crosses the base on Vandegrift Blvd and Stuart Mesa Rd (OSM access=permit). That needs a base bike pass, issued in person at the Main Gate visitor center (Mon–Fri 7:30–3:30) with a REAL ID-compliant ID, a background check, photo and fingerprints. It is valid one year and works only at the Main and Las Pulgas gates. The OC Bicycle Coalition said in May 2024 that no pass renewals had been issued for over a year; 2026 status unclear. Legal no-pass route: the I-5 shoulder from Harbor Dr (exit 54) to Las Pulgas Rd (exit 62), which Caltrans District 11 data marks open to bikes. Then take the Pacific Coast Bikeway/Old Pacific Hwy north through San Onofre. I-5 from Las Pulgas to Basilone is otherwise banned; riders have been allowed on it during military closures of the path.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Full I-5 freeway shoulder from Harbor Dr to Las Pulgas; I-5 traffic is heavy.
legs.hazards: Military closures of the Old Pacific Hwy path, fast freeway traffic, and possible refusal at the gates.

legs.leg: Long Beach → LA River path → Elysian Theater (I-8 line mi ~486–514)
legs.detail: The lower LA River path runs from Long Beach to Maywood/Vernon; no 2025–26 closure was found. There is still an 8-mile gap from Maywood to Elysian Valley. Metro's gap project is now estimated at about $1.1B and at least five years away (October 2025), and was still in public comment in early 2026. The app line uses city streets (Zonal Ave, Cypress Ave) through the gap to the Glendale Narrows path near the Elysian.
legs.shoulderAndTraffic: Separated path for about 15 mi, then urban streets through downtown and Boyle Heights.
legs.hazards: Urban traffic in the gap; path upkeep varies. Repairs at Griffith Park were made in 2024.

weather.advisories: As of ~9:30 PM MST Sun Nov 1: NO wind advisory, high wind warning or red flag warning anywhere on the three lines for Nov 2-8. ARIZONA (NWS Phoenix): Sunday's storm dropped 0.5-1.5 in. on the lower deserts; rivers and washes are running, some at flood stage. Flood Watch until 5 AM MST Mon covers West Pinal (Casa Grande/Maricopa), Buckeye/Avondale, Tonopah Desert and Gila Bend zones. Flood Warnings in effect tonight include the Hassayampa River (low-water crossings at Hassayampa/Arlington, to 3:45 AM Mon) and the New River (low-water crossings downstream to the Gila may become impassable; to 11:15 AM Mon). PSR expects flood warnings to be extended through Monday. For the Nov 2 ride: wet shoulders and possibly closed or flowing dips on AZ 238, Rainbow Valley Rd, Tuthill/Beloat Rds and Baseline Rd/Salome Hwy (Hassayampa, Centennial Wash) - check Maricopa County/ADOT closures (az511.gov) and never ride through moving water. Casa Grande tonight: showers/T-storms until ~2 AM (a few could be severe, damaging-wind threat), WSW gusts to 30 mph; Monday sunny, high ~69, W 0-5 mph; patchy fog possible Mon AM in sheltered valleys. Rest of week dry, highs a few degrees below normal, light winds with modest afternoon upslope gusts; late-week shortwave PoP <=10%. SAN DIEGO (NWS SGX): Beach Hazards Statement for San Diego and Orange County coasts through Mon afternoon (surf 3-6 ft, minor tidal overflow near the ~3:30 PM high tide). High tides rise to ~7 ft by Fri and ~7.5 ft over the weekend into early next week - possible overwash of beach-level paths/campsites on the I-8 coast segment. Pattern: weak N/NE offshore flow Mon; weak trough Tue (light drizzle chance coastal SD County, backing off; onshore breeze Tue afternoon); weak offshore Wed-Thu; ridge Fri-weekend warming coast and low deserts to the low/mid 80s; ~23% of ensemble members show a deeper late-week low with somewhat stronger offshore winds. LOS ANGELES (NWS LOX): Beach Hazards Statement for LA/Ventura beaches through Mon afternoon; Sunday's post-frontal W gusts of 30-40 mph on the coast are over. Weak offshore flow all week; offshore gradients increase late week and peak Sat Nov 7 near -4 mb, giving gusty offshore winds mainly in LA/Ventura County mountains and valleys; recent rain mitigates fire risk. Ridge holds to ~Nov 10; next rain-bearing trough ~Nov 11. No Santa Ana advisory has been issued; the NWS grids show this weak offshore event as NE 13-17 mph g22-26 at Jacumba/Pine Valley Nov 6-8, ENE/E 10-17 g16-26 at Banning Nov 5-8 (strongest at dawn), N 8-14 g17-25 down the lower Colorado River (Blythe/Yuma/Quartzsite) and Desert Center-Chiriaco Nov 6-8, and NNW 9-14 g16-23 at dawn Nov 6-7 on the Coachella Valley floor (Indio/Mecca).
weather.climatology: Computed for this trip from station archives (IEM copies of NWS-ingested obs), November riding hours 8 AM-5 PM local; 'westerly' = from SW through NW (head or quartering-head wind for a westbound rider); RAWS anemometers at 20 ft, ASOS at 33 ft; 'brutal day' = mean headwind component >=15 mph or any hour >=25 mph. SAN GORGONIO PASS: (1) Whitewater RAWS (WWAC1, 2,530 ft, pass mouth beside the I-10/CA 111 wind farms the bike line crosses near mi 325-340; Nov 2011-2025): westerly >=15 mph in 28% of riding hours, >=20 in 23%, >=25 in 15%. When it blows it is strong: median 24 mph, 90th pct 33 mph sustained; westerly gusts median 36, 90th pct 49, max 75 mph. ~8.7 brutal days per November (29% of days), usually in 2-day spells (longest 7). It is bimodal: 41% of days net a light tailwind (SE up-valley breeze or E offshore flow, rarely >=15 mph) and 27% are light/variable. An onshore westerly blows all day once it sets in (25% of hours at 8 AM vs 31% at 3 PM), so an early start does not dodge it. (2) Cabazon (BAZC1, 2,150 ft, mid-pass on the bike line; Nov 2012-2025): westerly >=15 mph in 14% of hours, >=20 only 2%; median 13 / 90th pct 18 mph; gusts median 21, max 48. Easterly >=15 mph is more common here in November (27% of hours); ~2.5 brutal + ~8 moderate-headwind days per November, 51% of days net tailwind. Westerlies here peak midday (7% of hours at 7 AM vs 20% at noon), so early starts help on the Cabazon-Banning half. (3) Palm Springs airport (KPSP, valley floor; Nov 2010-2025): 74% of riding hours under 8 mph, westerly >=15 just 2%, essentially no brutal days - the wind is confined to the Whitewater-Cabazon corridor, not the city. Contrast May 2021-2025: Whitewater westerly >=15 mph in 67% of hours and 72% of days brutal; Cabazon 59% / 48%. November is the pass's gentle season, with roughly a third as many brutal days as late spring (consistent with AMS work showing California pass winds peak in the warm months). OCOTILLO / IN-KO-PAH (I-8): (1) Jacumba-Mountain Springs Grade (TNSC1, 2,140 ft, on I-8 above the Ocotillo wind farm; Nov 2014-2025): 61% of riding hours under 8 mph; SW-W >=15 mph in 14% of hours, >=20 in 6%, >=25 in 2%; median 16 / 90th pct 25 mph when westerly; gusts median 27, 90th pct 40, max 55. ~3.1 brutal days per November (10%) plus ~11% moderate-headwind days, spells 1-2 days. The strong wind is SW gap flow straight down the grade - a direct headwind on the westbound climb - and it builds in the afternoon (10-11% of morning hours vs 16% after noon), so climb in the morning. NE offshore tailwind ~8% of days. May contrast: >=15 mph in 25% of hours, 24% brutal days. (2) El Centro NAF (KNJK, Imperial Valley floor; Nov 2010-2025): 71% of riding hours light, westerly >=15 mph 8%, ~2.4 brutal days per November. BOTTOM LINE: in an average November the I-10 pass mouth carries about a 3-in-10 daily chance of a 20-35 mph headwind (gusts 35-50), versus about 1-in-10 for a brutal day on the I-8 grade - normally I-8 is the wind-safer line in November. This week's forecast removes the pass risk.
weather.summary: VERDICT: the coming week favors the I-10 corridor. All three lines get an unusually benign, dry week after Sunday's storm - no wind advisories, and the strongest forecast headwinds a westbound rider would meet are 10-14 mph (coastal afternoon sea breezes Nov 3 and 6, a 7-8 AM WSW 12 gap wind at Ocotillo Nov 4, and a dawn down-valley NNW 9-14 g16-23 at Indio/Mecca Nov 6-7). Why I-10: (1) shortest - 440 mi vs 486 Hybrid and 514 I-8; (2) its signature risk, the San Gorgonio Pass (~mi 320-351), which in an average November throws a 20-35 mph westerly on about 3 days in 10, is forecast to run EASTERLY (a tailwind up the climb) every day Thu Nov 5 - Sun Nov 8 (Banning ENE/E 10-17 mph at dawn, gusts 16-26, easing to 5-10 by midday), with Wed Nov 4 light/variable; only Tue Nov 3 shows an onshore WSW 8 g15 afternoon there, before he can arrive; (3) at any pace from 70 to 100 mi/day he reaches the pass Nov 5-6, and even a 1-2 day slip lands on Nov 7-8, the strongest tailwind days. SUGGESTED I-10 TIMING (~85 mi/day): Mon 11/2 Casa Grande -> Buckeye or Tonopah (calm, highs ~70; post-flood caution at washes/low-water crossings). Tue 11/3 Tonopah -> Quartzsite (calm; the Salome Hwy/US 60 variant is equally calm, so pick it on shoulder, traffic and services, not wind). Wed 11/4 Quartzsite -> Blythe -> Desert Center or Chiriaco (N crosswind 5-9 mph, gusts to 20 near Blythe at midday). Thu 11/5 -> Indio -> Palm Springs -> Cabazon/Banning (light winds everywhere; light ENE tailwind up the pass). Fri 11/6 Banning -> Redlands -> Claremont -> Pasadena -> Elysian (~95 mi; E tailwind at the top, calm west of Redlands) or split Fri/Sat. I-10 WATCH-OUTS: N crosswinds 8-14 mph g17-25 on the lower Colorado River and Desert Center-Chiriaco Nov 6-8; the dawn NNW wind at Indio/Mecca Nov 6-7 is a quartering headwind on the WNW leg to Palm Springs (start that leg after ~10 AM); warmest days Nov 7-8 (mid-80s in the Coachella Valley). The Box Canyon variant (Nov 5-7) would put the N wind behind him on the SW-bound descent but adds 12 mi plus a NW-bound leg into that same dawn wind. I-8: also wind-friendly (calm Arizona Nov 2-5; NE offshore tailwind on the In-Ko-Pah climb and through Jacumba-Pine Valley-Alpine Nov 5-8, with gusts 22-26 on exposed grades Nov 6-8; coast light N mornings and WNW 8-10 mph sea-breeze afternoons, a mild headwind northbound). But it costs +74 mi, a ~4,000-ft climb and colder mountain camps (Jacumba/Pine Valley lows 45-52F vs 49-65F along the I-10 line; the Salome variant also dips to 44-48F). In a normal November the I-8 grade is the wind-safer choice (brutal days ~1 in 10 vs ~3 in 10 at Whitewater); this week that advantage disappears. HYBRID: +46 mi over I-10 with the same pass timing (Nov 5-7), but CA 111 and CV Link run NW into the Nov 6-7 dawn NNW wind near Mecca/Indio; no wind reason to choose it this week. CONFIDENCE: high Nov 2-5, moderate Nov 6-8 (SGX ensembles split on a late-week low; ~23% show stronger offshore winds, which would still be tail/crosswinds westbound). Re-pull the Banning/Palm Springs forecast the evening before the pass day - an onshore surge would show as W/WSW >=15 mph in those grids.

intel.summary:
I found 16 trip reports from 2018–2026, plus 2 older ones (2016–17) included because they are the only cyclist accounts of camping at Chiriaco Summit and the Salton Sea SRA. Only about 5 of the 16 in-window reports are self-supported trips that camped (RustyCrank 2023, Nick Sanders 2024, Two Boldly Go 2023, the Radavist ride from Dec 2019, Eppich 2019). Two more are ACA van-supported camping groups (2025). The rest are supported or hotel trips, useful mainly for road warnings. This step added nothing to the trip planner app.

Camps cyclists actually used:
- **I-10 and the Salome variant:** Salome KOA (ACA group, Apr 2025); Tamarisk RV Park near Palo Verde (2018, 2025); Dome Rock Rd BLM strip west of Quartzsite, signed with a 7-day limit (Jun 2023); Box Canyon wild camps (2023, 2024); an informal BLM camp past the I-10 fence near the last rest area before Buckeye, with the rest-area janitor's OK (2024); a Trek shop yard in Goodyear (2024).
- **Salton Sea / hybrid:** Cottonwood Campground was full in Dec 2019 and rangers enforced the rules; the riders were allowed into the day-use picnic area after paying. Fountain of Youth RV Resort near Niland (2019), whose booking terms reportedly now bar tents; I couldn't confirm. Slab City (2023). Salton Sea SRA Headquarters campground (2019).
- **I-8 contrast:** Ma-tar-awa RV Park in Alpine on the Viejas reservation (2019, 2025); the yard behind the Red Feather cafe in Ocotillo and an Ocotillo RV park (2023, 2025); Dateland RV Park ($12 in Dec 2019; tents again in 2022); a Brawley church hall (2025).

No 2018–2026 report describes camping at Desert Center, Chiriaco Summit, Corn Springs, Wiley's Well, Whitewater Preserve, Tonopah, Buckeye, Banning or Yucaipa. Those spots have no rider confirmation.

Key warnings across reports:
1. **Flats on the I-10 shoulder:** almost every I-10 report mentions steel wire from shredded truck tires. Sanders had 10 punctures in one day in 2024; a 2023 group had many flats; a 2025 rider had a failing tire plug. Carry sealant or tubeless, spare tubes and patches.
2. **Morongo reservation, Banning to Cabazon:** Sanders was turned away at the gate in 2024, a 2023 group needed a police escort, and a 2018 tour used about 2 mi of I-10 through Cabazon instead.
3. **San Gorgonio Pass wind:** eastbound groups had strong tailwinds in 2018 and 2023, which points to headwinds for Nick riding west.
4. **Other wind:** a north wind on the Salton Sea in Oct 2023 would be a headwind on the northbound hybrid. Gusts were extreme at Ocotillo and on the In-Ko-Pah grade (a semi blew over in June 2023; strong headwinds in Apr 2025), and in Pine Valley in March 2021.
5. **Desert Center:** in 2023 only the post office was working, the gas station was not operating, and there were no other services for about 40 mi.
6. **Closed or limited services on US 60:** Hope had no services, Dos Amigos was closed in 2023, Crystal's cafe in Wenden was seasonal, and Black Rock Cafe in Brenda was the only stop for miles.
7. **Box Canyon Rd** was closed by a flood washout in Oct 2023; Sanders rode and camped on it in Mar 2024. Check its current status.
8. **Bogart Park** in Cherry Valley was closed to tents in 2021.
9. **I-8 bike signs:** "Bicycles Must Exit / Prohibited" signs between CA 98 and Yuma; the 2019 riders rode past CHP anyway. Evan Hewes Hwy was badly potholed in 2019, and a rider crashed on a cattle guard between Tacna and Dateland in 2022.
10. **Pacific Electric Trail:** a 2019 rider abandoned it because of signalized crossings almost every block.

Current park status: the CA State Parks Salton Sea page, checked 2026-11-01, lists the Mecca Beach and Bombay Beach campgrounds as closed. It has no alert for Headquarters and still lists hike-and-bike sites.

Only a few reports fall near Nick's Nov 2–9 window: Nov 2018, Dec 2019 (two), late Oct 2023, and the older Dec 2016. Expect nights near freezing.

Gaps in this search: Reddit, crazyguyonabike and Medium blocked automated access, and I did not work around that, so no Reddit threads or crazyguyonabike journals are included. The shared web-search budget also ran out before I finished. One lead I couldn't open is a 2023 crazyguyonabike journal titled "Southern Tier 2023 – revisited". A search snippet says it rode LA → San Bernardino → Indio → CA 111 → Brawley → Blythe → Salome, which would cover most of the hybrid line.

reports.route: Westbound, solo, self-supported. Wickenburg → US 60 (Aguila, Wenden, Salome, Hope, Vicksburg, Brenda) → I-10 → Quartzsite → Dome Rock Rd → I-10 → Ehrenberg → Blythe → CA 78 (Ripley, Palo Verde, Glamis) → Brawley → Old Hwy 111 → Calexico → CA 98 → Ocotillo → I-8 In-Ko-Pah grade → Old US 80 (Jacumba, Boulevard) → San Diego. campsUsed: Wild camp on Arizona State Trust Land off US 60, just north of the Vulture Mountains west of Wickenburg (Jun 2). He doesn't say whether he had a permit.
Wild camp up a rocky dirt track off Dome Rock Road just west of Quartzsite (Jun 3). Other people were camping along Dome Rock Rd, which had a 'Camping seven day limit' sign.
Stealth camp beside a shed at a farmhouse in the alfalfa fields along CA 78, about 12 mi east of Brawley near Orita (Jun 4). This was private land, with loud trucks and feedlot smell.

Tent on a concrete slab behind the Red Feather Off-Road Market & Cafe in Ocotillo, with staff permission (Jun 5). There was an outlet and a water spigot; the cafe closes at 4 PM and an RV park is next door.
warnings: Hope had no services, Dos Amigos (Hope/Vicksburg) was closed, and the Black Rock Cafe in Brenda was the only service for miles (its A/C was broken).
I-10 from the end of US 60 to Quartzsite: about a 5-mile climb into a headwind on a shoulder littered with debris, with semis.
Most Quartzsite restaurants closed around 6 PM.

Dome Rock Rd ends at a cattle guard onto I-10. West of there the I-10 shoulder is wide and signed 'Bicycles use shoulder lane'. Services are at Ehrenberg Exit 5; use Frontage Rd and the bike lane on the Colorado River bridge.
Downtown Blythe is largely shuttered; services are clustered near I-10.
CA 78 from Palo Verde to Glamis: about 100°F and about 39 mi with no services. The Border Patrol station was closed but had an outdoor spigot; the Glamis store closed at 1 PM.
The turn onto CA 98 in Calexico had construction and no shoulder, and there are about 33 mi with no services west of Calexico. Border Patrol vehicles were everywhere.

Ocotillo and the I-8 grade: gusts above about 50 mph (the wind turbines had shut down) and a semi that had just blown over. He was blown into the gravel, walked the Devils Canyon Bridge, and pushed through a road cut. He found a scorpion under his tent.
The Jacumba restaurant was closed and being rebuilt (Mountain Sage market was open). The Manzanita Diner near Boulevard had burned down, leaving the Mountain Top Market as the only service.
reports.summary: This is the best in-window self-supported report for both the US 60 variant and the I-8 corridor. In June heat he wild or stealth camped every night. The legal-camping evidence is the Dome Rock Road BLM strip (7-day limit sign) and the Ocotillo cafe yard. Key lessons: long gaps with no services, and severe wind on the Ocotillo–In-Ko-Pah climb.

I-10 is the only paved link between Blythe and Quartzsite. Tom Wells Rd has no outlet.
At Desert Center he describes only history and ruins, no services.
A police officer in Goodyear warned him not to ride across the city at night because of drunk drivers.
A friendly but armed survivalist was camped beside the road near Dome Rock.
reports.summary: This is the only in-window self-supported account of the I-10 corridor east of Blythe and of the Box Canyon variant. He used no campgrounds at all: one canyon wild camp, one motel, one informal BLM camp by a rest area, and one bike-shop yard. The tire-wire flats are the biggest lesson. The Morongo access problem between Banning and Cabazon matches the 2023 group that needed a police escort.

reports.route: Westbound Adventure Cycling group with van support, camping. Wickenburg → US 60 → Salome → I-10 → Quartzsite (tire-repair stop) → Colorado River bridge path → Palo Verde → CA 78 via Glamis → Brawley → CA 86 / El Centro / CA 98 → Ocotillo → I-8 and Old US 80 → Alpine → San Diego
campsUsed: Salome KOA (Day 54)
Tamarisk RV Park near Palo Verde: tents under shady tamarisks, basic facilities, across from a convenience store (Day 55)
A church fellowship hall in Brawley with a pool and showers; the church isn't named (Day 56)
An unnamed RV park in Ocotillo with decent bathrooms, 'dry and dusty' (Day 57)
A campground with a pool on the Viejas Reservation in Alpine. It isn't named, but it matches the Ma-Tar-Awa RV Park in the 2019 report (Day 58).
warnings: It was 92°F at the Palo Verde finish and about 100°F near Brawley, in April.
I-10 had steady trucks but smooth pavement for the first 20 mi.
CA 78 had no shoulder for the first 35 mi, with rough pavement, heavy trucks and short steep climbs. Two bottles barely lasted the 40 mi to Glamis, and the headwind was strongest in the last 10 mi.
Drivers on CA 86 resented bikes in the lane, and local streets in El Centro had severe expansion cracks. The last 6 mi of CA 98 were brutal, and a 0.3-mi sand road near Ocotillo was unridable.
A strong headwind near Ocotillo slowed riding to 7–10 mph.

The I-8 climb (about 11 mi and 2,800 ft) had a smooth shoulder but steady trucks, oversize loads overhanging the shoulder, narrow bridge shoulders, and drain grates and gaps that can catch a wheel. Old US 80 was very rough in places, and the night was cold and windy.

reports.title: Peter across the US 2023, Days 3–5: Moreno Valley → Indio → Blythe → Wickenburg
reports.route: Eastbound supported group tour with support vehicles and hotels. Moreno Valley → Lamb Canyon → Beaumont → Morongo reservation (police escort) → Palm Springs → Indio → I-10 → Desert Center → Blythe → I-10 → Brenda → US 60 → Salome → Wenden → Aguila → Wickenburg
campsUsed: None: hotel-based supported tour (hotels not named)
warnings: Police escorted the group through the Morongo reservation.
They had a strong tailwind down the San Gorgonio Pass, averaging over 30 mph for miles, which means a likely headwind for a westbound rider. A strong-wind advisory was out for the next day.
Traffic in Palm Springs was heavy, with many junctions and a construction closure.
On I-10 they rode 90+ mi a few feet from traffic beyond a rumble strip. A pickup swerved across the shoulder, and some drivers passed trucks on the inside.
Shredded truck tires left tiny wire fragments; many riders flatted, one of them three times.

At Desert Center they ate lunch under the post office awning, the only working building. Fellow rider Barbara's blog (barbarasbigbikeride.blogspot.com, 2023/05) adds that the gas station isn't operating, there are no other services for about 40 mi, and the last 20 mi into Blythe were very windy.
On US 60, Buckaroo's store in Brenda was big but mostly empty, and Crystal's cafe in Wenden was 'closed till fall'. The shoulder was abrasive, gritty and narrow, with a faint rumble strip.
reports.summary: There's no camping, but this gives solid 2023 observations on the I-10 shoulder, Desert Center and US 60 services. A third rider's blog (davesbikeridefromlatoboston.blogspot.com) covers the same days.

reports.title: Alan Jacobsen's Ride Across America, Day 2: Twentynine Palms to Blythe
reports.route: Eastbound, supported by family. Twentynine Palms → Joshua Tree NP → Cottonwood Springs Rd down to I-10 → about 70 mi on the I-10 shoulder → Chiriaco Summit → Blythe (about 120 mi)
campsUsed: None: Holiday Inn Express in Twentynine Palms and a hotel in Blythe (not named)
warnings: The I-10 shoulder was 8–10 ft wide beyond a rumble strip, with debris and broken tire pieces. Traffic ran over 70 mph and was very loud.
He got a front flat that morning.
The 7-mile descent from the park to I-10 was rough, and grit from a storm wore down his brake pads.
There was no phone service inside Joshua Tree NP.
Chiriaco Summit was his refuel stop.
reports.summary: This confirms the Cottonwood Springs Road–I-10 link and Chiriaco Summit as a resupply point in winter 2023. No camping information.

reports.title: Crossroads 2018, LA to Boston (Mike Ruane): Day 3 Riverside → Indio, Day 4 Indio → Blythe
reports.route: Eastbound supported tour with hotels and a van. Riverside → Ramona Expwy past Lake Perris → CA 79 to Beaumont → Ramsey St through Banning → about 2 mi of I-10 through Cabazon → CA 111 → Indio; then 88 mi of I-10 to Blythe, exiting at Mesa Verde onto Hobsonway. Day 3 post: https://mruane1953.blogspot.com/2018/05/day-3-monday-may-14th-riverside-to.html
campsUsed: None: Holiday Inn Express in Indio; Blythe hotel not named
warnings: The I-10 shoulder was rough on the short Banning–Cabazon stretch.
A tailwind carried them for about 37 mi of descent (35 mph while coasting), then turned to a head/crosswind for the last 17 mi into Indio in 90°F+ heat.
The Indio → Blythe shoulder was mostly wide and clean, but from about mile 63 it had heat fissures and cracks for about 22 mi.
Heat in May: the author quit 12.7 mi short with dehydration and cramping.
Stops: Cactus City rest area, Chiriaco Summit, Desert Center, Wiley's Well rest area
reports.summary: Supported, with no camping. It's useful for the Banning–Cabazon I-10 shortcut and the shoulder condition east of Indio.

reports.title: Circling the U.S. (Connie Eppich & Rob), Chapters 59–61: San Diego → Alpine → Jacumba → Calexico → Yuma → Dateland → Gila Bend
reports.route: Eastbound couple carrying their own gear. San Diego → Alpine → I-8 / Pine Valley → Jacumba → I-8 down to the Yuha Desert → Calexico → CA 98 and I-8 → Yuma → I-8 → Dateland → Gila Bend. Earlier chapters: .../2020/01/circling-us-chapter-59-heart-troubles.html and ...-chapter-60-losing-rob-again.html
campsUsed: Ma-tar-awa RV Park on the Viejas reservation, Alpine (jacuzzi closed, shower not hot)
Jacumba Spa & Resort (a hotel with a 40% cyclist discount)
A Motel 6 after a medical detour, and a cheap motel in Calexico
Warm Showers hosts about 10 mi east of downtown Yuma
Dateland RV Park: $12, paid at the convenience store, a quarter mile down a dirt road. Concrete slab, no picnic table, hot showers.
Palms Inn in Gila Bend, chosen over a pricier KOA
warnings: I-8 between CA 98 and Yuma is posted 'Bicycles Must Exit' / 'Bicycles Prohibited'. They rode it anyway past parked CHP officers, because they'd read that the frontage roads were in poor shape.
The Dateland campground sits between I-8 and the railroad: trucks all night, about 8 freight trains overnight, and floodlights left on.
There are 33 mi with no services between the rest area and Gila Bend; they had a slight headwind.
Roads leaving San Diego were rough and busy, with steep climbs over the Tecate Divide and 'The Wall'.
Police told them to stop hitchhiking during a medical emergency.
reports.summary: December contrast on the I-8 corridor. Only Ma-tar-awa RV Park and Dateland RV Park were true campsites; the other nights were motels or hosts.

reports.title: Gass-powered Tandem: xcountry, Days 2–5: Pine Valley → El Centro → Wellton → Gila Bend → Casa Grande
reports.route: Eastbound group with van support, staying in hotels. Pine Valley → I-8 → El Centro → frontage roads, Yuma streets and I-8 → Wellton → Old Hwy 80, I-8 and frontage road → Gila Bend → Maricopa → Casa Grande. This is the app's I-8 line in reverse.
campsUsed: None: hotels, including the Best Western Space Age Lodge in Gila Bend and a hotel in Casa Grande
warnings: Northeast gusts in the high 20s mph climbing out of Pine Valley; 15 mi took 2 hours. Then 9 mi of I-8 at 6% downhill.
Roads around El Centro were badly broken.
El Centro → Wellton (97 mi): broken frontage road, busy 4-lane streets in Yuma, a 600-ft I-8 climb east of Yuma, then a 1.3-mi descent on a debris-filled shoulder.
Wellton → Gila Bend: I-8 freshly paved with wide, debris-free shoulders (2021). Southeast winds of 20+ mph gusting to 30, dust and sand storms on the frontage road, mornings in the 40s°F.
Gila Bend → Casa Grande: landfill dump trucks passing close, a flat near Maricopa, feedlot smells, and a northeast headwind for the last 15 mi.
reports.summary: Hotel-based with no camping, but it covers almost exactly the app's I-8 line, including the Casa Grande–Gila Bend leg.

reports.title: Across USA in 52 Days (Brian Anderson): Tacna and Dateland
reports.route: Eastbound Timberline Bike & Hike supported group on the I-8 corridor: Yuma area → Tacna → Dateland. Related entry: https://www.cycleblaze.com/journals/goaliecycler/jane-cattle-guard/
campsUsed: An RV park in Dateland (not named) where the group tent-camped for the first time on the tour
warnings: Between Tacna and Dateland a rider on an e-bike crashed on a cattle guard that twisted her wheel. She suffered a concussion and a broken upper arm and was airlifted out.
Food: Jac's Whistle Stop in Tacna and date shakes at the Dateland truck stop
reports.summary: The entries are short, but they confirm tent camping at Dateland and a real cattle-guard hazard on the Tacna–Dateland stretch.

dryStretches.from: Blythe: BB Travel Center / Chevron, exit 232 (mi 206.1)
dryStretches.note: LONGEST void on any line: no food or store for 59 mi. Water only at Wiley's Well rest area (mi 216.1, 10 mi out; open as of Oct 2026, mineral-heavy well water). Wiley's Well to Chiriaco is 49.2 mi with no water on the line. Desert Center (mi 246.3) is dead: cafe closed in 2012, no gas. The only fallback is Lake Tamarisk Library, 1.8 mi north of exit 192 (Tue/Thu 10-6, Sat 10-2). Leave Blythe carrying water for 60 mi.

Bouse Wash rest area (mi 137.8) is 33.7 mi from Burnt Well. It has restrooms and vending machines, but a Jan 2025 visitor found no tap to refill bottles. Exits 81, 69, 53 have NO services. Tonopah to Vicksburg is 49 mi with no store (vending only).

AZ 238, Riggs Rd and Rainbow Valley Rd have no stores. The only option is the Southern Dunes golf-clubhouse grill at mi 25.1 (daytime only; 37.7 mi from there to the DG). Off-route: Tempo Cafe in CantaMia (1 mi off at 57.5, 55+ clubhouse) and Estrella shops (2.8 mi off at 64.1). The Dollar General is not in OSM; if it is closed, Buckeye is 7 mi further (mi 69.9).
The Cactus City rest areas (mi 279.4) are CLOSED for reconstruction until spring 2027, so there is no water on I-10 in between.
Exits 31 and 26 have nothing on the interstate. Brenda (Buckaroo's store, Black Rock cafe) is a 1.5-1.8 mi detour up US 60 from exit 31 (~mi 158).

Shell N Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs (mi 321.7)

Dome Rock Rd and I-10 over Dome Rock pass.

Completely DRY: no store, rest area or tap on Indian School Rd, Salome Hwy, Courthouse Rd, Harquahala Valley Rd or Salome Rd. Saddle Mountain BLM (mi 9.2) has no water. That is worse than staying on I-10, which has Burnt Well water at 8 mi.

US 60 then I-10 from exit 31 (Gold Nugget exit 26 has nothing).
Box Canyon Rd has no water. JTNP Cottonwood visitor center/campground water is 7 mi north of exit 168 (14-mi uphill round trip). After Mecca no gap exceeds ~8.5 mi to Indio.

CA 111 along the east shore. The Ski Inn opens at 10am, so an early rider finds Bombay Beach shut (Bombay Market is unverified). Then the gap runs to the Salt Creek taps (mi 306.1, unverified) = 27.7 mi, or to Salton Sea SRA HQ water (mi 311.8) = 33.4 mi.
S31 farm road; El So Market on route at mi 259.8.
Skip's convenience store (mi 315.0, unverified) splits it. Mecca Beach campground (mi 310.8) is closed.
Two Rivers rest area (mi 267.2) has been closed since 2015.
